DefaultStrings.matchFor:1622, the 'this representative has not already elected' guard, in the arm where it FIRES and suppresses a second election. The header repeats 'nsl' at index 3; it is active (its weight compares equal to the representative's) and its range is again exactly the representative's semantic range, so conjunct 3 would elect it -- the guard is the only thing that stops that. DISCRIMINATION, measured against a build of lokalized-java 3.0.0 with the guard deleted and nothing else changed: with the guard the answer is the nsl catalog; without it the answer is the en catalog. The mechanism is matchFor:1772 -- index 2 governs the nsl catalog through an EXACT (syntactic) relationship, so when index 2 is still the elected semantic member that locale is served at the group's representative position 0, which precedes en's position 1; re-electing index 3 makes index 2 a nonsemantic syntactic governor, which moves the nsl catalog to position 2, and the preference-order walk at matchFor:1803 then reaches en at position 1 first. The interleaved 'en' member is therefore not decoration: with the header sgn-nsl,nsl,nsl the two arms agree, which is exactly the shape that would have closed this branch while specifying nothing. Both nsl members are byte-identical in range and weight (Locale.LanguageRange lowercases at construction), so nothing here can be attributed to a difference between them -- only to WHICH index the election records.

The same guard reached through a differently-spelled duplicate. Locale.LanguageRange lowercases its range at construction, so 'NSL' and 'nsl' are the same member content and the row must answer identically to owed.m3b.electionguard.duplicate-member-does-not-reelect -- also verified against the guard-deleted build, where it likewise degrades to the en catalog. This is the spelling axis the two M5b defects were found on: a port that compared the later member's range case-sensitively, or that normalized ranges only at some later stage, would take a different path to the same election and this row is what would catch it.

Reference leg. Three members at equal weight: 'sgn-nsl' is unrecognized and is the group representative (its semantic range is the extlang equivalent 'nsl'), 'en' forms its own group at index 1, and 'nsl' joins the representative's group at index 2 and is ELECTED as its semantic member because its range is exactly the representative's semantic range. Exactly one member is ever electable here, so matchFor:1622's 'already elected' guard is evaluated only in its unfired arm. Recorded rather than asserted: this is the row a port that re-elects on every active member also passes, which is what makes the four-member row below -- and only that row -- the discriminating one.
The end-to-end partner: the BOM-prefixed catalog is not merely loadable but resolvable, so a port that kept the BOM as part of the first KEY would be caught here rather than only at load.

An ordinary per-call ranges ingress, so it is partitioned requiredPortableIds unlike the four order-dependent rows around it. ITS ONE LIMITATION, stated rather than left to be discovered: this fixture's instance locale is also en, so an implementation that IGNORED per-call languageRanges entirely and fell through to the instance locale answers this row correctly by coincidence -- it anchors the corpus row, and cannot by itself catch that port. Same inputs, opposite outcome: there the ranges survive and the lookup is en-driven, here the locale survives and the lookup is zh-TW-driven with the longer chain. Neither row is 'the' answer for a both-present call -- together they say the answer is the LAST setter applied, which is the only proposition Java supports. The separate top-level match block is the oracle's own matchFor(zh-TW) probe, emitted whenever input.locale is present, and is identical in both rows: it shows the locale field was accepted in each and then kept or discarded by the order alone. pt at 1.5 exercises `i = 0..1` on a non-integral value: the integer-digit operand i must be the truncated integer part, not the rounded value. A port that computed i by rounding would get 2 here and pick the wrong category, and 1.5 is the only value in this family that catches it.

Because DefaultStrings compiles every loaded expression in its constructor, an implementation that measured the source as 18, or rejected at equality, would fail to construct the whole fixture rather than merely mis-evaluate. Verified against Java by probe: the same catalog at limit 16 is rejected with 'Expression length 17 exceeds maximum supported length 16'. The matching branch proves the expression was not just accepted but actually compiled and evaluated.
The same 17-character expression evaluating false. Without a miss case the fixture could be satisfied by an implementation that treated any at-limit expression as unconditionally true.

The generated-fragment predicate '(a > 1) && a == 2' is also exactly 17 characters, so the fragment path sits on the same boundary as the whole-message path rather than merely somewhere inside it (the earlier authored version used a 6-character predicate, which measured nothing). Compiled at DefaultStrings.java:576; probe-verified that the same fragment at limit 16 aborts construction with 'Unable to compile generated-fragment alternative 0 expression'.

The at-limit fragment predicate evaluating false falls through to the fragment's default translation, proving it was compiled and evaluated under the lowered character limit rather than skipped or short-cut to a constant.

A single parenthesised group under maximumExpressionNestingDepth 1. validateInfixTokens increments groupDepth on GROUP_START and throws when the running depth exceeds the limit, decrementing on GROUP_END, so a port that seeded the counter at 1 or never decremented would refuse this fixture at construction. Probe-verified: the same catalog at limit 0 reports 'Expression grouping depth exceeds maximum supported depth 0'.
The at-limit grouped expression evaluating false, so grouping is shown to be evaluated rather than merely tolerated.

The fragment predicate is also depth 1, so the nesting cap is measured on the generated-fragment path at the same boundary — matching the TranslationRuntimeLimits javadoc's claim that the three expression limits apply equally to both predicate kinds.
The at-limit grouped fragment predicate false under the nesting limit, falling through to the fragment default.

The exact-zero boundary for the only expression limit that permits zero (validateNonNegative at TranslationRuntimeLimits.java:425): with no parentheses anywhere in the catalog the group counter never leaves 0, so the fixture must construct and the ungrouped conjunction must still evaluate with normal precedence. A port that charged an implicit top-level group would reject the fixture outright.

The ungrouped conjunction evaluating false at nesting limit zero, so the pair shows real evaluation rather than a degenerate constant. Read against runtime-limits.expression-nesting.limit-one.alternative-misses it also shows the grouped and ungrouped forms agree, so the parentheses in the limit-one fixture are not changing the semantics being observed.
An ungrouped fragment predicate at nesting limit zero, confirming the zero setting does not disable generated-fragment predicates.

The same expression under maximumExpressionTokens 9, its exact infix token count: GROUP_START, a, >, 0, GROUP_END, &&, b, ==, 1. ExpressionEvaluator.validateInfixTokens runs on the infix list inside convertTokensToReversePolishNotation, before shunting-yard output is produced, and whitespace yields no token — so a port that counted RPN output (7 tokens, parentheses dropped) or counted whitespace would disagree and, because the check happens at construction, would take the whole fixture with it. Probe-verified: the same catalog at limit 8 reports 'Expression contains 9 tokens'.
The at-limit token expression evaluating false, so the case pair cannot be passed by an implementation that short-cuts an at-limit expression to a constant.

Token counting on the generated-fragment predicate path, which is also exactly 9 infix tokens, so a port that bounded only whole-message alternatives — or counted fragment tokens differently — cannot construct this fixture.
The at-limit fragment predicate false under the token limit, falling through to the fragment default.

The separately emitted match channel is computed straight from the per-call locale, so it and the result block disagree on purpose. The invalid ambient supplier stays unbuilt under both orders, so a second per-call ingress does not reopen it. The JS surface is an object literal, the analogue of Java's CONSTRUCTOR (which refuses) rather than of its ordered BUILDER, and choosing the port's answer is a plan decision this row must not be read as settling.

Served straight from the supplied fr-CA, so lookupLocale and resolvedLocale coincide and the resolved-locale term of the isFallback OR contributes nothing; only the fabricated PRIMARY_LANGUAGE type is left to decide it. Same instance shape with matchType CANONICAL. Only the fabricated type can decide isFallback here, so this row and its six siblings reconstruct TranslationResult.negotiationUsedFallback's whole switch through the supplied channel.

CLDR_FALLBACK claimed over a locale that actually served the key exactly. Whichever way isFallback lands, it is provably a function of the supplied diagnostic and not of resolution -- the strongest single statement that a supplied match is trusted.

Same instance whose supplied match claims EXACT on fr, but a key that exists only in en. isFallback is an OR (TranslationResult.java:250-253): the supplied type feeds the first term and the resolved-locale comparison feeds the second. Isolates the second term from the first, so a port cannot pass the seven-row type table by hard-wiring isFallback to the matchType alone.

Greeting.Hello exists in fr, so resolution serves the supplied locale directly and the second isFallback term (resolvedLocale not equivalent to lookupLocale) contributes nothing. Whatever isFallback reports therefore comes entirely from the SUPPLIED matchType. A port that re-derived the match from the catalog, or that computed isFallback from how the translation was actually served, diverges on the types the switch treats as fallback.
EXTENDED_RANGE sounds like a fallback relationship. A port that grouped the types by intuition rather than by the enumeration diverges here.
LIKELY_SUBTAG on an exact serve. Pairs with the EXTENDED_RANGE and WILDCARD rows, which are the near neighbours a port is most likely to sort onto the wrong side of the switch.
PRIMARY_LANGUAGE against EXTENDED_RANGE and WILDCARD is what makes the grouping non-guessable; the three cases are only meaningful together.
WILDCARD completes the seven non-NONE types. With all seven recorded, a port's own isFallback classification is fully pinned without needing NONE, which cannot be paired with a locale at all.

Verified order is Zulu/zc, Alpha/zeta, Alpha/beta, Alpha/gamma: keys in file declaration order (Zulu precedes Alpha though it sorts after), placeholders in declaration order (zeta precedes beta though it sorts after), and a key's own placeholders before its alternatives. Cardinality and ordinality warnings therefore interleave by declaration position rather than grouping by type. A port backed by a sorted map, or by a JS object that reorders keys, produces a different sequence.

Verified Irish ordinals are exactly [ONE, OTHER] while Irish CARDINALS are [ONE, TWO, FEW, MANY, OTHER]. This control must emit nothing; a port that reused the cardinal set for the ordinal check would emit a three-form warning here. Both axes warn, in declared placeholder order (c then o), and neither missing set contains the supplied TWO: cardinal missing is {ONE, OTHER} because English has no TWO cardinal, ordinal missing is {ONE, FEW, OTHER} because the supplied TWO is supported. warnings.message: unsupported-forms-ja: placeholder 'c' for key 'Pair' is missing Cardinality translation[s] for locale 'ja': [CARDINALITY_OTHER]. Supported forms are [CARDINALITY_OTHER]. Values that resolve to a missing form are treated as resolution failures at runtime.

unsupported-forms-ja: placeholder 'o' for key 'Pair' is missing Ordinality translation[s] for locale 'ja': [ORDINALITY_OTHER]. Supported forms are [ORDINALITY_OTHER]. Values that resolve to a missing form are treated as resolution failures at runtime.

cases.notes: The same catalog under Japanese, whose cardinal and ordinal sets are both [OTHER]: exactly one missing form on each axis. Confirms the catalog is incomplete for even the smallest NON-EMPTY CLDR set, which is the comparison the zz case needs.

Directly pins the premise the zz suppression case rests on: the supported cardinality set for 'zz' is empty rather than defaulting to {OTHER} or to the root locale's set. Without this, a failing zz suppression case cannot be diagnosed as a wrong supported table versus a missing empty guard. The fixture is only present because the oracle requires a constructible Strings for classifier operations; its contents are irrelevant to the observation.
The ordinal half of the same premise: supported ordinalities for 'zz' are empty. Both halves are needed because the zz suppression case observes silence on two axes at once.

Locale 'zz' has NO CLDR plural rules, so both supported sets are empty and warnOnIncompleteCardinalityTranslations/warnOnIncompleteOrdinalityTranslations return before computing a set difference (LocalizedStringLoader.java:2022 and 2072). The same catalog that warns twice under English and twice under Japanese warns ZERO times here. A port that computes supported-minus-provided without the empty guard emits a full form list instead.

accept-language-chooser.description: The eight flat single-language sources of browser-chooser-many-languages (en, fr, de, es, ja, pt, it, nl -- no shared primary language, therefore no tiebreakers), but with the fallback locale and the ambient instance locale deliberately SPLIT: fallback ja, instance en. browser-chooser-many-languages cannot serve the Accept-Language entry point, because its fallback is en and its instance locale defaults to en, so 'returned the configured fallback', 'matched the en catalog' and 'returned the ambient instance locale' collapse into one indistinguishable answer -- which is precisely the confusion every fail-soft arm of bestMatchForAcceptLanguage turns on. Split, they are three distinct tags, and one language tag per row is the operation's entire observation channel.

alternatives-structure-depth-1.description: Alternatives nested 1 levels deep. JSON container depth of the entry is 4. Generated, not hand-authored.

alternatives-structure-depth-10.description: Alternatives nested 10 levels deep. JSON container depth of the entry is 31. Generated, not hand-authored.

alternatives-structure-depth-41.description: Alternatives nested 41 levels deep. JSON container depth of the entry is 124. Generated, not hand-authored.

alternatives-structure-depth-42.description: Alternatives nested 42 levels deep. JSON container depth of the entry is 127. Generated, not hand-authored.

alternatives-structure-width-128.description: A single alternatives array 128 entries wide, all siblings. Probes whether any width limit exists distinct from the depth limit.

alternatives-structure-width-129.description: A single alternatives array 129 entries wide, all siblings. Probes whether any width limit exists distinct from the depth limit.

alternatives-structure-width-200.description: A single alternatives array 200 entries wide, all siblings. Probes whether any width limit exists distinct from the depth limit.

bidi-isolation-default-mode.description: Establishes the LIBRARY DEFAULT bidi mode without configuring one. DefaultStrings.java:73/80 declares DEFAULT_BIDI_ISOLATION = BidiIsolation.RTL_LOCALES and :477 applies it when the builder was handed null, so an he lookup isolates caller values and an en lookup does not. instanceLocale is he (fallbackLocale is en, deliberately different) so a case that passes no per-call locale still resolves into the RTL catalog, which pins that the AMBIENT locale drives the script test. Serves the 'bidi isolation modes' half of the section 8.3 clause.

bidi-isolation-failure-response.description: BidiIsolation.ALWAYS with an instance return-string handler whose text contains a placeholder-looking token, over a catalog that carries no translatable key. Distinguishes the three failure responses by whether isolation is reachable at all: RETURN_STRING returns translationFailureResponse.getTranslation() verbatim without interpolation (DefaultStrings.java:757-759), RETURN_KEY goes through interpolateFailureKey and does isolate (:754), and THROW_EXCEPTION reaches throwExceptionFor (:3196), which builds a MissingTranslationException from the raw key and touches neither the interpolator nor BidiUtils. Per-call handlers replace the instance one (:684), so all three run on one fixture.

bidi-isolation-generated-placeholder.description: BidiIsolation.ALWAYS with a template that mixes a file-defined (generated) placeholder with two caller-supplied ones. In interpolateTemplate only the immutableContext else-branch consults shouldApplyBidiIsolation (DefaultStrings.java:1365-1371); the placeholderBindings branch that expands generated values never does. So one resolved string carries isolated caller values and a bare generated value, which is the only shape that catches a port isolating every interpolated slot.

Greeting.Titled.commentary: title is file-defined and must not be isolated; name and city are caller-supplied and must be

bidi-isolation-instance-always.description: Instance-level BidiIsolation.ALWAYS over the same en/he catalogs. The en lookups isolate here and would not under the default, so the fixture separates the mode from the locale; per-call NONE and per-call RTL_LOCALES then override it downward, giving the mirror of bidi-isolation-instance-none.

bidi-isolation-instance-none.description: Instance-level BidiIsolation.NONE over the same en/he catalogs, so NONE can be shown to beat an RTL resolved locale and so per-call ALWAYS and RTL_LOCALES can be shown to override it. Every he case here would isolate under the library default, which is what makes the fixture discriminating rather than vacuous.

bidi-isolation-ltr-request-rtl-donor.description: The clause built in the opposite direction: Arabic is the fallback locale and owns the only Greeting.Named entry, so an English request is served by an RTL donor and the default RTL_LOCALES DOES isolate. localeFallbackCandidates appends getFallbackLocale() (DefaultStrings.java:2489), so the en request's candidate list is [en, ar]. Together with bidi-isolation-rtl-request-ltr-donor this answers, in both directions, which locale decides isolation when the requested and supplying locales disagree. 'Farewell {{name}}' is again absent everywhere so the returned-key path can be shown to use the requested (LTR) locale even on an RTL-fallback instance.

bidi-isolation-output-limit.description: BidiIsolation.ALWAYS with maximumInterpolatedOutputCharacters pinned to 10 -- far below DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_INTERPOLATED_OUTPUT_CHARACTERS (262144) and the MAXIMUM_ ceiling (1048576) in TranslationRuntimeLimits, and above the documented minimum of 1. The two isolate characters count against that budget: BidiUtils.isolatedValue wraps the value in a BoundedIsolatedValue, StringInterpolator hands render() the REMAINING budget (maximumOutputCharacters minus what is already emitted), and every character including FSI and PDI goes through an appendChecked. So the same value under the same limit succeeds with NONE and fails with ALWAYS. Sized so '[' + FSI + six characters + PDI + ']' lands exactly on 10 and a seventh character overruns it.

bidi-isolation-rtl-request-ltr-donor.description: The section 8.3 clause proper: an RTL lookup served by a fallback-locale entry. The ar catalog carries only a marker, so an Arabic request for Greeting.Named is supplied by the en fallback entry. getResult hands getInternal the candidateLocale (DefaultStrings.java:713), so shouldApplyBidiIsolation at :1367 sees en and the default RTL_LOCALES does NOT isolate. The key 'Farewell {{name}}' is deliberately in no catalog so the returned-key path -- which gets the REQUESTED locale instead (:754, :1406) -- can be contrasted on the identical request. Left at the default mode; NONE and ALWAYS are supplied per call. Same catalog shape as the existing evaluation-locale-bidi-donor-en fixture, restated here under its own id because that family cannot set a mode and this one exists to vary the mode on exactly this input.

bidi-isolation-script-detection.description: Isolates the two branches of BidiUtils.localeUsesRightToLeftScript on one primary language. 'ar' has no script subtag, so the method takes the CldrLocaleData.likelySubtagFor branch (ar -> ar-Arab-EG, script Arab, which is in GeneratedCldrLocaleData.RTL_SCRIPTS); 'ar-Latn' carries an explicit script that short-circuits that lookup and is LTR. Both are loaded catalogs so each request resolves to itself and the requested/donor question does not confound the script question. Two locales share the language code ar, so tiebreakers are mandatory and list exactly {ar, ar-Latn} -- an exact permutation, as DefaultStrings.java:393-408 requires.

bidi-isolation-value-shapes.description: BidiIsolation.ALWAYS in a plain en catalog so isolation is unconditional and every case varies only the caller-supplied VALUE. Exercises BidiUtils.isolate's whole decision table: the FSI/PDI wrap, idempotence for values already isolated with LRI/RLI/FSI, the isIsolated guards (valueLength < 2, depth returning to zero before the final character), dropping of unmatched PDIs, balancing of unclosed initiators, the zero-length early return, non-CharSequence rendering, and the value != null guard at DefaultStrings.java:1367. The template brackets the slot so the marks' position is observable.

browser-chooser-canonical-collision.description: Two pairs of loaded sources that collide under CLDR canonicalization without sharing a written primary language code: mo/ro and cmn/zh. DefaultStrings requires tiebreakers keyed by the CANONICAL language code here (ro:[mo, ro], zh:[cmn, zh]). VERIFIED by building it without them, which fails with: You must specify tiebreaker locales via 'tiebreakerLocalesByLanguageCode' to resolve ambiguity for language code 'ro' because localized strings exist for the following locale[s]: [mo, ro]. This is the configuration in which the whole-list solver and the single-locale kernel actually select different locales for the same request.

browser-chooser-en-regional.description: Supported {en-US, en-GB} with NO bare en source, tiebreaker en:[en-US, en-GB], and a French fallback. Every en-flavored request therefore has to be resolved heuristically among two same-language regional sources, which is the configuration in which tiebreaker order, q=0 exclusion, and wildcard fallback preference each become observable. The fallback is deliberately fr, so a wildcard returning 'the first supported locale' (en-GB in sorted order) differs from one returning the configured fallback.

browser-chooser-en-regional-reversed.description: browser-chooser-en-regional with the tiebreaker flipped to en:[en-GB, en-US] and nothing else changed, so the reversal cases have an otherwise-identical control.

browser-chooser-iana-aliases.description: One loaded source for each side of a set of pinned IANA/JDK equivalences that discriminate: he (vs iw), id (vs in), yi (vs ji), cmn (vs zh-cmn and zh-guoyu), yue (vs zh-yue), tlh (vs i-klingon), nan (vs zh-min-nan and zh-nan), jbo (vs art-lojban), ase (vs sgn-US and sgn-ase). MEASURED: only cmn collapses onto a shared canonical language code (zh) and it is alone there, so no tiebreakers are required and the fixture builds. zh itself is deliberately NOT loaded; browser-chooser-canonical-collision is the contrasting fixture where it is.

browser-chooser-jdk-cldr-conflict.description: The conflict DefaultStrings.java:1570-1576 documents in prose: the JDK's IANA equivalence table maps nsl to sgn-NO while CLDR canonicalizes sgn-NO to nsi. Both nsl and nsi are loaded so the two data sources point at different, individually reachable sources; they do not share a canonical language code, so no tiebreakers are needed and the fixture builds. A port that took the transitive union of the two tables would collapse nsl and nsi into one preference and could not reproduce these rows.

browser-chooser-many-languages.description: Eight unrelated single-language sources (en, fr, de, es, ja, pt, it, nl), no shared primary language and therefore no tiebreakers. A deliberately flat set: nothing here can be decided by tiebreaker order, and CLDR fallback is reachable only from an explicitly regional range, so the Accept-Language cases that use it isolate weight ordering, list ordering, q=0 rejection, header parsing, and the parsed-range limit.

browser-chooser-wildcard-fallback.description: Supported {de, fr, ja, zu} with the fallback set to ja, which is neither first nor last in sorted order. That separates the two rules in DefaultStrings.preferredLocaleForWildcard (DefaultStrings.java:1955): prefer the configured fallback when it survives, otherwise take the first surviving supported locale. A fixture whose fallback happened to sort first could not tell those apart, and having two locales sort ahead of the fallback lets a second exclusion prove the second rule really walks sorted order.

browser-chooser-zh-chooser.description: Plan v7 section 8.3's browser chooser, supported {zh, zh-Hant} plus en and fr, tiebreaker zh:[zh, zh-Hant], fallback en. Content-identical to ingress-smoke-browser-chooser by design: it is the baseline half of a reversal pair whose other half, browser-chooser-zh-chooser-reversed, differs ONLY in tiebreaker order, so any case whose answer depends on that order shows a different result across the two and any case that does not must show the same one.

browser-chooser-zh-chooser-reversed.description: The section 8.3 chooser with the tiebreaker flipped to zh:[zh-Hant, zh] and nothing else changed. Reversing an ordering the implementation genuinely consults must move the answer; reversing one it does not consult must not. Both outcomes are measured in this family, which is why the pair exists rather than a single fixture.

callback-interaction-expression-fragment.description: The third recognized contextualization branch. A generated placeholder declared with template members (translation plus fragment alternatives) is an ExpressionTranslation rather than a LanguageFormTranslation, and an expression evaluated over a non-numeric operand raises the library's own ExpressionEvaluationException -- the one recognized type at DefaultStrings.java:1270-1271 that no other fixture in this family can reach. Fragment.ViaPhonetic puts that fragment behind a phonetic placeholder, so a SUCCESSFUL resolver answer decides whether the fragment is reached at all. One locale, so the policy is never consulted and the contextualization is isolated.

Fragment.ViaPhonetic.commentary: The resolver's answer selects either a template that names the expression fragment or one that does not, so the callback's return value decides whether a later failure happens at all.

callback-interaction-first-cause.description: Three fallback candidates (en-US, en, fr) whose failures are structurally DIFFERENT, so the retained cause is identifiable by type and by message. The en-US entries fail through the PhoneticResolver (which always throws the sentinel 'sentinel-resolver-alpha'); the en entries fail either through a library-generated type mismatch (a String where Gender is required) or through the same resolver under a DIFFERENTLY NAMED generated placeholder, so a same-type pair is still distinguishable by the contextualized message. Fragment.First adds a third failure kind: an en-US expression-fragment placeholder over a poisoned operand, which raises the library's own ExpressionEvaluationException, paired against an en entry that fails through the resolver. Two keys pair an alternatives-only entry (NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE, no cause) with a resolver-failing entry in both orders, so the policy is consulted once with a null cause and once with one. The instance policy is any-failure so every candidate is reached by default and a per-call override can narrow it. Two loaded locales share 'en', so tiebreakers is mandatory and lists exactly en-US and en.

Article.commentary: Fails with IllegalArgumentException when personGender is a String, giving the en candidate a cause of a different TYPE from the resolver's.

Fragment.First.commentary: An expression-fragment placeholder. With a non-numeric badCount the comparison raises ExpressionEvaluationException, a library type that contextualization preserves rather than converting.

Mixed.NoMatchFirst.commentary: Alternatives-only with a false predicate: NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE with NO cause, so the first policy consultation carries a null cause.

callback-interaction-generated-error.description: A resolver that SUCCEEDS but answers with phonetic forms the catalog does not translate, so the failure is generated by the library after the callback returned rather than by the callback itself. One locale, so no policy consultation is possible and the contextualization of a library-generated error is isolated.

callback-interaction-nested-expansion.description: Generated placeholders that reference one another, so a resolver answer selects a template whose own resolution or expansion then fails. Nested.InnerFails has an outer placeholder over a TAGGED value selecting a template that names an inner placeholder over a RAW term, so only the inner one reaches the resolver and only it should be named by the contextualization -- and switching the tagged value to CONSONANT selects a template that names nothing, so the inner placeholder is never resolved at all and the same poisoned term never reaches the resolver. Nested.Cycle has the resolver's answer select a template that leads back to the placeholder that selected it, which is undetectable until interpolation and therefore produces the selection-annotated double contextualization at DefaultStrings.java:1356-1359. One locale, so the policy is never consulted.

callback-interaction-null-resolver.description: A resolver that returns null rather than throwing, so the failing exception is manufactured by the library on the callback's behalf at DefaultStrings.java:1169-1171. Both en catalogs use a phonetic placeholder over the same caller value but under DIFFERENT generated-placeholder names, so the two candidates fail with the same exception TYPE and the same inner message, and differ only in their contextualized wrapper -- which makes first-cause retention answerable by message alone. Two loaded locales share 'en', so tiebreakers is mandatory.

callback-interaction-policy-throws.description: Every extension point is hostile: the resolver throws, the fallback policy throws, and the failure handler throws, each with its own sentinel message so the escaping exception names which callback won. Three candidates (en-US, en, fr) so a policy consultation actually happens, and the en catalog carries an inert plain-text entry so a permissive per-call policy can recover. Two loaded locales share 'en', so tiebreakers is mandatory.

callback-interaction-recover.description: A resolver that always throws, plus two catalogs whose generated placeholders read DIFFERENT caller values: en-US reads a raw term (so the resolver is reached and throws) and en reads a value the caller may supply either tagged or raw. That makes a single lookup in which the resolver fails at the first candidate and is bypassed entirely at the second, so the fallback recovers and the retained failure is discarded. Both loaded locales carry 'en', so tiebreakers is mandatory.

callback-interaction-sentinel.description: One locale only, so no policy consultation is possible and the resolver-plus-handler pair is isolated. The resolver always throws a distinctively worded sentinel. Alongside the phonetic key sit a key that is simply absent from the catalog and an alternatives-only key whose sole predicate is false, so the two CAUSELESS failure reasons can be contrasted with the resolver's caused one under the same throwing handler.

Guest.Welcome.commentary: Alternatives-only with no default translation: an unmatched predicate yields NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE and no throwable.

callback-smoke-donor-locale.description: THE SHARP CASE. The key exists only in the fr fallback, so an en request is served by the fr catalog. The resolver returns VOWEL when handed fr and CONSONANT when handed en, so the rendered article reveals WHICH locale the callback received — the donor rule applied to callbacks.

callback-smoke-first-letter.description: A resolver that classifies by first letter. The control: proves the resolver is reached for a raw term and that its return value selects the branch.

callback-smoke-no-resolver.description: No resolver configured, so DefaultStrings installs its fail-fast default, which throws when first reached. Section 3.7: that becomes the current candidate's resolution failure.

callback-smoke-returns-null.description: A resolver that returns null. DefaultStrings.java:1169 raises IllegalArgumentException naming the placeholder and key.

callback-smoke-throws.description: A resolver that raises. Section 8.3 'callback exceptions' for the resolver rather than the failure handler.

classpath-discovery-basic.description: A well-formed two-locale catalog used as the fixed target for the package-validation cases: the package argument is overridden per case, so the catalog itself never varies and any difference in output is attributable to the package string alone.

classpath-discovery-empty-package.description: A package that EXISTS on the classpath but contains no loadable catalog — its only member is a plainly non-tag filename, expressed through rawFiles because only rawFiles can name a file. Distinguishes 'package present, nothing to load' (an empty result on both paths) from 'package absent' (a load failure). loadOnly because no locale is loaded at all.

classpath-discovery-entry-budget.description: One locale file under a discovery-entry budget of exactly 2, which is what a non-exhaustive classpath load of this package costs: one entry for the package URL and one for the directory entry. MEASURED to load successfully at that budget. The control half of the exhaustive-search pair. loadOnly because the budget is deliberately at the edge and nothing here needs a Strings.

classpath-discovery-entry-budget-exhaust.description: Byte-identical content and budget to classpath-discovery-entry-budget, with exhaustiveClasspathSearch enabled. MEASURED: the exhaustive pass charges an additional 'classpath roots' discovery entry, so this half exceeds the same budget the control half fits inside — the one place this oracle can observe the option at all. loadOnly because the load is meant to fail.

classpath-discovery-pkg-42-b7.description: A package name carrying digits and hyphens, which validateClasspathPackage must accept. The fixture id IS the package name, so the default-package case exercises the accepted shape end to end rather than merely surviving validation.

classpath-discovery-prefix-target.description: A real package whose name has 'classpath-discovery-prefix' as a strict prefix. Paired cases load this package exactly and then ask for the prefix, which must NOT resolve — an implementation matching classpath entries by prefix rather than by exact package resolution would find this catalog.

classpath-discovery-sibling.description: A single-locale catalog under its own package, existing only so another fixture's case can ask for THIS package by name. The oracle materializes every fixture as a sibling directory under one classpath root, so this proves discovery resolves the package argument against the root rather than against the case's own fixture directory.

classpath-filenames-accented-latin-decom.description: The DECOMPOSED spelling of the same name — 'cafe', U+0301 COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT, '.json' — kept in its own fixture because a normalization-insensitive filesystem would collide the two spellings inside one directory. Authoring note: verify the rawFiles key is 10 code points long and ends 'e', U+0301, '.json'. MEASURED on the oracle's host (APFS): the two spellings round-trip distinctly and the warning quotes each verbatim. Informational, because that is a filesystem property rather than a library one; where a platform normalizes, the two fixtures simply emit identical observations and nothing breaks.

classpath-filenames-accented-latin-preco.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named with PRECOMPOSED accented Latin — 'caf', U+00E9, '.json' — carrying the .json extension. Authoring note: the fixture is only meaningful if that single code point survives into the repository; verify the rawFiles key is 9 code points long. Informational: how a non-ASCII name reaches the loader depends on the platform's filename encoding and normalization policy.

classpath-filenames-case-collision.description: A valid en catalog plus 'de' and 'DE.json', two names that differ by case AND extension and therefore stay distinct on a case-insensitive filesystem while resolving to the SAME locale. Establishes that the classpath path's leniency is confined to filename PARSING and never extends to duplicate detection, and that the classpath diagnostic names BOTH colliding origins where the filesystem one names only the file it was on.

classpath-filenames-cjk-name.description: A valid en catalog plus a CJK-named file with a .json extension — multi-byte in UTF-8, one UTF-16 unit per character. Informational: filesystem encoding of non-ASCII names is platform-dependent.

classpath-filenames-dot-inside-stem.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'en.GB' — a dot used where a hyphen belongs, with no extension at all. LANGUAGE_TAG_PATTERN (LocalizedStringLoader.java:189) admits only hyphen-separated alphanumeric subtags, so the dot is fatal to recognition but not to the load.

classpath-filenames-doubled-json-extensi.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'de.json.json'. Exactly one .json is stripped, leaving 'de.json' — proving the strip is single-shot rather than repeated until no extension remains.

classpath-filenames-eight-letter-json.description: A valid en catalog plus a file whose stem is eight ASCII letters and .json. VERIFIED against the source: eight characters satisfy LANGUAGE_TAG_PATTERN, Locale.Builder builds a locale whose language is nonempty, so the stem is rejected only by CldrLocaleData.isKnownLanguageTag at LocalizedStringLoader.java:1672 — the second of the two rejection routes inside isLanguageTag.

classpath-filenames-emoji-name.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named with a single astral-plane emoji (U+1F389) and a .json extension — a surrogate pair in Java's and JavaScript's UTF-16 string model, so any diagnostic that slices by code unit can split it. Informational.

classpath-filenames-empty-extension-json.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'de..json' — a valid tag, an empty extension, then .json. languageTagForFileName removes exactly JSON_EXTENSION.length() characters (LocalizedStringLoader.java:1691), leaving the trailing dot behind, which the tag pattern rejects.

classpath-filenames-exhaustive-search.description: A valid en catalog plus one offending name, loaded with exhaustiveClasspathSearch enabled. classpath-smoke pins the option against a clean catalog only; this asks whether a broader scan re-visits the same directory entry and emits the warning twice. Exactly one offending file, so no ordering can vary.

classpath-filenames-explicit-bypass.description: A valid en catalog plus one file of each rejected class: 'catalog.json' (throws during discovery), '.de' (hidden), and 'notes.txt' (unrecognised, skipped in silence). Each is then also named as an EXPLICIT classpath resource, where the filename rules do not apply at all — same bytes, same package, different outcomes depending on the entry point. Also the host fixture for the three loadFromClasspathResources path-validation cases, which need only a classloader root.

classpath-filenames-hidden-extension-onl.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named '.json' — the extension with no stem at all. Hidden by the leading dot; had it been parsed, the stripped stem would be the empty string, which no other fixture can produce.

classpath-filenames-hidden-tag.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named '.de' — a leading dot over a valid tag. isHiddenFileName (LocalizedStringLoader.java:1682) is consulted BEFORE any tag parsing on all three discovery paths (:1257 filesystem, :1313 classpath directory, :1406 JAR).

classpath-filenames-hidden-tag-json.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named '.de.json'. Were the .json rule consulted first, the residual stem '.de' would make tag parsing throw exactly as 'de..json' does; the hidden-name check at :1257/:1313 runs first, so nothing is even attempted. The sharpest ordering assertion in the family.

classpath-filenames-invalid-json-only.description: A package containing ONE file, 'catalog.json', and no loadable catalog at all. Isolates what each path returns when every candidate name is rejected. MEASURED: the classpath path is an EMPTY SUCCESS with one warning; the filesystem path is a hard failure.

classpath-filenames-legacy-tag.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'i-klingon.json' — a grandfathered/legacy IETF tag. LANGUAGE_TAG_PATTERN admits it, Locale.Builder accepts it, and Locale.forLanguageTag REWRITES it. MEASURED: the loaded locale key is 'tlh', not 'i-klingon'. Plan section 8.3 requires legacy tags; this is the filename-discovery instance of that rule.

classpath-filenames-long-name-json.description: A valid en catalog plus a file whose stem is 200 ASCII letters and .json (205 bytes, comfortably inside the 255-byte per-component limit on the oracle's host). The diagnostic interpolates the whole filename twice — once in the warning source and once in the message — so this pins that neither is truncated or elided.

classpath-filenames-lowercase-region.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'de-de.json'. The stem is accepted case-insensitively and then handed to Locale.forLanguageTag, so the emitted locale key is the canonical REGION form rather than the filename's spelling. MEASURED: loads as 'de-DE'.

classpath-filenames-lowercase-script.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'zh-hant.json' — a lowercase SCRIPT subtag. Script canonicalization is title-case where region canonicalization is upper-case, so this is a separate transform from the de-de fixture and a port could get one right and the other wrong. MEASURED: loads as 'zh-Hant'.

classpath-filenames-mixed-case-extension.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'de.Json'. The mixed-case variant of the case-insensitive extension check at LocalizedStringLoader.java:1677, separated from the all-uppercase fixture so each spelling is asserted on its own.

classpath-filenames-nine-letter-json.description: A valid en catalog plus a file whose stem is nine ASCII letters and .json. Nine characters fail LANGUAGE_TAG_PATTERN outright at LocalizedStringLoader.java:1652 — the first rejection route — so this and the eight-letter fixture reach the same throw and the same message by different internal paths.

classpath-filenames-nine-letter-stem.description: A valid en catalog plus an extensionless file whose stem is nine ASCII letters, one past LANGUAGE_TAG_PATTERN's 8-character subtag ceiling. The extensionless half of the length-boundary pair; the .json half throws on the identical stem.

classpath-filenames-non-ascii-no-extensi.description: A valid en catalog plus the precomposed accented name with NO extension. The control for the non-ASCII group: without .json a non-ASCII name returns null instead of throwing, so it never reaches the diagnostic at all. MEASURED: silent skip on both paths. Informational for the same platform-encoding reason as the rest of the group.

classpath-filenames-non-json-extension.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'de.txt' — a VALID tag under a non-.json extension. The extension is not stripped, so the whole name is tested against the tag pattern, which the embedded dot defeats. MEASURED: skipped in silence on both paths, no warning.

classpath-filenames-numeric-first-subtag.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named '419.json'. LANGUAGE_TAG_PATTERN requires the FIRST subtag to be alphabetic ([A-Za-z]{1,8}) while later subtags may be alphanumeric, so a purely numeric stem fails the pattern for a reason unrelated to length. The rejection route that the nine-letter fixture cannot reach.

classpath-filenames-private-use-stem.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'x-custom.json'. isLanguageTag has an explicit early return for stems beginning 'x-' (LocalizedStringLoader.java:1663) that runs AFTER Locale.Builder but BEFORE both the empty-language check and the CLDR known-tag lookup. MEASURED: loads as 'x-custom'.

classpath-filenames-region-dot-json.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'en.GB.json'. Stripping exactly one .json leaves 'en.GB', which the tag pattern rejects — so this is the throwing counterpart of the extensionless 'en.GB' fixture, and a port that split on the FIRST dot would derive 'en' and collide with the real en catalog instead.

classpath-filenames-root-stem.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'root.json'. 'root' satisfies LANGUAGE_TAG_PATTERN and Locale.Builder and resolves to a nonempty language, so it survives every check except CldrLocaleData.isKnownLanguageTag (LocalizedStringLoader.java:1672). MEASURED: it is REJECTED — a port that special-cases 'root' alongside 'und' loads a catalog Java refuses.

classpath-filenames-rtl-name.description: A valid en catalog plus an Arabic-script (right-to-left) named file with a .json extension. The diagnostic quotes the name inside a left-to-right message with no bidi isolation applied, so this also records how an RTL run is embedded in a warning. Informational.

classpath-filenames-three-letter-languag.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'deu.json' — the ISO 639-2 alpha-3 code for German. MEASURED: the loaded key stays 'deu' and is NOT folded to the alpha-2 'de', which several JS canonicalisation routines would do.

classpath-filenames-trailing-dot.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'de.' — a valid tag followed by a bare trailing dot and no extension. Neither the .json branch nor the tag pattern accepts it. MEASURED: skipped in silence on both paths.

classpath-filenames-two-invalid-json.description: A valid en catalog plus TWO offending names, 'zz.json' and 'notes.json'. Pins that discovery reports one warning PER offending file rather than collapsing to one, and that the filesystem path aborts on the first it reaches rather than collecting. Warning order and which name the filesystem failure quotes both follow DirectoryStream iteration order, which is filesystem- and platform-dependent — hence both its cases are informational.

classpath-filenames-underscore-separator.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'de_DE.json' — the Java Locale.toString() spelling rather than the BCP 47 one. Underscore is absent from LANGUAGE_TAG_PATTERN. The single most likely filename a port would wrongly accept.

classpath-filenames-undetermined-stem.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'und.json'. isLanguageTag treats the explicitly-undetermined tag as an exception (LocalizedStringLoader.java:1666) to the empty-resolved-language rejection at :1669, then still requires CLDR membership at :1672. MEASURED: loads as 'und'.

classpath-filenames-undetermined-with-sc.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'und-Latn.json'. The undetermined exception at LocalizedStringLoader.java:1666 is a DISJUNCTION — equalsIgnoreCase("und") OR startsWith("und-") — and only this fixture exercises the second half. MEASURED: loads as 'und-Latn'; a port implementing only the exact-'und' half loses it.

classpath-filenames-unknown-language-jso.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'zz.json'. The stem 'zz' is syntactically a well-formed tag and Locale.Builder accepts it, but CldrLocaleData.isKnownLanguageTag rejects it; classpath-smoke already pins that the EXTENSIONLESS 'zz' is skipped in silence, so this fixture isolates the extension as the only difference.

classpath-filenames-uppercase-extension.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'DE.JSON'. hasJsonExtension lowercases the whole name before the endsWith check (LocalizedStringLoader.java:1677), so an all-uppercase extension is still recognised and stripped. MEASURED: loads as 'de'.

classpath-filenames-uppercase-private-us.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'X-Custom.json'. The 'x-' gate at LocalizedStringLoader.java:1663 lowercases with Locale.ROOT before testing the prefix, so an uppercase private-use marker takes the same escape hatch. MEASURED: loads, and the key canonicalises to lowercase 'x-custom'.

classpath-filenames-uppercase-stem.description: A valid en catalog plus an extensionless file named 'DE'. isLanguageTag (LocalizedStringLoader.java:1649) runs the stem through LANGUAGE_TAG_PATTERN, Locale.Builder and CldrLocaleData.isKnownLanguageTag, all of which accept it case-insensitively; the emitted key is then Locale.forLanguageTag's canonical form. MEASURED: loads as 'de'.

classpath-filenames-valid-json-extension.description: A valid en catalog plus a file named 'de.json' — a valid IETF BCP 47 tag carrying the .json extension. Serves the 'valid tag WITH .json' side of the filename boundary; the classpath-smoke family only ever wrote extensionless names. MEASURED: loads as de on both paths.

classpath-filenames-warning-limit-zero.description: A valid en catalog plus one offending name, loaded with maximumWarnings set to 0. The classpath path downgrades a filename throw to a warning, but that warning still goes through the loading session's warning budget. MEASURED: with a zero budget the classpath load HARD-FAILS, with a limit message rather than the filename message — the classpath path's leniency is conditional, not absolute. One offending file, so the outcome is order-independent.

classpath-resources-alt.description: A second, separate classpath package holding one file with its own marker key Only.Alt. Exists so a case anchored on classpath-resources-catalog can name a resource in a DIFFERENT package, proving explicit resource paths resolve from the classpath root rather than relative to the package under test. Verified loadable on its own (single en locale), so it is safe as a non-loadOnly fixture even though no case uses it as its own subject.

classpath-resources-byte-budget.description: Two catalogs of exactly 52 bytes each as build.mjs materializes them (JSON.stringify with two-space indent plus a trailing newline — measured, not assumed) under a 60-byte maximumTotalInputBytes: one resource fits, two do not, and the same resource mapped twice also does not. Sized so the budget can only be explained by accumulation across the whole mapping, never by a per-file cap. loadOnly because the filesystem load reads both files.

classpath-resources-catalog.description: A clean three-locale catalog in which every file carries a unique marker key (Only.En, Only.De, Only.Fr) alongside a shared Common.Greeting. The markers are the point: because loadFromClasspathResources takes the locale from the caller, the only way to observe WHICH resource landed under WHICH locale is a per-file key. Serves the multi-locale, locale-key, conflict and resource-path clauses. Verified to load from the filesystem as de/en/fr with three distinct primary languages, so no tiebreakers are required and Strings construction succeeds.

classpath-resources-discovery-budget.description: Two files under maximumDiscoveryEntries of 1. Discovery on this package fails on the budget; an explicit mapping of both files succeeds, because loadFromClasspathResources never charges a discovery entry. The two cases on this fixture are a matched pair on one option. loadOnly because directory discovery fails — verified for both the filesystem and classpath directory forms.

classpath-resources-file-limit.description: Three loadable files under an aggregate maximumLocalizedStringsFiles of 2, so a mapping of three trips the limit, a mapping of two sits exactly at it, and discovery over the whole package trips it with different wording. loadOnly because the filesystem load of three files also exceeds the limit — verified.

classpath-resources-malformed.description: One good catalog plus four files that discovery treats very differently from an explicit mapping: 'messages' (valid JSON, a well-formed but CLDR-unknown language subtag), 'blank' (zero bytes), 'broken.json' (unterminated, and the only name here that makes tag parsing THROW because of its .json extension) and 'dupes' (repeated JSON member). Every filename must be a rawFiles entry, since 'files' names each file by its locale tag and cannot express an arbitrary name. loadOnly because broken.json hard-fails the filesystem load — verified. Serves the content-diagnostic, load-order and validation-precedence clauses.

classpath-resources-nonascii.description: NEW. One ordinary en catalog plus two rawFiles that are byte-for-byte twins except for the encoding of their NAME: 'messages' (ASCII) and '文字' (non-ASCII). CJK was chosen deliberately over a Latin accent because CJK ideographs have no canonical decomposition, so the name cannot differ between an NFC-writing build machine and an NFD-normalizing filesystem. Serves the clause's 'portable ASCII identifiers, and non-ASCII identifiers classified as informational' requirement. Not loadOnly: verified that both the filesystem and discovery loads pick up only 'en' and skip the two non-tag names silently, so Strings construction succeeds.

classpath-resources-warner.description: A single catalog whose only placeholder declares CARDINALITY_ONE and nothing else, so it emits exactly one INCOMPLETE_CARDINALITY_TRANSLATIONS warning whose missing-form set is decided entirely by the locale it is validated against. Mapped under three different keys to prove the caller's key drives validation, not the filename. Verified to load and construct Strings from the filesystem (single ru locale, fallback ru).

classpath-resources-warning-budget.description: REWORKED from the authored draft, which held one file under maximumWarnings 0 and so could not demonstrate anything shared across a mapping. Now TWO incomplete-cardinality catalogs (ru and de) under maximumWarnings of 1: one mapped resource succeeds at exactly the limit, two exceed it. That pair is the only way to show the warning counter lives in the same LoadingSession that spans the whole explicit mapping. loadOnly because the filesystem load reads both files and fails the same way — verified.

classpath-smoke-bad-filename.description: A valid catalog plus files whose names are not loadable locale tags. The filesystem loader SKIPS these silently, while classpath discovery emits INVALID_CLASSPATH_LOCALE_FILENAME and ignores them — the only reachable source of that warning type, and a genuine divergence between the two paths.

classpath-smoke-basic.description: A well-formed two-locale catalog, loaded both ways. The classpath and filesystem discovery paths must agree on identical inputs; this fixture is the paired control that makes any later divergence attributable to the input rather than the path.

classpath-smoke-exhaustive.description: The same catalog loaded with exhaustiveClasspathSearch toggled, so the option's effect on discovery is observable rather than assumed.

classpath-smoke-json-extension.description: A valid catalog plus a file whose name carries a .json extension over a stem that is not a loadable tag. On the filesystem this shape is a HARD load failure naming the file. This fixture asks what classpath discovery does with the same shape.

custom-policy-dedup-chain.description: Post-resolution first-wins dedup observed through the POLICY channel. Loads ro and en with fallback en; no mo catalog exists, so every mo observation is resolution behavior rather than loading behavior. Requesting mo-MD produces a raw candidate set containing both mo and ro, but localizedStringsFor folds each raw candidate onto a catalog BEFORE the putIfAbsent at DefaultStrings.java:2498, which is keyed by that RESOLVED attempted locale; the executed chain is therefore exactly [mo-MD, ro, ro-MD, en] — measured, not assumed — with raw mo already collapsed onto loaded ro and the later raw ro candidate producing NO second entry and hence no second consultation. Requesting bare mo collapses further to [ro, en], with mo absent from attemptedLocales entirely. Dedup.OnlyInRo and Dedup.OnlyInEn separate the two catalogs, Dedup.Shared exists in both so first-wins is visible, and Dedup.Missing exists nowhere. Loaded ro and en have distinct primary language codes, so no tiebreakers are required.

custom-policy-four-candidate-chain.description: A FOUR-candidate chain for the caller-supplied-policy clauses. Requesting en-GB against loaded en-GB, en-001, en with FALLBACK LOCALE fr makes localeFallbackCandidates (DefaultStrings.java:2474-2503) produce exactly [en-GB, en-001, en, fr] — measured by execution, not assumed. The fallback locale is fr and not en precisely because DefaultStrings.java:2489 appends getFallbackLocale() as the terminal candidate: with fallbackLocale en this same file set yields only THREE candidates and fr is never reached at all. Four distinct candidates are what make 'stopped at the second' separable from 'stopped at the last', and what make 'three policy calls for four attempts' a real count rather than a coincidence. Keys are built so different candidates fail for structurally different reasons inside ONE walk: Chain.NoMatchAtGb is alternatives-only at en-GB and absent at en-001, giving NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE followed by MISSING_TRANSLATION; Chain.ResolutionAtEn001 throws only at the second candidate; Chain.ThreeDistinctCauses throws a DIFFERENT exception type at each of the first three candidates (java.lang.IllegalStateException from a missing GENDER_NEUTER branch, java.lang.IllegalArgumentException from a placeholder whose context name is never supplied, and com.lokalized.ExpressionEvaluationException from comparing a raw string with >), all three confirmed distinct by execution, so the policy's cause argument is observable per call; Chain.FailsEverywhere fails at ALL FOUR candidates so policyCalls can be counted against attemptedLocales with no candidate succeeding. Chain.MissingEverywhere and Chain.OnlyInFallback serve the pure truncation arms, Chain.OnlyInEn the succeeds-after-truncation arm, and Chain.InEveryCatalog the no-consultation control. Three loaded locales share the primary language en, so tiebreakers is mandatory and lists that exact permutation; fr is alone in its language and needs none.

en.Chain.NoMatchAtGb: en: plain text the third candidate can serve
en.Chain.OnlyInEn: en: only the third candidate has this
en.Chain.ResolutionAtEn001: en: plain text the third candidate can serve

Chain.ThreeDistinctCauses.commentary: rank is supplied as the raw string 'high', so evaluating rank > 1 throws ExpressionEvaluationException, a THIRD distinct type.

Chain.ResolutionAtEn001.commentary: GENDER_NEUTER absent: IllegalStateException at the SECOND candidate only.

Chain.ThreeDistinctCauses.commentary: Reads context name absentCount, which no case supplies: IllegalArgumentException, a DIFFERENT type from en-GB's.

Chain.FailsEverywhere.commentary: Reads context name absentCount, which no case supplies: IllegalArgumentException.

Chain.NoMatchAtGb.commentary: Alternatives-only. tier == 1 matches; any other tier yields NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE at the FIRST candidate.

Chain.ThreeDistinctCauses.commentary: GENDER_NEUTER is deliberately absent, so a tagged NEUTER value throws IllegalStateException 'Missing Gender translation for NEUTER'.

fr.Chain.OnlyInFallback: fr: only the fallback catalog has this
fr.Chain.ThreeDistinctCauses: fr: fallback text after three distinct causes

custom-policy-instance-continue-for-loca.description: A caller-supplied policy installed at the INSTANCE, not per call, so DefaultStrings.java:685-686 (options.getTranslationFallbackPolicy().orElse(getTranslationFallbackPolicy())) is exercised in both directions for a policy that is not one of the three library singletons. Requesting es-AR against loaded es-AR, es-419, es with fallback en yields the four-candidate chain [es-AR, es-419, es, en], verified by execution. The instance policy continues only for es-AR and es-419, so it halts at es and forfeits the en catalog that holds Inst.OnlyInFallback unless a per-call policy replaces it. Inst.InEveryCatalog is the no-consultation control and Inst.MissingEverywhere exists nowhere. Three loaded locales share the primary language es, so tiebreakers lists that exact permutation.

en.Inst.OnlyInFallback: en: only the fallback catalog has this

custom-policy-resolver-exception-chain.description: The THIRD callback's exception inside a multi-candidate walk. Section 8.3's 'callback exceptions' clause covers the policy and the handler in the fixtures above; this one covers the PhoneticResolver, which callback-smoke exercises only on single-candidate chains where no policy consultation can occur. The instance resolver is throw, so any RAW phonetic term at any candidate raises IllegalStateException inside getInternal and is converted to a RESOLUTION_FAILURE the policy then decides on — the resolver's own throwable reaching the policy's cause argument, which no other family shows. Loading fr-CA, fr and en with fallback en, requesting fr-CA executes as exactly [fr-CA, fr, en], verified. Res.Article carries a phonetic placeholder at BOTH fr-CA and fr and plain text at en, so a policy that continues past RESOLUTION_FAILURE produces TWO resolver invocations carrying two DIFFERENT donor locales before en serves — the donor rule for callbacks proven across a walk rather than at one candidate. Res.OnlyAtEn is absent from the first two catalogs and carries the phonetic placeholder at the LAST candidate, so its resolver exception lands where no further consultation may occur. Loaded fr-CA and fr share the primary language fr, so tiebreakers lists that exact permutation.

en.Res.Article: en: plain text after two resolver failures

Res.OnlyAtEn.commentary: Present ONLY at the final candidate, so its resolver exception occurs where DefaultStrings.java:731-733 has already broken out of the consultation.

Res.Article.commentary: The same placeholder at the SECOND candidate, so a continuing policy produces a second resolver call with a different donor locale.
Phonetic placeholder at the FIRST candidate. A raw term reaches the throwing resolver; a tagged value does not.

custom-policy-single-candidate-throwing-.description: A ONE-candidate chain with a throwing policy AND a throwing handler installed at the instance, deliberately given different messages so which callback fires is readable from the thrown identity alone. Loading only en with fallback en and requesting en produces the single-element chain [en], verified by execution. DefaultStrings.java:731-733 breaks on candidateIndex + 1 >= fallbackCandidates.size() BEFORE reaching shouldTryNextLocale, so a policy that would throw on any consultation is inert here and the handler's exception is what escapes. Requesting an unloaded de against the same fixture builds the two-element chain [de, en], restoring one consultation and making the policy fire, so chain length is isolated as the only variable. This is the sharpest available statement of 'no policy call after the final distinct candidate': the two callbacks are made to disagree, and which one fires names the answer.

custom-policy-throwing-policy.description: A caller-supplied policy that itself raises. The instance policy is throw-in-policy with a fixed message and the instance handler is return-key. DefaultStrings.java:734-735 calls shouldTryNextLocale OUTSIDE the try block that guards getInternal, so the exception is not converted into a RESOLUTION_FAILURE and not recoverable by fallback: it leaves getResult entirely, before the failure handler at :747 is ever consulted. FALLBACK LOCALE fr gives the same four-candidate [en-GB, en-001, en, fr] shape as custom-policy-four-candidate-chain (with fallbackLocale en the chain is three long and fr is unreachable, which would make the neutralized-policy case assert a walk that cannot happen), so the throw occurs at the FIRST consultation and the message identifies which policy fired. Throwing.Present exists only at en-GB, giving a control in which the walk returns before any consultation; Throwing.OnlyInFallback is served by the last candidate once the policy is replaced; Throwing.MissingEverywhere is served by none. Three loaded locales share the primary language en, so tiebreakers lists that exact permutation.

en-GB.Throwing.Present: en-GB: present at the first candidate

fr.Throwing.OnlyInFallback: fr: only the fallback catalog has this

dedup-and-candidates-alias-region.description: First-wins dedup through a region alias rather than a language alias. Loads hy-AM and en with fallback en. CldrLocaleData.fallbackLocalesFor(hy-SU) is [hy-SU, hy, hy-AM] and canonicalLanguageTag('hy-SU') is 'hy-AM' (both verified against the library), so localizedStringsFor maps the requested hy-SU onto loaded hy-AM and the later raw hy-AM candidate is dropped as a duplicate. The resulting attempted chain leads with the alias TARGET and never contains the requested tag, while the bare 'hy' candidate - which CLDR orders before hy-AM - ends up second. Alias.Missing exists nowhere.

dedup-and-candidates-equivalent-am-first.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 'distinct-but-equivalent loaded tags remaining separate and resolving through exact identity plus tiebreakers'. hy-AM and hy-SU are canonically equivalent (canonicalLanguageTag('hy-SU') is 'hy-AM') but are DISTINCT java.util.Locale values, so the loader keeps two catalogs. Both normalize to language code 'hy', so DefaultStrings requires - and this fixture supplies - the exact permutation tiebreaker list, here ordered hy-AM before hy-SU. Pair.InBoth exists in both equivalent catalogs so the tiebreaker choice is visible in the translation itself; Pair.OnlyInAm and Pair.OnlyInSu prove the catalogs were not merged; Pair.Missing exercises the whole deduped chain. Paired with dedup-and-candidates-equivalent-su-first, which differs ONLY in tiebreaker order.

dedup-and-candidates-equivalent-fallback.description: The tiebreaker-resolved FALLBACK locale, the third branch of DefaultStrings.java:446-469, which no other fixture in the corpus reaches. Loads the same two canonically-equivalent catalogs, hy-AM and hy-SU, but configures fallbackLocale arm-SU - a tag that is loaded nowhere and is canonically equivalent to BOTH of them (canonicalLanguageTag('arm-SU') is 'hy-AM', verified), so neither the exact-hit branch at 446 nor the single-equivalent branch at 448 can settle it. Construction therefore walks the tiebreaker list and adopts its first entry that is canonically equivalent to the configured tag: hy-AM here. Paired with dedup-and-candidates-equivalent-fallback-su-first, whose only difference is the reversed list.

Byte-identical files and fallbackLocale to dedup-and-candidates-equivalent-fallback-am-first, with the tiebreaker list reversed to hy-SU before hy-AM. The instance's effective fallback locale must flip to hy-SU, which is observable in every emitted match object as well as in the tail of every candidate chain.

dedup-and-candidates-equivalent-mo-ro-lo.description: The load half of the clause's named mo/ro pair, which the resolution cases cannot reach (see skipped). LocalizedStringLoader keys catalogs by Locale.forLanguageTag(fileName) (LocalizedStringLoader.java:1260-1269) and does NOT canonicalize, so mo and ro - canonically equivalent but distinct Locale values - must survive as two separate catalogs with two separate key sets. loadOnly because DefaultStrings would refuse to build from this pair without tiebreakers keyed by their shared canonical language code 'ro', and that fixture shape is not expressible through the ingest linter today; the load itself succeeds, which is exactly what this fixture observes.

dedup-and-candidates-equivalent-su-first.description: Byte-identical files to dedup-and-candidates-equivalent-am-first with the tiebreaker list REVERSED to hy-SU before hy-AM. Everything a port could accidentally key on - file contents, load order, tag alphabetical order, canonical form - is unchanged, so any difference in the two fixtures' observations is attributable to the tiebreaker list alone. The tiebreakers govern lookupMatchByLikelySubtag (DefaultStrings.java:2586) and the tiebreaker candidates appended at DefaultStrings.java:2482-2488, so both the selected catalog and the deduped attempted order flip.

dedup-and-candidates-fallback-alias.description: The configured fallback locale is itself subject to equivalence resolution, through the single-equivalent branch at DefaultStrings.java:448-449. fallbackLocale is mo, but only ro and en are loaded; exactly one loaded locale is canonically equivalent to mo, so the instance adopts it and its effective fallback is ro. Every candidate chain therefore terminates at ro, the en catalog is unreachable from a request that does not select it, and the emitted match.fallbackLocale is ro rather than the configured mo. The ingest linter warns that fallbackLocale is not among the loaded files; that is the point of the fixture.

dedup-and-candidates-legacy-collision.description: Two filenames that canonicalize to the SAME locale, which the loader treats as a conflict rather than a merge or a last-wins overwrite. he and iw both map to Locale.forLanguageTag('iw') == Locale.forLanguageTag('he'), so the containsKey guard at LocalizedStringLoader.java:1265-1267 throws LocalizedStringLoadingException. Written as rawFiles because the two names are FILENAMES, not two locale-tagged catalogs. loadOnly because the load is deliberately unloadable.

dedup-and-candidates-legacy-filename.description: Distinct-spelling filename that is NOT distinct as a locale. LocalizedStringLoader.java:1260-1269 turns a filename into Locale.forLanguageTag(tag) and keys the catalog by that Locale; Locale.forLanguageTag('iw') and Locale.forLanguageTag('he') are the SAME value, whose toLanguageTag() is 'he' (verified against the pinned JDK). So the file written as 'iw' surfaces as loaded locale he, and both spellings of the request reach it. Contrast with dedup-and-candidates-equivalent-am-first, where the equivalent tags stay separate because their Locale values differ.

dedup-and-candidates-mo-ro.description: Post-resolution first-wins dedup for the clause's named example, mo resolving to loaded ro. Loads ro and en with fallback en; no mo catalog exists, so every mo observation is resolution behavior rather than loading behavior. localeFallbackCandidates (DefaultStrings.java:2474-2503) builds the raw candidate set for mo as [mo, ro, en]: CldrLocaleData.fallbackLocalesFor(mo) is [mo, ro], the likely-subtag match for ro-Latn re-adds ro, the auto-identity tiebreaker DefaultStrings installs for language code 'ro' re-adds it again, and the fallback locale is appended at 2489. Dedup happens AFTER each raw candidate is resolved to a catalog by localizedStringsFor (2506) - canonicalLanguageTag('mo') is 'ro', so mo maps onto loaded ro - and the putIfAbsent at 2498 is keyed by that RESOLVED attempted locale, so the walk sees two candidates, not three. Dedup.Shared exists in both catalogs to show which one first-wins keeps. Dedup.ResolutionFailure is a cardinality placeholder over the context name 'absentCount', which no case supplies, so ro throws IllegalArgumentException at DefaultStrings.java:966-968 while the same key is a plain string in en; that pair makes policy truncation visible against a reachable translation. Its ro translations declare Romanian's complete cardinality set (one/few/other) so the load emits no warning and the fixture isolates exactly one failure cause. Dedup.Missing exists nowhere. Loaded ro and en have distinct language codes, so no tiebreakers are required.

dedup-and-candidates-ro-only.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 'no policy call after the final distinct candidate'. Exactly one loaded catalog, ro, which is also the fallback locale. Requesting mo produces the raw candidate set [mo, ro, ro, ro] (CLDR fallback, likely-subtag match, identity tiebreaker, fallback locale), every entry of which resolves onto loaded ro, so the loop at DefaultStrings.java:2493-2500 hands the walk a ONE-element candidate list. The walk at DefaultStrings.java:731 then breaks on candidateIndex + 1 >= size BEFORE reaching the translationFallbackPolicy call on line 734, so the policy is never invoked. Cases pair the default policy against neverFallback on this fixture: Java must emit identical observations for both, which is the corpus's observable form of the no-trailing-policy-call rule.

direct-en-au.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 seed row 3: en-AU reaches en-001 through the CLDR parent chain rather than jumping straight to en. Tiebreakers are mandatory here because two loaded locales share the language code 'en'; they order a bare 'en' request and must not be what carries en-AU to en-001.

direct-en-us.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 seed row 5: a direct en-US lookup against a lone loaded en must still report a non-null cldr-fallback diagnostic rather than a null selection.

direct-fr-be.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 seed row 2: fr-BE is not loaded; the tiebreaker list prefers fr-FR to fr-CA and the diagnostic channel reports a likely-subtag selection.

direct-und-latn.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 seed row 1: an undetermined-language request with a script reaches no loaded locale and lands on the fallback, while the diagnostic channel reports no selection at all.

direct-zh-tw.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 seed row 4: the diagnostic channel selects zh-Hant, but zh-Hant lacks the key, so per-key resolution continues to the fallback en WITHOUT visiting the loaded zh that does have it. This is the case that proves the two channels are genuinely independent.

evaluation-locale-alternative-passthroug.description: Two donors in one lookup, each evaluated under its own locale. Chain.Alt exists in BOTH pl and en. The pl entry has no `translation` and a single alternative gated on `itemCount == CARDINALITY_FEW`, so when Polish rules do not say FEW the entry yields Optional.empty -- NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE, which the default policy DOES continue past. The en entry is then evaluated under English rules, and its alternative is gated on `itemCount == CARDINALITY_OTHER`. A count therefore has to be classified twice, under two different locales, inside one getResult call. LocalizedStringLoader accepts a bare string as an alternative's value (parseLocalizedString's isString branch), so no nested {"translation": ...} wrapper is needed.

Chain.Alt.commentary: No default translation on purpose: an unmatched alternative here yields Optional.empty, which getResult records as NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE -- the one failure reason the default fallback policy continues past.

evaluation-locale-bidi-donor-en.description: The bidi channel of 'evaluated under the supplying locale'. interpolateTemplate wraps caller-supplied placeholder values in isolate marks when shouldApplyBidiIsolation(locale, bidiIsolation) is true, and that `locale` is the donor (DefaultStrings.java:1367); interpolateFailureKey (DefaultStrings.java:754) is handed the REQUESTED locale instead. With the default BidiIsolation.RTL_LOCALES an Arabic request served by the English donor therefore gets no isolation, while the returned-key path for the same Arabic request does. Confirmed empirically against the oracle: the resolved Arabic-request translation is 'Hello, Sarah' with no U+2068/U+2069, while the returned-key one is 'Farewell.Named ⁨Sarah⁩'. Only en carries Greeting.Named; the key used by the returned-key cases exists in no catalog at all.

evaluation-locale-donor-missing-branch.description: An under-translated Russian donor: Items.Sparse declares only CARDINALITY_ONE and CARDINALITY_OTHER even though Russian has four categories. Selecting FEW or MANY under the donor's own rules therefore reaches the 'Missing Cardinality translation for ...' IllegalStateException in DefaultStrings, which getResult records as a RESOLUTION_FAILURE; the default TranslationFallbackPolicy (DefaultTranslationFallbackPolicy.MISSING_OR_NO_MATCH returns reason != RESOLUTION_FAILURE) stops there rather than trying another locale, and the default TranslationFailureHandler then produces the returned key. Verified against the oracle: status RETURNED_KEY, failureReason RESOLUTION_FAILURE, translation 'Items.Sparse'. The point is that the failure only happens if evaluation used Russian rules: under English rules every one of these counts would land on OTHER and quietly succeed.

evaluation-locale-fallback-ar.description: Arabic is the fallback donor for en, pl, ru and fr requests. Arabic is the only one of the seven languages with ZERO and TWO categories, so a fallback that lands on CARDINALITY_ZERO or CARDINALITY_TWO is proof positive that evaluation used the donor's rules. The catalog also carries an RTL template with a caller-supplied placeholder, because interpolateTemplate decides bidi isolation from the same `locale` argument it uses for plural selection (shouldApplyBidiIsolation(locale, bidiIsolation) at DefaultStrings.java:1367), i.e. from the donor.

evaluation-locale-fallback-en.description: English is the fallback donor for pl, ru, ar, fr and pt requests, and its Items.Fallback entry declares ONLY CARDINALITY_ONE and CARDINALITY_OTHER. That makes the fixture an asymmetric detector: under correct behavior every count resolves under English rules to ONE or OTHER and succeeds, while an implementation that evaluated under the REQUESTING locale would select FEW / MANY / ZERO / TWO, find no branch, raise the 'Missing Cardinality translation' IllegalStateException, and -- because the default TranslationFallbackPolicy does not fall past a RESOLUTION_FAILURE -- return the key. Rank.Fallback declares all six ordinality constants so English's ONE/TWO/FEW ordinal categories (which pl, ru, ar and pt do not have at all) are observable through a fallback as text rather than as a throw.

Items.Fallback.commentary: Deliberately only the two categories English actually has, which is what a real shipped English catalog looks like.

evaluation-locale-fallback-fr.description: French is the fallback donor for en, pl, ru and ar requests. French discriminates in the opposite direction from the Slavic donors: its one-rule is `i = 0,1`, so 0 selects ONE (where pl and ru say MANY, ar says ZERO and en says OTHER) and the decimal 1.5 also selects ONE because the rule tests i and ignores v. Its many-rule fires only at integer multiples of a million (or a compact exponent outside 0..5), which no other non-Portuguese locale here shares.
