evaluation-locale-fallback-pl.description: Polish is the fallback donor for en, ru, ar, fr and pt requests. Polish is the sharpest donor against Russian: verified against GeneratedCldrPluralData, the two rule sets agree at every integer except where i%10 = 1 and i != 1 and i%100 != 11 (21, 31, ..., 101, 1001), where pl says MANY and ru says ONE. Six loaded locales, six distinct primary language codes, so tiebreakers are null.

evaluation-locale-fallback-pt.description: NEW IN THIS REVIEW. Portuguese as a donor for requesters OUTSIDE its own language, which the pt-pair fixture cannot provide because both of its Portuguese donors serve Portuguese requesters. Loaded: pt (donor), en, ru, ar. French is deliberately NOT loaded here: verified against GeneratedCldrPluralData, fr and pt have equivalent cardinal rule sets ('i = 0,1' versus 'i = 0..1' are the same predicate, and their many-rules are the identical string), so no count could discriminate an fr requester from a pt donor and such a case would be pure decoration. Four loaded locales, four distinct primary language codes, so tiebreakers are null.

evaluation-locale-fallback-pt-pt.description: NEW IN THIS REVIEW. pt-PT as a donor for requesters outside its own language -- the last unexercised role in the clause's seven-locale list. pt-PT's cardinal rule set is one:'i = 1 and v = 0' (identical to English), many:'e = 0 and i != 0 and i%1000000 = 0 and v = 0 or e != 0..5', other:everything else. So it is discriminated from en only at a millions count, and from fr/ru/ar at 0. Only pt-PT is loaded for the 'pt' language code, so DefaultStrings installs it as its own identity tiebreaker and no explicit tiebreakers entry is required; five loaded locales, five distinct primary language codes.

evaluation-locale-fallback-ru.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 'fallback entries evaluated under the supplying locale': a Russian catalog is the fallback donor for en, pl, fr and ar requests. Only `ru` carries Items.Fallback / Rank.Fallback / Actor.Fallback / Basket.Alt, so DefaultStrings.getResult (DefaultStrings.java:712) hands `candidateLocale` = ru down to getInternal, which threads it into cardinalityForValue, ordinalityForValue, alternativeMatches and shouldApplyBidiIsolation. Every non-donor catalog also carries Items.Own so the SAME count can be observed resolving locally versus through the donor. instanceLocale is deliberately fr (a loaded, third locale) so that a port which leaks the ambient locale into evaluation is caught separately from one which uses the requested locale. Tiebreakers are null: five loaded locales, five distinct primary language codes.

Actor.Fallback.commentary: Gender selection in DefaultStrings is a direct map lookup on the caller's Gender value; no locale is consulted. This entry pins that a fallback cannot change it.

Basket.Alt.commentary: Whole-message alternatives comparing a number against a cardinality constant. ExpressionEvaluator.cardinalityFromOperand classifies itemCount under the locale it is handed, which getInternal receives as candidateLocale.

Items.Fallback.commentary: All six cardinality branches carry self-identifying text so the emitted translation names the category that was actually selected; no case in this family has to depend on a throw to discriminate. Russian's own CLDR set is one/few/many/other, but LocalizedStringValidator does not require a catalog's declared branches to match its locale's category set (only a LocalizedStringWarning.Type.INCOMPLETE_CARDINALITY_TRANSLATIONS warning exists, and the oracle loads with LocalizedStringWarningHandler.ignore()).

Rank.Fallback.commentary: GeneratedCldrPluralData gives ru exactly one ORDINAL rule ('other'), so only ORDINALITY_OTHER is declared. Under English ordinal rules 1/2/3 select ONE/TWO/FEW, which have no branch here, so wrong-locale evaluation fails loudly.

evaluation-locale-pt-pair.description: The pt / pt-PT half of the clause. GeneratedCldrPluralData keeps pt and pt-PT as distinct cardinal rule sets: pt's one-rule is `i = 0..1` while pt-PT's is `i = 1 and v = 0`, so the two disagree at 0 (pt ONE, pt-PT OTHER) and at 1.5 (pt ONE, pt-PT OTHER) and nowhere else. Three keys route three different donors: Boxes.PtOnly makes pt the donor for a pt-PT request through the CLDR parent chain, Boxes.PtPtOnly makes pt-PT reachable for a bare pt request through the tiebreaker limb of localeFallbackCandidates, and Boxes.EnOnly makes the fallback locale en the donor for both. Tiebreakers are MANDATORY here because pt and pt-PT share the primary language code 'pt', and DefaultStrings requires the list to be an exact permutation of the loaded pt-language locales; 'pt' is listed first so a bare pt request still selects pt itself.

Boxes.EnOnly.commentary: Only the two categories English has, so a port that evaluated this donor entry under pt or pt-PT rules would select MANY at 1000000 and find no branch.

evaluation-locale-uncatalogued-request.description: Separates 'the requested locale has a catalog but not this key' from 'the requested locale has no catalog at all'. Only pl and en are loaded; ru and ar are requested and never loaded, so localeFallbackCandidates yields a candidate whose localizedStrings map is null and the Polish fallback locale supplies. The distinction matters because an implementation could plausibly consult the donor's rules only when it had a catalog to skip, and default to the requested locale otherwise. Verified against the oracle: attemptedLocales is ['ru','pl'] / ['ar','pl'] and resolvedLocale is pl.

expressions-operand-typing.description: Serves the plan v7 section 8.3 expression clause for missing/null/cross-axis operands, raw-string non-equality (both '==' and '!='), and runtime operand typing. Deliberately generic keys and variable names ('value', 'left', 'right') so one compiled expression can be driven with many runtime operand types -- integer, decimal, plural operands, raw CharSequence, JSON boolean, and each language-form axis -- entirely from the case file. Static operand typing is NOT exercised here because lokalized-java rejects it at load/construction time (verified; see the skipped list); canBeEqualExpressionValue treats every VARIABLE as UNKNOWN_VARIABLE, which is compatible with everything, and that deferral is precisely what makes these runtime cases authorable while their bare-constant twins are not. Only 'en' is loaded, so tiebreakers is null.

Expr.Operand.LeftNotEqualsRight.commentary: The non-equality operator, so a port cannot pass the raw-string rule by special-casing '==' alone.

Expr.Operand.ValueVsPhoneticConstant.commentary: Bounds the 'a caller string is PHONETIC' rule: an explicit Phonetic value compares without a resolver, a raw string does not.

expressions-owed-axes.description: M3b owed-case catalog for ExpressionEvaluator. One key per expression SHAPE, deliberately generic ('value', 'left', 'right', 'count') so a single compiled expression can be driven with every runtime operand type from the case file. Covers the four axes no corpus expression ever mentioned (definiteness, classifier, clusivity, animacy), '!=' on every language-form axis, '<=' (which appeared in no expression at all), constant-on-the-left equality, and the constant-pair forms that are the only things able to execute canBeEqualExpressionValue's same-type and NUMBER/CARDINALITY-NUMBER/ORDINALITY rules. 'ja' carries only the constant-pair numeric keys, so the LOCALE-driven classification of a numeric LITERAL is pinned against 'en' (1 is 'one' in en and 'other' in ja).

expressions-owed-loader-ceilings.description: The LOADER's expression ceilings pinned from below. LocalizedStringLoader validates every alternative expression through an evaluator built with TranslationRuntimeLimits.hardCeilings() (4096 characters / 512 tokens / depth 64), NOT with the library defaults (2048 / 256 / 32), because an application's runtime policy is not available at load time; the configured limits are applied later, at Strings construction. Each file here carries an expression strictly between the default and the ceiling on exactly one axis, so it must LOAD. loadOnly because a DefaultStrings over these catalogs would refuse them at construction under the default limits -- which is precisely the distinction being pinned.

expressions-owed-plural-operand-limits.description: maximumCompactExponent and maximumVisibleDecimalPlaces lowered so ExpressionEvaluator.validatePluralOperands -- the evaluator's OWN copy of the plural-operand ceiling check, distinct from the placeholder-boundary one -- can be driven at its limit and one unit over it, on an expression operand. The corpus reaches this method only from the plural-form path, so a port enforcing these ceilings at the placeholder boundary and not on an expression operand passes everything today.

expressions-owed-static-rejections.description: Deliberately unloadable catalogs, one locale file per statically-rejected expression, so each load-time diagnostic is observed on its own rather than aborting a shared run. Covers the checks the corpus reached but never made FIRE: the boolean-operand rule for '&&' (both orientations -- the JavaScript-truthiness trap), the chained-comparison rule with the boolean on the RIGHT, the ordering-operator numeric rule in both orientations, canBeEqualExpressionValue's refusal, '<=' proven to be an ordering operator at validation, the two constant pairs that must be refused so the NUMBER/CARDINALITY allowance is not read as 'anything goes', an expression that ends on a bare operand, and the three expression size ceilings breached by exactly one unit. The size cases are measured against TranslationRuntimeLimits.hardCeilings(), which is what LocalizedStringLoader validates with; the last file is a control that loads.

expressions-precedence.description: Serves the plan v7 section 8.3 expression clause for operator precedence, parenthesized override, short-circuit evaluation, and the two behaviors that surround an expression: what a throwing expression does to the alternative scan, and that the SECOND expression site (generated-placeholder fragment expressions, compiled by DefaultStrings.compileExpressions and evaluated by resolveExpressionTranslation) obeys the same rules. Every expression here is statically valid so the fixture constructs -- lokalized-java validates alternative expressions three times before any case runs (LocalizedStringLoader at load, LocalizedStringValidator via DefaultStrings.validateLocalizedString, and ExpressionEvaluator.compile in the constructor), and a single invalid expression aborts the whole corpus run, so discrimination has to come from which branch's translation is emitted and from whether an unbound right-hand operand is ever reached. Each key's default translation is the literal string 'no alternative' so a non-match is distinguishable from a match and from a resolution failure. Only 'en' is loaded, so there is no same-language ambiguity and tiebreakers is null.

Expr.Alternative.EarlierAlternativeFailu.commentary: Alternative 0 can never be evaluated; alternative 1 would match. A throw in an earlier alternative must abort the key rather than fall through.

Expr.Alternative.LaterAlternativeIsReach.commentary: Control shape for the abort key: both alternatives are always evaluable, so array order and fall-through are observable on their own.

Expr.Fragment.OrShortCircuitsAbsentOpera.commentary: Short-circuiting at the fragment expression site.

Expr.Fragment.PrecedenceAndBindsTighterT.commentary: Second expression site: a generated-placeholder fragment expression, compiled and evaluated by resolveExpressionTranslation rather than alternativeMatches.

Expr.Precedence.AndBindsTighterThanOr.commentary: Correct parse is alpha || (beta && gamma). A parse of (alpha || beta) && gamma emits 'no alternative' for the same inputs.

Expr.Precedence.AndBranchShortCircuitsBe.commentary: (alpha && absentRight) || beta. The and-branch must short-circuit to false and the or-branch must still be evaluated.

Expr.Precedence.OrShortCircuitsAndBranch.commentary: alpha || (absentLeft && absentRight). Neither absent placeholder may be touched when alpha matches.

Expr.Precedence.ParenthesesOverrideAndBi.commentary: Same operands as Expr.Precedence.AndBindsTighterThanOr, parenthesized the other way, so the same tuple must invert.

Expr.ShortCircuit.LeftOperandAlwaysEvalu.commentary: The left operand is unconditionally evaluated even when the right operand alone would settle the result.

Expr.ShortCircuit.OrSkipsIllTypedRight.commentary: The skipped right operand fails on operand TYPE rather than on a missing binding.

expressions-review-static-axis-types.description: Adversarial-review addendum to expressions-owed. The M3b owed cases closed expressionValueTypeForToken's per-axis arms (ExpressionEvaluator:1893/1895/1897/1901/1903) by putting a CASE_*, DEFINITENESS_*, CLASSIFIER_*, CLUSIVITY_* and ANIMACY_* literal into an expression for the first time -- but every one of those expressions is 'variable == CONSTANT', whose static validation succeeds whatever type the constant is given, because canBeEqualExpressionValue returns true the moment either side is UNKNOWN_VARIABLE. A port that typed those constants as UNKNOWN_VARIABLE at load would execute the same arm and produce byte-identical output on every corpus case. These files put each constant where its STATIC type decides load success: paired with a NUMBER under an operator that refuses the pairing, so the diagnostic names the type. FORMALITY, ORDINALITY and PHONETIC are included on the same argument even though their arms were already covered. loadOnly because every file here is meant to fail at load.

failure-handler-final-reason-precedence.description: Serves final-failure precedence from the same 8.3 bullet as callback exceptions. Three keys arrange the three reasons in different orders across a two-locale chain: Mixed.NoMatchThenFailure misses its alternatives in Russian and then raises in English; Mixed.FailureThenNoMatch raises in Russian and then misses in English; Mixed.MissingThenNoMatch is absent from Russian and misses in English. DefaultStrings.java:742-746 computes the reported reason from firstFallbackFailure and the sticky noMatchingAlternativeEncountered flag rather than from the last attempt, so a port that reports the last -- or the first -- attempt's reason diverges on at least one of these. Two loaded locales with distinct primary languages, so tiebreakers are null.

Mixed.FailureThenNoMatch.commentary: Alternatives-only miss, reached only when the policy keeps walking past the Russian raise.

Mixed.MissingThenNoMatch.commentary: Absent from Russian entirely, so the chain is MISSING_TRANSLATION then NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE.

Mixed.NoMatchThenFailure.commentary: Only ONE is translated, so an English OTHER count (2) raises here.

Mixed.FailureThenNoMatch.commentary: Only ONE is translated, so a Russian FEW count (2) raises here.

Mixed.NoMatchThenFailure.commentary: Alternatives-only, and the predicate is false for the counts the cases pass.

failure-handler-instance-return-string.description: Identical catalog again, with an instance handler returning TranslationFailureResponse.returnString. The configured text deliberately contains a placeholder token and is longer than the key, so a port that interpolates or truncates the handler's own string is caught: DefaultStrings.java:758-760 puts that string on the TranslationResult verbatim and never routes it through interpolateFailureKey.

failure-handler-instance-throws.description: Identical catalog to failure-handler-missing-template-key with exactly one difference: the INSTANCE failure handler is TranslationFailureHandler.throwException(). Serves 'callback exceptions' by pinning where the throw surfaces (DefaultStrings.java:761-763 puts the THROW_EXCEPTION arm inside getResult, and get() is only getResult(...).getTranslation() at DefaultStrings.java:643), and pairs with per-call overrides that must replace it wholesale rather than compose with it.

failure-handler-instance-throws-in-handl.description: Identical catalog, with an instance handler whose own body raises before returning a response. This is section 8.3's 'callback exceptions' in its literal form: the exception escapes from inside translationFailureHandler.handle at DefaultStrings.java:749-750, before any TranslationFailureResponse action is inspected, so neither the returned-key nor the returned-string arm can run. The oracle's throw-in-handler behavior raises an IllegalStateException carrying the configured message.

failure-handler-key-interpolation-limit.description: Serves 'failure-key fail-soft behavior' directly. maximumInterpolatedOutputCharacters is lowered to 12; TranslationRuntimeLimits documents its range as 1 through MAXIMUM_INTERPOLATED_OUTPUT_CHARACTERS = 1048576 (1024*1024), so 12 is legal and well under the hard ceiling. Twelve puts the failure-key interpolation of 'Hi {{name}}' exactly on the boundary: the literal prefix 'Hi ' costs 3, so StringInterpolator.appendChecked admits a 9-character replacement (9 > 12-3 is false) and refuses a 10-character one. Bidi isolation is charged against the same budget -- interpolateFailureKey passes the same limit into BidiUtils.isolatedValue at DefaultStrings.java:1405-1408, and BoundedIsolatedValue.render adds FSI and PDI inside it -- so the isolation option alone can flip the outcome. interpolateFailureKey swallows any RuntimeException and returns the raw key (DefaultStrings.java:1414-1416). The catalog holds no resolvable key beyond a marker, so nothing else can consume the tiny budget. One loaded locale, so tiebreakers are null.

failure-handler-missing-template-key.description: Serves section 8.3's 'missing keys containing placeholders and failure-key fail-soft behavior' and the handler half of 'callback exceptions'. Every library option is left at its default (DefaultStrings.java:472-477: returnKey handler, MISSING_OR_NO_MATCH policy, RTL_LOCALES bidi -- DEFAULT_BIDI_ISOLATION at DefaultStrings.java:80), so each case's per-call translationFailureHandler is the only variable and DefaultStrings.java:684 (per-call REPLACES instance) is exercised against a known baseline. The catalog deliberately contains exactly one resolvable key, Greeting.Present, so a control case can show the handler is consulted only on failure; every key the failure cases look up is absent from every loaded locale, which forces MISSING_TRANSLATION with no cause. One loaded locale, so tiebreakers are null.

failure-handler-multi-locale-chain.description: Serves the attempted-locale and placeholder-map halves of what TranslationFailure exposes. The instance ambient locale (es) differs from the fallback locale (en) and from the requested locale (es-MX), so lookupLocale, the ambient default, and the fallback are three distinct tags and a port that conflates any two is caught. A request for the unloaded es-MX walks its CLDR parent chain before the fallback (CldrLocaleData.fallbackLocalesFor plus the fallback locale, DefaultStrings.java:2475-2503), giving an attempted-locale list of more than one entry; every candidate is appended at DefaultStrings.java:702 BEFORE it is attempted, so unloaded candidates appear too. The exact length is the oracle's to record -- the cases assert only that it is longer than the never-policy sibling's. Two loaded locales with distinct primary languages, so tiebreakers are null.

failure-handler-no-matching-alternative.description: Serves the NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE reason, which the clause needs in order to tell the two causeless reasons apart from the one that carries a cause. Both entries are alternatives-only roots with no default translation, which LocalizedStringLoader permits when at least one alternative is present (the shape the existing gender-multi-axis-alternatives-only fixture already proves loadable), so a miss returns Optional.empty from getInternal and DefaultStrings.java:719-720 records NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE with no throwable. The second entry's KEY is itself a placeholder template and is PRESENT in the catalog, so the returned-key path can be observed under a reason other than MISSING_TRANSLATION. One loaded locale, so tiebreakers are null.

Guest.Welcome.commentary: Alternatives-only root: a masculine guest matches nothing and there is no default translation.

Hello {{name}}.commentary: A key that is itself a template AND exists in the catalog, so a miss is NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE rather than MISSING_TRANSLATION while the returned key still interpolates.

fallback-policy-precedence-chain.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 'final failure precedence'. A three-catalog chain (de-AT, de, en with fallback en) requested at de-AT, built so DIFFERENT candidates fail for DIFFERENT reasons inside one walk. DefaultStrings.java:742-746 computes the final reason by precedence, not by recency: firstFallbackFailure != null wins as RESOLUTION_FAILURE, else the sticky noMatchingAlternativeEncountered flag wins as NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE, else MISSING_TRANSLATION -- and firstFallbackFailure is assigned only while still null, so it retains the FIRST resolution failure's throwable, never the last. Precedence.FirstCauseRetention deliberately makes de throw IllegalStateException ('Missing Gender translation for NEUTER') and en throw IllegalArgumentException ('Missing value for placeholder absentCount'), verified by resolving each locale directly, so first-versus-last cause retention is observable. Precedence.HaltsMidChain gives the three policies three different attempted-locale lengths AND three different reported reasons from one key. Two loaded locales share the primary language de, so tiebreakers is mandatory and lists the exact permutation {de-AT, de}.

gender-multi-axis-alternatives-only.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 'alternatives-only children that hit and miss'. Each definition contains an alternative that supplies ONLY a nested alternatives list and no translation of its own, selected on gender (LocalizedStringLoader permits translation==null when at least one alternative is present). Delivery.Status deliberately places a LATER sibling alternative (packageCount == 0) that matches the very same context the nested children miss on, and gives the root its own translation, so a miss inside the selected child can be told apart from fall-through to a later sibling AND from falling back to the root translation -- the two ways a port can get DefaultStrings.java:806-810 wrong. The root translation deliberately references no placeholder, so the root path cannot fail for an unrelated reason. Guest.Welcome repeats the shape with a root that has no translation at all. Tiebreakers are null: only 'en' is loaded.

gender-multi-axis-gender.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 'multi-axis language-form dispatch': two axes selected independently inside ONE definition, from two different caller values. Actor.Bio is single-axis gender with two placeholders reading one value; 'Bio for {{actorGender}}' repeats the gender selector under a key that EMBEDS the selector name, so the RETURNED_KEY translation a resolution failure produces is interpolated from the caller context and therefore differs per failure mode (DefaultStrings.interpolateFailureKey, DefaultStrings.java:1391) instead of collapsing to one indistinguishable token. Books.Read pairs gender with cardinality and is loaded in Polish as well, so the cardinality half runs under a four-form plural rule set while the gender half stays constant. Race.Result pairs the two NUMERIC axes (ordinality and cardinality) in one definition, which is where a port that shares one classification step between axes diverges. Award.Announcement's alternatives select on gender while its inherited placeholders select on cardinality. Tiebreakers are null: 'en' and 'pl' share no primary language code, so no tiebreaker list is required or permitted.

Actor.Bio.commentary: Two independent gender placeholders read the same caller value.

Award.Announcement.commentary: Alternatives select on gender; placeholders select on cardinality. The 'winner' map deliberately omits GENDER_NEUTER, which is unreachable because the NEUTER branch's translation does not reference {{winner}} -- only placeholders REFERENCED by the selected translation are resolved.

Bio for {{actorGender}}.commentary: The key deliberately references the selector value. On a resolution failure DefaultStrings returns the key INTERPOLATED with the caller context, so each failure mode renders a different translation: a tagged Gender renders its enum name, a raw string renders itself, and an absent or null value leaves '{{actorGender}}' literal. Without that, every failure in this family would observe the same RETURNED_KEY / RESOLUTION_FAILURE token.

Race.Result.commentary: The two numeric axes in one definition. Ordinality and cardinality are the only axes that accept a bare number, so they are the pair a port is most likely to route through one shared classification step.

gender-multi-axis-nominal-axes.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 multi-axis dispatch for the axes that have NO numeric fallback: grammatical-case, definiteness, classifier, formality, clusivity, animacy and phonetic each get a dispatching definition, so every one of the ten arms of the language-form branch in DefaultStrings.getInternal is exercised by some case in this family. Invitation.Message dispatches on three axes at once (formality, gender, cardinality). Arrival.Announcement's alternatives select on formality while its inherited placeholders select on definiteness and animacy. Section 3.7 says these selectors REQUIRE the expected tagged axis, so the fixture also carries the maps a wrong-axis, raw-string, or numeric value is fed into; each rejection uses a DIFFERENT key so the RETURNED_KEY translations stay distinguishable. The classifier map deliberately omits CLASSIFIER_PERSON so the absent-form path is reachable. Only the tagged-Phonetic input path is used: a CharSequence phonetic input would route through PhoneticResolver, which is outside the oracle's scope. Tiebreakers are null: only 'en' is loaded.

Arrival.Announcement.commentary: Alternatives select on formality; the inherited placeholders select on definiteness and animacy.

Article.Choice.commentary: The tenth axis. A tagged Phonetic dispatches directly without consulting any PhoneticResolver (DefaultStrings.java:1159), so this arm is reachable inside the oracle's current scope; the CharSequence input path is not.

Invitation.Message.commentary: Formality, gender, and cardinality dispatch independently in one definition.

generated-placeholders-cycles.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 generated-placeholder clause: cycles among generated placeholder definitions. Covers a self-reference, a minimal two-node ring, a cycle that exists only under a branch's replacement, a cycle that exists only in a fragment's unselected default text, and a shared diamond that must be memoized rather than misreported as a cycle. The last two conditional keys are what force detection to run against the effective post-inheritance bindings and against the text actually selected, rather than against the catalog as written.

generated-placeholders-depth-limit.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 generated-placeholder clause: the generated-placeholder nesting limit at its default of 32. Entering placeholder p_k's template happens at recursion depth k and DefaultStrings.interpolateTemplate throws when depth > 32, so a 32-link chain sits exactly on the boundary and a 33-link chain is one past it.

generated-placeholders-expansion-limit.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 generated-placeholder clause: the cumulative generated-expansion character budget at its default of 1,048,576. Six independent doubling chains of 18 levels each; every distinct placeholder is expanded and billed exactly once (StringInterpolator.placeholderNamesIn returns a set, and interpolateTemplate memoizes by name), so chain level j costs 2^(18-j) characters, one chain costs 262,143 and six cost 1,572,858, while the largest single expansion is 131,072 — half the 262,144-character interpolated-output cap. The cumulative budget is therefore what stops the render, and it trips inside the fifth chain.

generated-placeholders-inheritance.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 generated-placeholder clause: one English catalog whose keys exercise branch inheritance of a parent placeholder definition, whole-definition replacement inside a branch, replacement that changes the placeholder KIND in both directions, and three-level inheritance where the nearest ancestor's definition wins. The 'Partial replacement' key, whose branch table omits a form the parent supplies, is what pins that the replacement is whole-definition rather than a per-form merge.

generated-placeholders-late-binding.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 generated-placeholder clause: dependencies discovered only after another placeholder resolves. A generated fragment's selected text and a language form's selected text are both rescanned for further generated placeholders, so only the branch that was actually chosen pulls its dependency into resolution.

generated-placeholders-scope.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 generated-placeholder clause: the scope in which raw caller input is visible. Language-form selectors, range endpoints, and generated-fragment alternative expressions read only the caller's placeholder map, never the values other generated placeholders produced, while interpolation of a file-defined name prefers the generated value over a same-named raw input. Every generated value is deliberately chosen to differ from the raw value of the same name, and the sibling that a selector names is always referenced EARLIER in the template so it is genuinely resolved before the selector runs — otherwise a port reading the wrong scope would merely fail for the same reason Java does instead of rendering a visibly different string.

ingress-matrix-bidi-always.description: Bidi ingress matrix, instance leg pinned to ALWAYS. Same catalog as ingress-matrix-bidi-default. ALWAYS differs from both NONE and the RTL_LOCALES default precisely at an LTR request, so every case on this fixture probes en.

ingress-matrix-bidi-default.description: Bidi ingress matrix, instance leg UNSET so the library default applies (DefaultStrings.java:80 sets DEFAULT_BIDI_ISOLATION = RTL_LOCALES; :477 substitutes it when the builder was given null). One catalog carries Greeting.Named in both an LTR locale (en) and an RTL one (ar) so any of the three values can be separated from the other two by choosing the probe locale. 'Farewell.Named {{name}}' exists in no catalog, which routes the same option through interpolateFailureKey (:754/:1406) against the LOOKUP locale instead of interpolateTemplate (:1367) against the donor.

ingress-matrix-bidi-none.description: Bidi ingress matrix, instance leg pinned to NONE. Same catalog as ingress-matrix-bidi-default so the only difference between the two fixtures' results is the instance option itself. NONE differs from the RTL_LOCALES default precisely at an RTL request, so template cases here probe ar; the returned-key cases probe en, where NONE differs from ALWAYS.

ingress-matrix-bidi-rtl-locales.description: Bidi ingress matrix, instance leg pinned EXPLICITLY to RTL_LOCALES. Same catalog as ingress-matrix-bidi-default; the pair of fixtures exists so the corpus records that an explicitly configured RTL_LOCALES and an unset instance option are the same thing, which is only checkable by comparing two fixtures.

ingress-matrix-combined.description: All three options set at the instance to NON-default values simultaneously (ALWAYS, any-failure, throw), so each is individually observable and each is wrong if a port silently substitutes a default. instanceLocale is ru and fallbackLocale is en, giving a two-candidate walk. Three keys serve different purposes. 'Items.Sparse {{tag}}' under-declares Russian's categories so itemCount 5 fails at ru with RESOLUTION_FAILURE, and its en counterpart interpolates the caller-supplied tag so the bidi setting shows in a resolved translation. 'Sparse.RuOnly {{tag}}' fails the same way at ru but has NO en counterpart, so the walk ends in a failure whose attemptedLocales separates the inherited any-failure ([ru, en]) from the library default ([ru]) — without this key an inherited policy is invisible, because on a plain MISSING_TRANSLATION any-failure and the default behave identically. 'Absent.Named {{tag}}' is in no catalog at all, driving the options through interpolateFailureKey where isolation keys off the LOOKUP locale. Every key carries a placeholder so bidi stays observable even when the handler responds.

Items.Sparse {{tag}}.commentary: Only ONE and OTHER declared. itemCount 5 selects Russian MANY, which is missing, so getInternal throws and getResult classifies the attempt as RESOLUTION_FAILURE. An en counterpart exists, so a permissive policy resolves.

Sparse.RuOnly {{tag}}.commentary: Same sparse declaration, but deliberately ABSENT from en. A RESOLUTION_FAILURE at ru followed by a missing en entry is the only shape in which an inherited any-failure policy is observable through attemptedLocales while the handler still responds.

ingress-matrix-handler-default.description: Failure-handler ingress matrix, instance leg UNSET so the library default TranslationFailureHandler.returnKey() applies (DefaultStrings.java:472). Absent.Key is in no catalog, so every lookup of it reaches the handler. A single loaded locale means localeFallbackCandidates yields exactly one candidate, so the fallback policy is never consulted (:731) and the row is about which handler responds and nothing else.

ingress-matrix-handler-return-string.description: Failure-handler ingress matrix, instance leg pinned to a return-string handler with a distinctive payload. Identical catalog to ingress-matrix-handler-default. The payload text is what makes an instance-versus-per-call return-string pair discriminating even though both sides share a behavior name. Cases on this fixture use `get` wherever the responding handler returns a string, because DefaultStrings.java:758 sets TranslationResultStatus.RETURNED_STRING and the corpus schema's translationResult.status enum admits only TRANSLATED and RETURNED_KEY.

ingress-matrix-handler-throw.description: Failure-handler ingress matrix, instance leg pinned to throwException(). Identical catalog to ingress-matrix-handler-default. DefaultStrings.java:762 runs throwExceptionFor inside getResult itself, so this instance option makes getResult throw as well as get; both are exercised. The failure reason here is MISSING_TRANSLATION, so throwExceptionFor (:3196) takes its MissingTranslationException branch rather than rethrowing a cause.

ingress-matrix-handler-throw-in-handler.description: Failure-handler ingress matrix, instance leg pinned to a handler that throws from inside itself (section 8.3's 'callback exceptions'). Identical catalog to ingress-matrix-handler-default. The message is distinctive so a per-call handler of the SAME behavior with a DIFFERENT message still discriminates, and so a port that composed rather than replaced handlers would surface the wrong message.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-baseline.description: Legacy-alias arm. On disk are the MODERN catalogs he, id, ro, sr, fil and en, each translated as its own tag so the resolved catalog is readable off the translation. The four deprecated request spellings split into two groups: iw and in are rewritten by Locale.forLanguageTag itself, while mo, sh and tl survive as their own Locale values and can only reach a modern catalog through CLDR canonicalization inside the matcher. Six distinct primary language codes, so no tiebreakers. No ambient supplier.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-instance-in.description: Alias arm catalog with the deprecated spelling in as the INSTANCE locale.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-instance-iw.description: Alias arm catalog (he, id, ro, sr, fil, en; fallback en) with the deprecated spelling iw as the INSTANCE locale.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-instance-mo.description: Alias arm catalog with the deprecated spelling mo as the INSTANCE locale.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-instance-sh.description: Alias arm catalog with the deprecated spelling sh as the INSTANCE locale.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-instance-tl.description: Alias arm catalog with the deprecated spelling tl as the INSTANCE locale.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-locale-supplie.description: Alias arm catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning the deprecated spelling in.
Alias arm catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning the deprecated spelling iw.
Alias arm catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning the deprecated spelling mo, which Locale.forLanguageTag leaves untouched.
Alias arm catalog with a localeSupplier that negotiates the header 'iw' and collapses the answer to a bare Locale, erasing the iw/he expansion from the reported ranges.
Alias arm catalog with a localeSupplier that negotiates the header 'mo' and collapses the answer to a bare Locale, erasing the mo/ro expansion from the reported ranges.
Alias arm catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning the deprecated spelling sh.
Alias arm catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning the deprecated spelling tl, which Locale.forLanguageTag leaves untouched.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-match-supplier.description: Alias arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the deprecated spelling in through the single-locale kernel.
Alias arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the deprecated spelling iw through the single-locale kernel.
Alias arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the deprecated spelling mo through the single-locale kernel.
Alias arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the header 'in' through the whole-list solver (expansion in, id).

Alias arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the header 'iw' through the whole-list solver, so the IANA equivalence expansion (iw, he) happens inside the supplier and survives onto the result.
Alias arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the header 'mo' through the whole-list solver (expansion mo, ro).

Alias arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the header 'sh' through the whole-list solver. sh has NO entry in the pinned IANA equivalence table, so the expanded list stays a single range.

Alias arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the header 'tl' through the whole-list solver. tl has NO IANA equivalent, so the range list stays single — yet CLDR's own tl to fil alias still reaches the loaded catalog.
Alias arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating sh through the single-locale kernel. The match is NONE, so the lookup locale comes from the match's fallbackLocale.
Alias arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating tl through the single-locale kernel.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-mo-on-disk.description: The other half of the mo question: a FILE named mo. LocalizedStringLoader keys catalogs by Locale.forLanguageTag, which leaves mo as mo, so the catalog really is loaded under mo and no ro catalog exists. Mirror of ingress-matrix-java-alias-baseline, where ro is on disk and mo is only ever a request. One catalog per canonical language code, so no tiebreakers.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-mo-on-disk-loc.description: A file named mo reached through a constant localeSupplier spelled ro — the canonical tag asking for a catalog that exists only under its deprecated spelling.

ingress-matrix-java-alias-mo-on-disk-mat.description: A file named mo reached through the supplied-match ingress, negotiated from the deprecated spelling mo.

ingress-matrix-java-case-baseline.description: Case-spelling arm. Loaded zh, zh-Hant, en; tiebreaker zh:[zh, zh-Hant]. Unlike the zh-TW seed row EVERY catalog carries the key and each translation is its own tag, so the resolved locale and the translation together name which catalog served the request. No ambient supplier.

ingress-matrix-java-case-instance.description: Case arm with the mixed-case spelling ZH-hant as the INSTANCE locale.

ingress-matrix-java-case-locale-supplier.description: Case arm with ZH-hant returned by a constant localeSupplier. Locale.forLanguageTag normalizes case before the library sees it, so this must agree with the canonical spelling; a port comparing tags case-sensitively misses here.
Case arm with ZH-hant negotiated inside a localeSupplier and collapsed to a bare Locale.

ingress-matrix-java-case-match-supplier.description: Case arm with ZH-hant through the supplied-match ingress, single-locale kernel.

ingress-matrix-java-case-match-supplier-.description: Case arm with ZH-hant through the supplied-match ingress, whole-list solver. zh-hant has no IANA equivalent, so the expanded list stays a single range — the negative control for the alias and extlang arms.

ingress-matrix-java-en-au-baseline.description: Seed row 3 catalog (loaded en-001, en; tiebreaker en:[en, en-001]; fallback and instance locale en). No ambient supplier. MEASURED per-call locale en-AU: CLDR_FALLBACK/en-001, lookupLocale en-AU, attempted [en-AU, en-001].

ingress-matrix-java-en-au-instance.description: Seed row 3 catalog with the request tag en-AU as the INSTANCE locale (realized as a constant localeSupplier, as in every -instance fixture here).

ingress-matrix-java-en-au-locale-supplie.description: Seed row 3 catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning en-AU: the derived-match route, lookup locale en-AU.
Seed row 3 catalog with a localeSupplier that negotiates 'en-AU' and collapses to the bare Locale en-001, whose re-derived match is EXACT rather than the CLDR_FALLBACK the negotiation produced.

ingress-matrix-java-en-au-match-supplier.description: Seed row 3 catalog with a localeMatchSupplier returning matchFor(Locale en-AU); lookup starts at the selection en-001.
Seed row 3 catalog, supplied match from the whole-list solver on header 'en-AU'.

ingress-matrix-java-en-us-baseline.description: Seed row 5 catalog (a lone loaded en; fallback and instance locale en). No ambient supplier. MEASURED per-call locale en-US: CLDR_FALLBACK/en, lookupLocale en-US, attempted [en-US, en], isFallback true.

ingress-matrix-java-en-us-case-instance.description: Seed row 5's lone loaded en with the mixed-case spelling EN-us as the instance locale.

ingress-matrix-java-en-us-case-locale-su.description: Seed row 5's lone loaded en with EN-us returned by a constant localeSupplier.

ingress-matrix-java-en-us-case-match-sup.description: Seed row 5's lone loaded en with EN-us through the supplied-match ingress. The supplied match's locale is en, so the lookup collapses to en and the en-US candidate never appears in the attempted chain.

ingress-matrix-java-en-us-instance.description: Seed row 5 catalog with the request tag en-US as the INSTANCE locale (realized as a constant localeSupplier).

ingress-matrix-java-en-us-locale-supplie.description: Seed row 5 catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning en-US: derived match, lookup locale en-US.

Seed row 5 catalog with a localeSupplier that negotiates 'en-US' and collapses to the bare Locale en. The re-derived match is EXACT/en and isFallback goes FALSE, while the match supplier on the same header preserves CLDR_FALLBACK/en and isFallback TRUE — the same selection reported two ways.

ingress-matrix-java-en-us-match-supplier.description: Seed row 5 catalog with a localeMatchSupplier returning matchFor(Locale en-US); lookup starts at the selection en, so the en-US step disappears from the chain.
Seed row 5 catalog, supplied match from the whole-list solver on header 'en-US'.

ingress-matrix-java-extlang-baseline.description: Extlang arm. Loaded zh, cmn, yue and en, each translated as its own tag. cmn canonicalizes to zh, so zh and cmn share a canonical language code and tiebreakers are MANDATORY and must be the exact permutation [zh, cmn]. The two per-call routes diverge sharply: Locale.forLanguageTag promotes the extlang, so zh-cmn becomes the Locale cmn, while LanguageRange.parse('zh-cmn') keeps zh-cmn and adds zh-guoyu and cmn. No ambient supplier.

ingress-matrix-java-extlang-instance-sgn.description: Extlang arm catalog with the grandfathered spelling sgn-BE-FR as the INSTANCE locale.

ingress-matrix-java-extlang-instance-zh-.description: Extlang arm catalog (zh, cmn, yue, en; tiebreaker zh:[zh, cmn]) with the extlang spelling zh-cmn as the INSTANCE locale.
Extlang arm catalog with the extlang spelling zh-yue as the INSTANCE locale.

ingress-matrix-java-extlang-locale-suppl.description: Extlang arm catalog with a localeSupplier that negotiates the header 'zh-cmn' and collapses the answer to a bare Locale, erasing the three-range expansion and the CANONICAL diagnostic.
Extlang arm catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning the grandfathered spelling sgn-BE-FR, which Locale.forLanguageTag collapses to sfb.
Extlang arm catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning the extlang spelling zh-cmn.
Extlang arm catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning the extlang spelling zh-yue.

ingress-matrix-java-extlang-match-suppli.description: Extlang arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the header 'sgn-BE-FR' through the whole-list solver (expansion sgn-be-fr, sgn-sfb, sfb, sgn-be-fx); still NONE, but with four ranges on record.
Extlang arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the header 'zh-cmn' through the whole-list solver, which keeps the literal range and reaches a DIFFERENT catalog than the kernel does.
Extlang arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the header 'zh-yue' through the whole-list solver (expansion zh-yue, yue).
Extlang arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating sgn-BE-FR through the single-locale kernel; the match is NONE.
Extlang arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating zh-cmn through the single-locale kernel, which sees the PROMOTED Locale cmn.
Extlang arm catalog with a localeMatchSupplier negotiating zh-yue through the single-locale kernel.

ingress-matrix-java-extlang-no-cmn-basel.description: The extlang question with the promoted target REMOVED: only zh and en are loaded, so a zh-cmn request cannot succeed by promotion. The per-call-locale route promotes to the unloaded cmn; the header route still carries the literal range zh-cmn. No tiebreakers (one catalog per canonical language).

ingress-matrix-java-extlang-no-cmn-local.description: The zh-only catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning the extlang spelling zh-cmn, which Locale.forLanguageTag promotes to the unloaded cmn.

ingress-matrix-java-extlang-no-cmn-match.description: The zh-only catalog reached through a localeMatchSupplier negotiating the header 'zh-cmn', so the whole-list solver runs in the ambient ingress instead of per call.

ingress-matrix-java-fr-be-baseline.description: Seed row 2 catalog (loaded fr-FR, fr-CA; tiebreaker fr:[fr-FR, fr-CA]; fallback and instance locale fr-FR). No ambient supplier. MEASURED per-call locale fr-BE: LIKELY_SUBTAG/fr-FR, lookupLocale fr-BE, attempted [fr-BE, fr, fr-FR].

ingress-matrix-java-fr-be-instance.description: Seed row 2 catalog with the request tag fr-BE as the INSTANCE locale. As with every -instance fixture here, the harness realizes an instance locale as a constant localeSupplier, so this and ingress-matrix-java-fr-be-locale-supplier-constant drive the same DefaultStrings branch; the pair records that equivalence rather than testing a distinct Java code path.

ingress-matrix-java-fr-be-locale-supplie.description: Seed row 2 catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning fr-BE. The derived-match route: the lookup locale stays fr-BE (DefaultStrings.java:2456-2458).

Seed row 2 catalog with a localeSupplier that negotiates 'fr-BE' and collapses the answer to the bare Locale fr-FR. DefaultStrings re-derives the match from that Locale, so the LIKELY_SUBTAG diagnostic the negotiation actually produced is replaced by EXACT/fr-FR — the observable cost of the collapse.

ingress-matrix-java-fr-be-match-supplier.description: Seed row 2 catalog with a localeMatchSupplier returning matchFor(Locale fr-BE). The lookup locale comes from the match (fr-FR), so the attempted chain loses fr-BE and fr.
Seed row 2 catalog, supplied match from the whole-list solver on header 'fr-BE'.

ingress-matrix-java-und-latn-baseline.description: Seed row 1 catalog (loaded en, fr; fallback and instance locale fr). NO ambient supplier, so only a per-call locale or a per-call language-range list can move the lookup off fr. MEASURED per-call locale und-Latn: match NONE, lookupLocale und-Latn, attempted [und-Latn, und, fr], resolved fr.

ingress-matrix-java-und-latn-instance.description: Seed row 1 catalog with the request tag und-Latn as the INSTANCE locale and no per-call locale. Note for porters: DefaultStrings has no separate instance-locale slot — the harness installs a constant localeSupplier for instanceLocale, so this fixture and ingress-matrix-java-und-latn-locale-supplier-constant drive the SAME branch (DefaultStrings.java:2456-2458). The pair records that equivalence for a port that does model an instance locale separately.

ingress-matrix-java-und-latn-locale-supp.description: Seed row 1 catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning und-Latn. localeLookupFor DERIVES the match with matchFor(suppliedLocale) and keeps the SUPPLIED tag as the lookup locale (DefaultStrings.java:2456-2458), so this must agree with the per-call-locale route on every channel except the supplierCalls record.

Seed row 1 catalog with a localeSupplier that negotiates the header 'und-Latn' and hands back a bare Locale — the winning locale, or the fallback locale when nothing matches, which is what happens here (und-Latn matches nothing, so the supplier returns fr). DefaultStrings then RE-DERIVES a match from that Locale, so the lossy collapse is observable: EXACT/fr instead of the NONE every other route in this row reports.

ingress-matrix-java-und-latn-match-suppl.description: Seed row 1 catalog with a localeMatchSupplier returning matchFor(Locale und-Latn). localeLookupFor takes the lookup locale from the MATCH — its locale, or the match's own fallbackLocale when the match is NONE (DefaultStrings.java:2449-2453) — so resolution starts at fr rather than at und-Latn. This is the 'intentional lookup difference for supplied matches' half of the clause.

Seed row 1 catalog, supplied match produced by the whole-list solver on the header 'und-Latn'. Paired with ingress-matrix-java-und-latn-match-supplier-locale to show the two solvers agree here, and with the baseline to show a supplied match does not agree with a per-call locale.

ingress-matrix-java-zh-tw-baseline.description: Seed row 4 catalog (loaded zh, zh-Hant, en; tiebreaker zh:[zh, zh-Hant]; fallback and instance locale en). zh carries Checkout.Title, zh-Hant carries ONLY Unrelated.Key, so the two keys expose the resolution chain at different depths. No ambient supplier. MEASURED per-call locale zh-TW on Checkout.Title: LIKELY_SUBTAG/zh-Hant, lookupLocale zh-TW, attempted [zh-TW, zh-Hant, en], resolved en.

ingress-matrix-java-zh-tw-instance.description: Seed row 4 catalog with the request tag zh-TW as the INSTANCE locale (realized as a constant localeSupplier).

ingress-matrix-java-zh-tw-locale-supplie.description: Seed row 4 catalog with a constant localeSupplier returning zh-TW: derived match, lookup locale zh-TW.

Seed row 4 catalog with a localeSupplier that negotiates 'zh-TW' and collapses to the bare Locale zh-Hant. The re-derived match is EXACT/zh-Hant with range zh-hant, where the match supplier on the identical header preserves LIKELY_SUBTAG/zh-Hant with range zh-tw: same ingress family, same selection, different reported match.

ingress-matrix-java-zh-tw-match-supplier.description: Seed row 4 catalog with a localeMatchSupplier returning matchFor(Locale zh-TW). The lookup locale is the selection zh-Hant, so the chain loses the zh-TW step the per-call-locale route walks.
Seed row 4 catalog, supplied match from the whole-list solver on header 'zh-TW' — the plan's published browser-chooser request, moved from the call site into the ambient ingress.

ingress-matrix-locale-ingress.description: The three TranslationOptions construction paths the oracle's optionsFrom can reach: none(), forLocale(), and the full builder. instanceLocale is deliberately fr while fallbackLocale is en, and Ingress.Probe/Ingress.Named are translated distinctly in en, fr and de, so each possible locale source produces a different string: none() must yield fr, forLocale(de) must yield de, and a builder object with no locale must yield fr rather than the fallback en. Three distinct primary languages, so tiebreakers are null. Absent.Probe is in no catalog, giving both the builder and the none() paths a failure case whose lookupLocale and attemptedLocales reveal which locale the options object actually carried.

ingress-matrix-policy-any-failure.description: Fallback-policy ingress matrix, instance leg pinned to any-failure (the permissive 2.x-compatible policy). Identical catalog to ingress-matrix-policy-default so the fixtures differ only in the instance option.

Items.Sparse.commentary: Only ONE and OTHER declared, though Russian also selects FEW and MANY. Reaching MANY throws inside getInternal, which getResult classifies as RESOLUTION_FAILURE.

ingress-matrix-policy-default.description: Fallback-policy ingress matrix, instance leg UNSET so the library default applies (DefaultStrings.java:473 installs fallbackOnMissingTranslationOrNoMatchingAlternative). A ru request against fallback en gives exactly two candidates, so the policy is genuinely consulted (:731 skips the call at the last candidate). Two distinct failure reasons in one catalog separate all three policy values: Items.Sparse declares only ONE/OTHER, so itemCount 5 selects Russian MANY and raises the 'Missing Cardinality translation for MANY' IllegalStateException = RESOLUTION_FAILURE; Items.EnOnly is simply absent from ru = MISSING_TRANSLATION. Verified by execution that the sparse placeholder LOADS (LocalizedStringValidator does not require complete cardinality coverage) and fails only at resolution.

Items.Sparse.commentary: Only ONE and OTHER declared, though Russian also selects FEW and MANY. Reaching MANY throws inside getInternal, which getResult classifies as RESOLUTION_FAILURE.

ingress-matrix-policy-missing-or-no-matc.description: Fallback-policy ingress matrix, instance leg pinned EXPLICITLY to missing-or-no-match. Identical catalog to ingress-matrix-policy-default; the pair exists so the corpus records that explicitly configuring the default and leaving it unset are the same thing, checked on BOTH failure reasons rather than only one.

Items.Sparse.commentary: Only ONE and OTHER declared, though Russian also selects FEW and MANY. Reaching MANY throws inside getInternal, which getResult classifies as RESOLUTION_FAILURE.

ingress-matrix-policy-never.description: Fallback-policy ingress matrix, instance leg pinned to never. Identical catalog to ingress-matrix-policy-default. never is the only value that halts on a plain MISSING_TRANSLATION, which is what Items.EnOnly produces at the ru candidate.

Items.Sparse.commentary: Only ONE and OTHER declared, though Russian also selects FEW and MANY. Reaching MANY throws inside getInternal, which getResult classifies as RESOLUTION_FAILURE.

ingress-smoke-browser-chooser.description: Plan v7 section 8.3's small browser chooser verbatim: supported {zh, zh-Hant} plus en, tiebreaker zh:[zh, zh-Hant]. The clause states preferences zh-TW select zh-Hant through the shared single-locale kernel, so this fixture checks a published expectation the same way the direct-locale seed rows do.

ingress-smoke-fabricated-match.description: THE SHARP CASE. A localeMatchSupplier returning a match built with LocaleMatchResult's public constructor: it claims an EXACT match on fr while naming de as the requested range — something the matcher would never produce, since de is not even loaded. Section 8.3 requires the intentional lookup difference for supplied matches to be preserved rather than re-derived.

ingress-smoke-locale-supplier.description: The other ambient ingress: a localeSupplier returning a plain Locale negotiated from ranges. MEASURED: this does NOT leave the result without a match — the library derives an EXACT match for the supplied locale, so the observable difference from a match supplier is the RANGE it reports (the supplier's own locale, not the negotiated preference list), never the presence of diagnostics.

ingress-smoke-supplied-match.description: An instance whose ambient locale comes from a localeMatchSupplier negotiating an Accept-Language header, rather than from a constant. The supplied match is what getResult reports, so the negotiation is observable end to end.

interpolation-escapes-lenient.description: Single en catalog that deliberately does NOT contain the keys the lenient cases look up; it holds one unrelated anchor translation so the file is a real loaded catalog. A missing key drives DefaultStrings.interpolateFailureKey (DefaultStrings.java:1391), which uses StringInterpolator.placeholderNamesInLeniently plus the non-strict interpolate overload, making the lookup KEY itself the string being interpolated. This is the only route by which the oracle can observe lenient interpolation, and it is the lenient half of the section 8.3 escape clause. Every lenient case here binds at least one real placeholder or contains at least one escape, so its rendered output differs from the raw key - interpolateFailureKey swallows any RuntimeException and returns the raw key, so a case whose correct output equals its key would pass even against a port that threw.

en.esc.lenient.anchor: Anchor translation that the lenient cases never look up

interpolation-escapes-strict.description: Single en catalog whose translations carry every StringInterpolator escape sequence and every index-advancement boundary of the escape state machine. Every key here RESOLVES, so DefaultStrings.interpolateTemplate runs interpolateStrictly - this is the strict half of the plan v7 section 8.3 interpolation-escape clause. Every translation is deliberately strict-VALID because LocalizedStringLoader.validatePlaceholderReferences (LocalizedStringLoader.java:2308) runs the same strict scan at load time; a strict-invalid translation raises LocalizedStringLoadingException and aborts the whole corpus build rather than producing a case row (re-verified in this review with throwaway probe fixtures). The last two keys add generated language-form placeholders: one whose form translation itself contains an escape (single-pass expansion), and one whose only reference sits inside an escaped region (never expanded at all).

en.esc.backslash.tripled-before-placeholder: \\\{{name}} is a backslash then a literal placeholder

esc.generated.escaped-only-reference.commentary: The sole reference to the declared generated placeholder sits inside an escaped region, so placeholderNamesIn never reports it and it is never expanded.

esc.generated.single-pass.commentary: The language-form translations contain an escaped placeholder that must survive expansion without being re-interpolated against the outer context.

en.esc.mixed.all-forms: Literal \{{count}} vs real {{count}}, close \}} and backslash \\ end

loader-smoke-clean.description: A well-formed two-locale catalog. The control: proves the load observation reports locales and keys for a load that succeeds.

loader-smoke-duplicate-members.description: Duplicate JSON member names in one object. JSON.stringify cannot produce this, so the file is written verbatim. Which value wins (or whether it is rejected) is exactly what section 8.3 asks to pin.

loader-smoke-incomplete-cardinality.description: A Russian catalog whose cardinality placeholder declares only CARDINALITY_ONE. Russian's CLDR set is one/few/many/other, so the validator should emit INCOMPLETE_CARDINALITY_TRANSLATIONS. Loading normally ignores warnings; the load operation captures them.

loader-smoke-lone-surrogate.description: A lone high surrogate escape. Syntactically valid JSON, not valid Unicode.

loader-smoke-magic-keys.description: Keys named __proto__, constructor and prototype. Harmless in Java, but a JS port storing catalogs in a plain object would corrupt its prototype chain, so the Java behavior must be pinned as the target.

loader-smoke-malformed-utf8.description: Raw bytes that are not valid UTF-8. Only expressible as bytes; a JS string cannot carry them.

loader-smoke-node-limit.description: A catalog loaded with maximumTranslationNodes lowered to 1, so the limit is exceeded by an ordinary two-key file.

loader-smoke-truncated-utf8.description: A truncated multi-byte UTF-8 sequence at end of string.

loader-smoke-unparseable.description: A directory containing a syntactically invalid strings file. Deliberately unloadable, so it is marked loadOnly: constructing a Strings from it is not the point, observing the load failure is.

loading-limits-depth-above-ceiling.description: The same catalog with maximumJsonNestingDepth at 129, one above the ceiling. Verified to produce the identical builder message as 0, so the discriminating content is the option value, not the text.

loading-limits-depth-at-ceiling.description: The same catalog with maximumJsonNestingDepth at the documented ceiling of 128.

loading-limits-depth-one-flat.description: A flat one-level catalog loaded with maximumJsonNestingDepth at 1, the lowest value the builder accepts.

loading-limits-depth-one-nested.description: A catalog whose single entry is an object, so the file reaches container depth 2, loaded with maximumJsonNestingDepth at 1.

loading-limits-depth-two-nested.description: The same depth-2 catalog loaded with maximumJsonNestingDepth at exactly 2.

loading-limits-depth-zero.description: A trivially loadable catalog whose loading options request maximumJsonNestingDepth 0, which the builder refuses before any file is opened.

loading-limits-discovery-above-ceiling.description: A single-file directory whose loading options request maximumDiscoveryEntries 1000001, one above the documented ceiling.

loading-limits-discovery-at-ceiling.description: A single-file directory loaded with maximumDiscoveryEntries at the ceiling of 1000000.

loading-limits-discovery-mixed-exceeds.description: The same three-child directory loaded with maximumDiscoveryEntries at 2.

loading-limits-discovery-mixed-fits.description: A directory with three children: one locale file, one dot-prefixed hidden file, one non-language-tag file. Loaded with maximumDiscoveryEntries at exactly 3.

loading-limits-discovery-one-exceeds.description: A directory with two children -- one locale file and one file whose name is not a language tag -- loaded with maximumDiscoveryEntries at 1. readme.txt has no .json extension, so languageTagForFileName returns null rather than throwing, and the file is silently skipped after being charged.

loading-limits-discovery-one-fits.description: A directory with exactly one child, loaded with maximumDiscoveryEntries at 1.

loading-limits-discovery-zero.description: A single-file directory whose loading options request maximumDiscoveryEntries 0.

loading-limits-files-one-exceeds.description: A two-file directory loaded with maximumLocalizedStringsFiles at 1. Two distinct primary languages, so no tiebreakers are required.

loading-limits-files-one-fits.description: A single-file directory loaded with maximumLocalizedStringsFiles at 1, the lowest value the builder accepts. Also the fixture behind the single-resource parse case.

loading-limits-files-zero.description: A single-file directory whose loading options request maximumLocalizedStringsFiles 0. Also the fixture behind the parse-path zero-rejection case.

loading-limits-input-bytes-exact.description: A verbatim 13-byte catalog loaded with maximumInputBytes at exactly 13.

loading-limits-input-bytes-integer-max.description: The same two-byte file with maximumInputBytes at Integer.MAX_VALUE (2147483647). The per-resource byte guard excludes the sentinel as well as 0, because the reader allocates limit+1; this is the second, non-obvious arm of the same refusal, and it is expressible under the corpus schema as it stands today.

loading-limits-input-bytes-one.description: A two-byte empty-object file loaded with maximumInputBytes at 1, the lowest value the builder accepts. Written through rawFiles because a JSON-serialized fixture would add indentation and a trailing newline and the byte count would stop being exact.

loading-limits-input-bytes-one-short.description: The same verbatim 13-byte catalog loaded with maximumInputBytes at 12. Also the fixture behind the per-resource byte-limit parse case.

loading-limits-input-bytes-zero.description: A two-byte empty-object file, written verbatim so its size is exact, whose loading options request maximumInputBytes 0.

loading-limits-manifest-256-default.description: A directory of 256 trivial locale files under the DEFAULT options, whose DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_LOCALIZED_STRINGS_FILES is 256. The admitting side of the manifest clause, and the ONLY deterministic half: a successful load emits its locales in language-tag order, with no filename-dependent message. Verified to load all 256.

loading-limits-manifest-257-default.description: A directory of 257 trivial locale files loaded under the default options, one above DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_LOCALIZED_STRINGS_FILES. Deliberately unloadable, hence loadOnly.

loading-limits-manifest-257-raised.description: The same 257-file directory with maximumLocalizedStringsFiles raised to exactly 257. Verified: all 257 locales load and the emitted locale list is in language-tag order, independent of directory iteration order.

loading-limits-nodes-composition-exceeds.description: The same five-node entry loaded with maximumTranslationNodes at 4, one short.

loading-limits-nodes-composition-fits.description: One root entry that also carries one expression-fragment placeholder with two fragment alternatives and one whole-message alternative: 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 5 nodes, loaded with maximumTranslationNodes at exactly 5. Executed: admitted at 5, refused at 4, so the composition is measured rather than assumed.

loading-limits-nodes-negative.description: A trivially loadable catalog whose loading options request maximumTranslationNodes -1. The builder refuses it as not nonnegative, which is what makes 0 a legitimate value rather than an accident.

loading-limits-nodes-one-single-key.description: One root entry loaded with maximumTranslationNodes lowered to 1: the exact budget the file spends. The admitting side of the one boundary.

loading-limits-nodes-zero-empty-catalog.description: An empty JSON object catalog loaded with maximumTranslationNodes lowered to 0. The node limit is documented NONNEGATIVE (unlike the positive-only limits), so 0 survives the builder, and a zero-member root object charges 0 nodes. Verified loadable end to end, so loadOnly is false and a Strings instance is built from it.

loading-limits-nodes-zero-single-key.description: One root entry loaded with maximumTranslationNodes lowered to 0. The single root entry costs one node, which a budget of 0 cannot pay, so the load fails. Also the fixture behind the node-limit parse case.

loading-limits-reader-characters-one.description: A catalog far larger than one UTF-16 code unit loaded with maximumReaderCharacters at 1. The reader limit governs Reader input only; filesystem and InputStream loading are bounded by the byte limits. Verified to load successfully.

loading-limits-reader-characters-zero.description: A trivially loadable catalog whose loading options request maximumReaderCharacters 0, refused by the builder before any directory is listed.

loading-limits-total-bytes-exact.description: A verbatim 13-byte catalog loaded with maximumTotalInputBytes at exactly 13.

loading-limits-total-bytes-one.description: A two-byte empty-object file loaded with maximumTotalInputBytes at 1. The aggregate is charged as bytes are read, so it trips before the per-resource size comparison and reports the aggregate message.

loading-limits-total-bytes-one-short.description: The same verbatim 13-byte catalog loaded with maximumTotalInputBytes at 12, one short. Deliberately the same file and the same number as the per-resource fixture, so the two budgets can be told apart by their messages alone.

loading-limits-total-bytes-zero.description: A two-byte empty-object file whose loading options request maximumTotalInputBytes 0. The aggregate budget is a long and carries its own builder message.

loading-limits-warnings-negative.description: A warning-free Russian catalog whose loading options request maximumWarnings -1. The builder refuses it as not nonnegative, which is what makes 0 a legitimate value rather than an accident.

loading-limits-warnings-one-single-warni.description: The same one-warning Russian catalog loaded with maximumWarnings at exactly 1. Verified: the load succeeds and the single INCOMPLETE_CARDINALITY_TRANSLATIONS warning is delivered.

loading-limits-warnings-one-two-warnings.description: A Russian catalog with two incomplete-cardinality entries, loaded with maximumWarnings at 1. Verified: the first warning IS delivered to the handler and the second trips the budget, so the observation carries failed:true alongside a one-element warnings array.

loading-limits-warnings-two-two-warnings.description: The same two-warning Russian catalog loaded with maximumWarnings at exactly 2: both warnings are delivered, in JSON document order (Items before Books), and the load succeeds.

loading-limits-warnings-zero-clean-load.description: A warning-free Russian catalog loaded with maximumWarnings lowered to 0. The builder accepts 0 and a load that emits nothing never charges the budget, so this establishes that the failure in the one-warning fixture comes from the warning rather than from the value 0.

loading-limits-warnings-zero-one-warning.description: A Russian catalog whose cardinality placeholder declares only CARDINALITY_ONE, loaded with maximumWarnings lowered to 0. The first warning the validator emits has no budget to be delivered under, so the non-fatal warning becomes a hard load failure. Also the fixture behind the warning-limit parse case.

locale-identity-deprecated-fallback-loca.description: fallbackLocale and instanceLocale are both spelled hy-810 - a tag that is on disk under NEITHER of its two loaded equivalents. DefaultStrings must canonicalize the configured fallback locale, find it equivalent to both hy-AM and hy-SU, and break the tie from the tiebreaker list (DefaultStrings.java:446-470), whose first entry here is hy-AM. Identical files and identical cases to locale-identity-deprecated-fallback-locale-reordered; only the tiebreaker ORDER differs.

Byte-for-byte the same files and the same hy-810 fallback and instance locale as locale-identity-deprecated-fallback-locale, with the tiebreaker list flipped to [hy-SU, hy-AM]. Every observable channel flips with it, which is the only way to show that the choice is made by list order rather than by canonicalization, alphabetical order, or directory order.

locale-identity-duplicate-grandfathered-.description: A grandfathered filename and its modern equivalent in one directory: zh-min-nan.json and nan both key Locale 'nan', which the loader treats as a duplicate localized strings file. zh-min-nan.json must go through rawFiles because `files` keys are written extensionless and cannot express a .json suffix. Deliberately unloadable, so loadOnly.

locale-identity-equivalent-tags-both-loa.description: hy-SU and hy-AM are the same locale after canonicalization but are loaded as two separate catalogs. Tiebreakers are mandatory and must be an exact permutation of the LOADED spellings [hy-AM, hy-SU]; the canonical set {hy-AM} would be rejected as incomplete, which is the trap this fixture exists to document. The list order also decides which sibling an ambiguous canonical request lands on - see the deprecated-fallback pair for the controlled flip.

locale-identity-explicit-canonicalizatio.description: The three canonicalizations section 8.3 names explicitly - hy-SU to hy-AM, ru-SU to ru-RU, pap-AN to pap-CW - with only the canonical targets on disk, so a requested alias tag can only arrive by being canonicalized. Three distinct primary languages plus en, so no tiebreakers are needed.

locale-identity-filename-grandfathered.description: Grandfathered/legacy IETF tags as filenames. Locale.forLanguageTag applies the JDK's registry mapping before the loader ever sees a locale, so the emitted tags are the modern replacements. Load-only: no `en` catalog exists here, so no Strings instance can be built from it.

locale-identity-filename-legacy-language.description: Deprecated language codes and one compound CLDR language alias as filenames, chosen so the two rewriting layers can be told apart: the JDK rewrites iw/in/ji, CLDR would rewrite sh (to sr-Latn), tl (to fil), mo (to ro), cmn (to zh) and aa-Saaho (to ssy), and only the first layer runs at load. Load-only.

locale-identity-filename-normalization.description: Section 8.3 locale-identity clause: filenames spelled zh-hant, nb-no, und, private use, and the three alias-bearing tags hy-SU/ru-SU/pap-AN loaded together, so the emitted locale list shows exactly which normalization the loader applies to a filename. Load-only, and necessarily so: no `en` file is present, so the `en` fallback locale has no canonically equivalent loaded locale and DefaultStrings could not be constructed even if a case wanted one.

locale-identity-filename-rejected.description: Filenames the loader refuses to treat as locales at all, each failing a DIFFERENT clause of isLanguageTag (LocalizedStringLoader.java:1649): root passes Locale.Builder but is not CldrLocaleData.isKnownLanguageTag; en-ANT builds to the extlang-promoted 'ant' and is likewise not known; i-enochian IS a known tag but builds to x-i-enochian, whose primary language is empty and which is not explicitly undetermined. One valid file proves the load still succeeds around them. Load-only.

locale-identity-grandfathered-requests.description: The mirror of the grandfathered-FILENAME fixture: here the modern catalogs are on disk and the grandfathered spellings arrive as REQUESTS. Locale.forLanguageTag rewrites the request before the library sees it, so each case pins one row of the JDK's legacy table plus the match category the rewritten tag then earns. Catalogs are chosen so the eight rows land on four different match types (EXACT, CANONICAL, LIKELY_SUBTAG, CLDR_FALLBACK). Eight distinct primary languages, so no tiebreakers are needed.

locale-identity-legacy-tags-on-disk.description: The reverse of the canonicalization fixture: the DEPRECATED spellings are what the deployer put on disk (hy-SU, pap-AN, sh, mo, cmn) and callers ask with modern tags. Directly serves the 'candidate tags differing from loaded file tags' clause. The five canonical primary languages (hy, pap, sr, ro, zh) are distinct from each other and from en, so no tiebreakers are needed.

locale-identity-mo-tiebreaker-language-c.description: Loaded mo and ro are two catalogs whose CANONICAL primary language is the same (mo aliases to ro), so DefaultStrings groups them under language code 'ro'. The fixture supplies the tiebreaker under the deprecated key 'mo' on purpose: normalizedTiebreakerLanguageCode (DefaultStrings.java:2649, called from line 325) canonicalizes the supplied key before the exact-permutation check at line 404, so a port that compares raw keys cannot even construct this instance. The list itself is the exact permutation of the LOADED spellings, not of the canonical one.

locale-identity-nb-no-macrolanguage.description: nb-NO alone on disk, so every no-* request must arrive through the Norwegian macrolanguage bridge in CldrLocaleData.addMacrolanguageBridgeTags (line 403) rather than by ordinary parent walking.

locale-identity-no-macrolanguage-catalog.description: The mirror of the nb-NO fixture: the macrolanguage tag 'no' is the one on disk and the specific tag is requested, proving the Norwegian bridge runs in both directions.

locale-identity-region-alias-extlang-col.description: The five multi-valued region aliases that are three ALPHA characters - ANT, NTZ, SCG, SUN, YUG. BCP 47 reads a three-letter subtag after a language as an extlang, and Locale.forLanguageTag promotes it to primary language, so these aliases can never reach the region-alias table. Catalogs for the resulting languages are loaded to make the collapse observable rather than merely absent; ru and sr are loaded as the languages the caller thought they were asking for.

locale-identity-region-alias-first-prefe.description: Every multi-valued region alias that survives Java's Locale boundary, requested against English. English's likely region (US) appears in none of the twenty-three alias value lists, verified against vendor cldr-locale-data.json, so each request must land on the FIRST value of its list. One en-<first value> catalog per distinct target, plus en-US for the single-valued 840 control. Tiebreakers are MANDATORY here and are an exact permutation of all eleven loaded en locales.

locale-identity-region-alias-likely-pref.description: The other branch of CldrLocaleData.preferredRegionAlias: languages whose likely region appears LATER in the alias value list. Each language loads two catalogs - the alias list's first value and the likely-subtag value - so a wrong preference rule selects a real but different catalog instead of failing to match. The list covers picks at index 1 (sk, vic, ckb, hy), 2 (cal), 3 (hr and pau, the last value of their four-value rows), 4 (et), 5 (bs, the last value of the six-value 890 row) and 14 (uz, the deepest pick reachable anywhere in the alias table). Every language here needs tiebreakers, each an exact permutation of its two loaded locales.

locale-identity-root-json-filename.description: root.json: the same name that is silently skipped without an extension becomes a hard load failure with one, because a .json file MUST be named with a valid tag. rawFiles is required to write a name carrying the extension. Deliberately unloadable, so loadOnly.

locale-identity-ru-su-plural-rules.description: A Russian catalog whose FILENAME is the deprecated ru-SU and whose only cardinality forms are ONE and OTHER. Locale identity is observed through plural-rule selection: the forms the validator demands and the form the evaluator selects both depend on resolving ru-SU to Russian.

locale-identity-undetermined-and-private.description: und, und-Latn, x-private and en-x-custom loaded together. LocaleUtils.normalizedLanguage returns empty for undetermined and private-use tags, so und and und-Latn create no tiebreaker ambiguity at all (DefaultStrings skips them when grouping loaded locales by language code), while en-x-custom DOES carry primary language en and therefore forces a tiebreaker permutation with en. That asymmetry is the point of the fixture. NOTE (ingest): the und-Latn catalog was REMOVED. Loading both und and und-Latn makes the language 'und' ambiguous, and DefaultStrings then rejects the required tiebreaker entry outright with "Tiebreaker language code 'und' must identify a primary language" — so that catalog set cannot be built at all. und-Latn survives here as a REQUESTED tag, which is what the cases actually exercise.
