locale-identity-zh-hant-script.description: zh-Hant as the sole Chinese catalog, so every request is judged on script identity. Deliberately different from the section 8.3 seed row 4 fixture (direct-zh-tw), which also loads zh: here zh-Hant is the only place a Chinese key can come from.

m3b-canonicalization-aliases.description: One catalog per CANONICALIZATION OUTCOME. Every locale here is the tag some deprecated, aliased or placeholder-bearing request is supposed to canonicalize TO, and nothing else in the set is reachable from that request, so the selected catalog names the canonical form the implementation actually computed. That is what makes these cases discriminating rather than merely reaching: CldrLocaleData has no public surface, and its output is only observable as WHICH CATALOG a negotiation lands on. en/en-Zinh, the three sr catalogs, and the two fa catalogs each need tiebreakers because they share a normalized language code; the tiebreaker orders are deliberately the ones that would win if canonicalization did NOT run, so a port that skipped an alias falls back to the tiebreaker's first entry and produces a different answer.

m3b-form-diagnostics-lowered-compact-exp.description: The same catalog as m3b-form-diagnostics-sparse with maximumCompactExponent lowered to 3, so a PluralOperands record carrying compactExponent 10 -- perfectly legal at PluralOperands' own default ceiling of 64 -- is refused by the INSTANCE limit inside DefaultStrings.ordinalityForValue's validatePluralOperands call rather than at operand construction. Separating the two ceilings is the whole point of the fixture.

m3b-form-diagnostics-sparse.description: M3b owed cases for DefaultStrings.getInternal's per-axis missing-value, wrong-type and sparse-form diagnostics. Every language-form map here is DELIBERATELY INCOMPLETE, and each key isolates exactly one axis so the composed failure message identifies which arm fired. The two range keys separate the missing-range-END diagnostic (Range.Books, whose start is supplied and whose end is not) from the sparse-range-result diagnostic (Range.SparseResult, whose map carries only CARDINALITY_ONE while an en 1-1 range computes OTHER). Ordinal.Finish's map covers only ONE and TWO of en's four ordinal forms, so a value of 4 selects the absent OTHER. Loading only warns about incomplete form maps, which is what makes these states reachable at all.

m3b-negotiation-de-regional.description: Two German regional catalogs plus an unrelated en-US, so an extended range's structural filter has both matching and non-matching locales to choose between, and a LEADING wildcard ('*-CH') has more than one language to pick from.

m3b-negotiation-en-only.description: A single bare 'en' catalog with a French fallback. Every en-REGIONAL range therefore relates to it only through CLDR fallback, which is the one anchor category that is NOT eligible for q=0 exclusion, and en-GB and en-AU relate to it with identical specificity. That is the configuration the governor and anchor sweeps need: two equally specific anchors on one locale, whose competition can only be decided by weight and then by request order.

m3b-negotiation-equivalent-parent.description: A Moldavian catalog and nothing else Romanian. mo is canonically equivalent to ro but is loaded under its deprecated spelling, so a ro-MD request can only be satisfied by the SECOND pass of CLDR parent-locale fallback -- the one that matches by canonical equivalence rather than by exact tag.

m3b-negotiation-extension-singleton.description: A catalog loaded under a tag carrying a BCP 47 extension singleton (de-u-co-phonebk). RFC 4647 extended filtering treats a single-character subtag in the tag as terminating the match instead of being skipped, and no corpus locale carries one.

m3b-negotiation-private-and-undetermined.description: A catalog set that mixes an ordinary locale with the two SHAPES the range solver treats specially: a private-use tag (x-private) and an undetermined one (und-Latn). Both are loadable and both are unreachable by ordinary language matching, which is what makes them the right probes for the private-use and undetermined arms of the member classification.

m3b-negotiation-sr-cyrillic.description: A Cyrillic-only Serbian catalog. sr's likely subtag is sr-Cyrl-RS, so a Latin-script Serbian request shares the primary language but implies a different script -- the exact state DefaultStrings.languageRangeSpecificityFor:2077 and compatibleLikelyScripts:2427 exist to refuse.

m3b-negotiation-zxx-regional.description: Three regional catalogs of zxx ('no linguistic content'), a language with no likely-subtag entry of its own. Used for the extended-range structural filter, where two of the three loaded locales must be REJECTED by the filter rather than carried through.

m3b-region-slot-alias-region-adoption.description: A Persian pair whose only difference is whether the language alias's region survives: fa-AF is loaded and fa is loaded, so a range that adopts prs's alias region AF selects a DIFFERENT catalog from one that does not. The unrelated fr fallback makes 'selected nothing' a third, distinguishable outcome.

m3b-supplied-match-locale-not-considered.description: A localeMatchSupplier handing the library a LocaleMatchResult built through its PUBLIC constructor. The supplier is invoked lazily at lookup time, so the constructor's refusal surfaces as a per-case throw rather than as an unbuildable fixture. Caller-supplied match results are revalidated on every use, so each of these is a live validation path a port must reproduce rather than a Java-only assertion. A selected locale absent from the result's own considered-locale list.

m3b-supplied-match-locale-with-none-type.description: A localeMatchSupplier handing the library a LocaleMatchResult built through its PUBLIC constructor. The supplier is invoked lazily at lookup time, so the constructor's refusal surfaces as a per-case throw rather than as an unbuildable fixture. Caller-supplied match results are revalidated on every use, so each of these is a live validation path a port must reproduce rather than a Java-only assertion. A matched result naming a locale, range and weight but typed NONE.

m3b-supplied-match-locale-without-range.description: A localeMatchSupplier handing the library a LocaleMatchResult built through its PUBLIC constructor. The supplier is invoked lazily at lookup time, so the constructor's refusal surfaces as a per-case throw rather than as an unbuildable fixture. Caller-supplied match results are revalidated on every use, so each of these is a live validation path a port must reproduce rather than a Java-only assertion. A MATCHED result naming a locale but omitting the language range.

m3b-supplied-match-locale-without-weight.description: A localeMatchSupplier handing the library a LocaleMatchResult built through its PUBLIC constructor. The supplier is invoked lazily at lookup time, so the constructor's refusal surfaces as a per-case throw rather than as an unbuildable fixture. Caller-supplied match results are revalidated on every use, so each of these is a live validation path a port must reproduce rather than a Java-only assertion. A matched result naming a locale and range but omitting the effective weight.

m3b-supplied-match-none-with-range.description: A localeMatchSupplier handing the library a LocaleMatchResult built through its PUBLIC constructor. The supplier is invoked lazily at lookup time, so the constructor's refusal surfaces as a per-case throw rather than as an unbuildable fixture. Caller-supplied match results are revalidated on every use, so each of these is a live validation path a port must reproduce rather than a Java-only assertion. An UNMATCHED result (no selected locale) that nevertheless carries a language range.

m3b-supplied-match-none-with-weight.description: A localeMatchSupplier handing the library a LocaleMatchResult built through its PUBLIC constructor. The supplier is invoked lazily at lookup time, so the constructor's refusal surfaces as a per-case throw rather than as an unbuildable fixture. Caller-supplied match results are revalidated on every use, so each of these is a live validation path a port must reproduce rather than a Java-only assertion. An unmatched result carrying an effective weight.

m3b-supplied-match-type-without-locale.description: A localeMatchSupplier handing the library a LocaleMatchResult built through its PUBLIC constructor. The supplier is invoked lazily at lookup time, so the constructor's refusal surfaces as a per-case throw rather than as an unbuildable fixture. Caller-supplied match results are revalidated on every use, so each of these is a live validation path a port must reproduce rather than a Java-only assertion. A non-NONE match type with no selected locale.

m3b-supplied-match-valid.description: A localeMatchSupplier handing the library a LocaleMatchResult built through its PUBLIC constructor. The supplier is invoked lazily at lookup time, so the constructor's refusal surfaces as a per-case throw rather than as an unbuildable fixture. Caller-supplied match results are revalidated on every use, so each of these is a live validation path a port must reproduce rather than a Java-only assertion. The WELL-FORMED control: identical in every other respect to the nine refusals, and it must resolve normally.

m3b-supplied-match-weight-above-one.description: A localeMatchSupplier handing the library a LocaleMatchResult built through its PUBLIC constructor. The supplier is invoked lazily at lookup time, so the constructor's refusal surfaces as a per-case throw rather than as an unbuildable fixture. Caller-supplied match results are revalidated on every use, so each of these is a live validation path a port must reproduce rather than a Java-only assertion. An effective weight above the closed upper bound of 1.

m3b-supplied-match-weight-zero.description: A localeMatchSupplier handing the library a LocaleMatchResult built through its PUBLIC constructor. The supplier is invoked lazily at lookup time, so the constructor's refusal surfaces as a per-case throw rather than as an unbuildable fixture. Caller-supplied match results are revalidated on every use, so each of these is a live validation path a port must reproduce rather than a Java-only assertion. An effective weight of exactly 0, the open lower bound.

m3b-tag-validity-filenames.description: Ten strings files named after tags that sit on either side of CldrLocaleData.isKnownLanguageTag's three subtag-validity gates, loaded as a DIRECTORY so the loader's own accept/reject decision is the observation. LocalizedStringLoader gates every candidate filename on isKnownLanguageTag (LocalizedStringLoader.java:1672), so the set of locales that appear in the load result IS the predicate's truth table -- which is the only place the predicate is directly observable, since matchFor can only report which catalog it landed on. loadOnly, because several of these tags are deliberately unloadable and the fixture must never be asked to build a Strings.

m3b-wildcard-preference-multilingual-ch.description: Two languages that both have a Swiss regional catalog, so a LEADING wildcard range ('*-CH') survives into a candidate list spanning two primary languages, and an ANCHORED wildcard ('de-*') survives into a two-locale list whose configured tiebreaker order is deliberately NOT list order. preferredLocaleForWildcard consults the FALLBACK LANGUAGE's tiebreaker list and then falls to the first candidate; preferredLocaleForRange consults the RANGE's primary-language tiebreaker list and then the fallback locale and then the first candidate. Here those two rules pick different locales for both shapes, which is what makes DefaultStrings.matchFor:1845 observable.

malformed-structure-alternatives.description: Violations of the whole-message alternatives array: wrong container type, empty array, null and non-object elements, empty and multi-member alternative objects, an unparseable expression key, and alternatives whose values have the wrong node type.

malformed-structure-degenerate-keys.description: A catalog whose keys include the empty string and a whitespace-only string alongside an ordinary key. Deliberately LOADABLE: whether these are rejected at load or become ordinary keys is exactly the clause's question, and it turns out they load, so the fixture also carries lookup cases.

malformed-structure-fragment-placeholder.description: Violations inside a template-mode (generated fragment) placeholder definition: a missing default translation, a null default translation, a non-string default translation, non-array and null fragment alternatives, empty alternatives, null and non-object alternative elements, a non-string alternative result, an unparseable fragment expression, and a multi-expression fragment alternative object.

malformed-structure-invalid-expressions.description: Alternative keys that are syntactically valid JSON member names but not parseable expressions: empty, operand-only, an unclosed and an unopened parenthesis, a dangling logical operator, an unknown operator symbol, and a chained comparison. Each pins a DISTINCT evaluator diagnostic surfaced at load time; the last file is an alternatives-only control that loads.

malformed-structure-language-form-transl.description: Violations inside a language-form placeholder definition: missing value/range, missing translations, wrongly typed translations, non-language-form translation keys, non-string translation values, mixed axes, explicit nulls for two different members, value plus range, a range with non-cardinality forms, an empty translations table, and a value that is mistyped or is not a valid identifier.

malformed-structure-load-halts-directory.description: A directory with one perfectly good locale and one structurally invalid locale. Serves the load-time-versus-lookup-time distinction: proves a structural violation is a startup error for the WHOLE load, not a per-file skip.

malformed-structure-nested-duplicate-mem.description: Duplicate JSON member names nested BELOW the top level -- inside a localized-string object, inside a translations table, inside the placeholders map, and inside an alternatives array element. loader-smoke pins only top-level duplicates; these exercise the recursive check and its JSON-path reporting, and require verbatim text because JSON.stringify cannot emit a duplicate member.

malformed-structure-object-members.description: Wrong node types and unknown members inside the object form of a localized string: a numeric translation, an explicitly null translation, a numeric commentary, an unknown field, an empty object, and an object carrying neither translation nor alternatives.

malformed-structure-placeholder-referenc.description: Templates whose {{...}} references are structurally invalid: a malformed name, an unclosed placeholder, a stray closing delimiter, a reserved language-form constant, and malformed references reached through a placeholder translation and through an alternative (which exercises the declaration-path rendering).

malformed-structure-placeholders-contain.description: Violations of the placeholders container and placeholder-name rules: placeholders as an array, placeholders as explicit null, a placeholder definition that is a bare string, an empty definition, an unknown definition member, an invalid identifier, a reserved language-form name, and a definition mixing language-form with template members -- plus a well-formed but unreferenced definition as the control (sv, whose cardinality set is one/other, so the control emits no warning).

malformed-structure-range-shape.description: Violations of the range object inside a language-form placeholder: not an object, a missing end, a non-string start, a non-string end, an explicitly null start, an endpoint that is not a legal identifier, and an unknown member -- plus a well-formed range as the control. The range shape has its own member whitelist and its own error messages.

malformed-structure-top-level-shape.description: Files that are syntactically valid JSON but not a catalog at the top level (array, string, number, null), and files that are blank or nearly blank (all four characters the loader counts as JSON whitespace, an empty file, and a single U+00A0 which it does NOT count) -- plus an empty JSON object as the control that loads. Written verbatim because a top-level non-object cannot be expressed through the locale-keyed files map.

malformed-structure-undefined-references.description: A catalog that is entirely well formed but whose translation references a placeholder no definition supplies, and whose alternative expression reads a variable no caller need supply. The classic loads-fine, fails-later shape: nothing here is a load-time error, so the fixture is loadable and carries both a load case and lookup cases.

malformed-structure-value-types.description: One file per wrong JSON type for a translation entry's value: number, boolean, array, and explicit null. Each parses as JSON but is not a valid catalog entry, and all four reach the same terminal else-branch of LocalizedStringLoader.parseLocalizedString. Serves the section 8.3 'wrong node types' clause.

manifest-loads-complete.description: A complete four-locale manifest: en (the fallback, carrying an extra en-only key), de, de-AT, and fr, all well-formed. Serves the 'complete manifest loads' clause of section 8.3 and anchors the partial fixtures that follow. Two German locales share a primary language, so the exact tiebreaker permutation is mandatory.

manifest-loads-duplicate-locale-spelling.description: Two filename spellings of the same locale — extensionless 'en' and 'en.json' — in one directory. Both resolve to Locale en and the load fails with a duplicate-file diagnostic. CORRECTED BY REVIEW to loadOnly: true; the authored version said false while its own description said otherwise, which left the oracle building a Strings it must fail to build. It survives only because no lookup case names it, and would abort the whole corpus build the moment one did.

manifest-loads-empty-catalog-file.description: The extreme of key-level partiality: fr's file is a valid but EMPTY JSON object. Verified: fr is still a first-class loaded locale with a zero-length key list, and a request for fr is selected EXACTLY by the matcher while resolution walks past it to en. The one fixture in this family where the two channels disagree about a locale that really loaded.

manifest-loads-fallback-only-file.description: A directory whose only file is the fallback locale — the minimal loadable manifest. Carries two keys so that a missing-key case can be distinguished from a missing-locale case.

manifest-loads-file-limit-exceeded.description: Added by review: the same cap of 1 against TWO loadable files. The whole directory load aborts with the aggregate file-limit diagnostic. loadOnly. Its case is informational only, because the diagnostic names whichever file the directory stream reached second, and that is filesystem-dependent; the portable half of the proposition lives in manifest-loads-file-limit-skipped-entries.

manifest-loads-file-limit-skipped-entrie.description: Added by review: maximumLocalizedStringsFiles lowered to 1 in a directory holding one loadable file plus four entries discovery skips (an unrecognized name, an unknown language, a hidden tag, a non-tag). Verified: the load SUCCEEDS. LoadingSession.beginLocalizedStringsFile is only reached for files that are actually parsed, so skipped entries cost nothing against the file cap — they are counted separately by maximumDiscoveryEntries, which this corpus's schema cannot express.

manifest-loads-hidden-files-only.description: A non-empty directory whose only entry is hidden. The load succeeds and returns an EMPTY manifest with no warnings; loadOnly because a zero-locale catalog cannot build a Strings. The extreme end of 'deliberately partial'.

manifest-loads-json-extension-invalid-ta.description: The same stem that manifest-loads-unrecognized-filenames skips silently, here given a .json extension. Discovery rejects it with a hard LocalizedStringLoadingException naming the file, so the whole load fails and the fixture is loadOnly. The skip-vs-reject asymmetry turns entirely on the extension. The diagnostic quotes only the bare filename, no path, so it is iteration-order independent.

manifest-loads-language-entirely-absent.description: The sharp clause of section 8.3. en (fallback) and fr load normally; German is represented on disk by de.txt and de-AT.txt, whose names are not language tags and which carry no .json extension, so discovery skips both silently. German therefore contributes NOTHING and receives no tiebreaker entry at all rather than an empty one. Paired with manifest-loads-language-one-child-loaded, which shows the observable difference an entry makes.

manifest-loads-language-files-unparseabl.description: The other reading of 'every file for one nonfallback language fails': the single German file is genuinely unparseable rather than undiscovered. Java's filesystem load has no per-file tolerance, so the entire directory load throws even though en is valid and the observed locale list comes back EMPTY. loadOnly because no Strings can be built from it. Exactly one bad file, so the diagnostic does not depend on directory iteration order.

manifest-loads-language-one-child-loaded.description: The contrast to manifest-loads-language-entirely-absent: the de file is again unrecognized, but de-CH loads. German therefore has exactly one loaded locale and DefaultStrings synthesizes the identity tiebreaker de:[de-CH] (DefaultStrings.java: 'If there is exactly 1 locale for the language code, it's its own identity tiebreaker'), which visibly changes the attempted-locale chain for de and de-AT requests. de-CH is chosen over de-AT deliberately so the loaded child is NOT the likely-subtag expansion of the requests, isolating the tiebreaker route.

manifest-loads-non-object-root.description: Added by review: a German file that is perfectly valid JSON but whose root is an ARRAY, not an object. Verified to fail with a distinct diagnostic ('a localized strings file must be comprised of a single JSON object') carrying no line:column, unlike the syntax-error path. Isolates one cause, and one bad file only, so the message is iteration-order independent. loadOnly.

manifest-loads-partial-catalog.description: A deliberately partial manifest at the KEY level: both locales load, but fr carries one of the three keys en carries. Serves the 'deliberately partial manifest loads' clause where partiality is inside a file rather than in the file set.

manifest-loads-single-nonfallback-file.description: A directory with a single file, for a locale that is NOT the configured fallback. The load itself succeeds and is indifferent to the fallback locale; it is Strings construction that would refuse, so the fixture is loadOnly and carries only a load case. Ingest warns that the fallback is not among the loaded files — that warning is the point of the fixture.

manifest-loads-tiebreaker-order-reversed.description: Two German children load and the supplied tiebreaker list is de:[de-CH, de-AT] — the REVERSE of both the file-write order and alphabetical order. Added by review: it makes the CONTENT of a tiebreaker entry observable, which is what gives the absent-vs-present pair its meaning. The existing seed row 2 (direct-fr-be, fr:[fr-FR, fr-CA]) rules out alphabetical order only; it cannot rule out a port that follows manifest insertion order, because there the two coincide. Here they do not.

manifest-loads-unassigned-region-filenam.description: A file named de-XX, an unassigned region. Verified against the library: discovery ACCEPTS it and the manifest gains a real de-XX locale, because LocalizedStringLoader.isLanguageTag validates the tag's LANGUAGE against CldrLocaleData, not its region. Written through rawFiles because the literal filename is the subject of the case; German has one loaded locale either way, so no explicit tiebreaker is required.

manifest-loads-unrecognized-filenames.description: Files whose names are not loadable locale tags, alongside a valid en. 'notes.txt' fails the tag grammar outright; 'zz' is well-formed but not a CLDR-known language; 'strings' is grammatically a language subtag but unknown — and is the exact stem that manifest-loads-json-extension-invalid-tag turns into a hard failure by appending .json; '.en-GB' is a valid tag hidden behind a leading dot. Verified: all four are skipped silently, with no warning and no failure.

manifest-loads-uppercase-filename.description: A single file named with an uppercase tag. Discovery parses the name into a Locale and keys the manifest by the canonical lowercase form, which is the mechanism behind the duplicate-spelling collision. Written through rawFiles so the literal uppercase filename reaches disk.

no-catalog.description: A minimal catalog for operations that exercise the public classifier functions rather than translation. The Strings instance is built but unused; the fixture exists so every case has a uniform shape.

numeric-boundaries-catalog.description: Plan v7 section 8.3: safe-integer boundaries, compact exponents, and trailing zeros carried through the translation path. `Order {{orderId}}` alternatives compare against exact 16- and 21-digit literals; `{{position}} place` exposes the English ordinal categories that separate 2^53 from 2^53+1; `{{itemCount}} counted` selects a category-tagged generated placeholder in en, ru, and fr. No two loaded locales share a primary language code, so tiebreakers are absent.

Order {{orderId}}.commentary: Exact-equality alternatives on integers an IEEE-754 binary64 cannot represent.

{{position}} place.commentary: English ordinals separate the three safe-integer boundary values by their last digit, so this key exposes 2^53 and 2^53+1 as different translations.

numeric-boundaries-indic.description: Plan v7 section 8.3: the Indic `i = 0 or n = 1` cardinal family (hi, bn, gu) carried through the translation path at 10^17, 10^18, and 10^20 as well as through both the i = 0 and the n = 1 branches. Each locale's generated placeholder tags the category it selected so the recorded translation names the branch. Every non-fallback catalog is selected by at least one case. No two loaded locales share a primary language code, so tiebreakers are absent.

{{itemCount}} counted.commentary: The required fallback catalog. Emits only the generated form so that if fallback ever were used the recorded translation would name it.

options-smoke-bidi.description: Parallel Arabic and English templates interpolating a caller value, so bidi isolation is observable as added directional isolates. shouldApplyBidiIsolation takes the EVALUATION locale, which the donor rule makes the supplying locale.

options-smoke-policy.description: An en catalog whose entry declares ONLY CARDINALITY_ONE, so any other category raises a RESOLUTION_FAILURE, and a fr fallback that declares both. The two policies therefore diverge visibly: the default halts on the failure, any-failure walks on to fr.

owed-bidi-private-use-locale.description: BidiIsolation.RTL_LOCALES with three catalogs whose LOCALES decide isolation: ar maximizes to ar-Arab-EG and isolates, en maximizes to en-Latn-US and does not, and x-private has no script subtag AND no likely subtag at all -- the only route to BidiUtils.localeUsesRightToLeftScript's `likelySubtag.isPresent()` FALSE arm, where `script` stays empty and isRightToLeftScript("") decides.

owed-bidi-repeated-placeholder.description: BidiIsolation.ALWAYS with a template naming the SAME placeholder twice. StringInterpolator looks the value up per occurrence, so one BoundedIsolatedValue's render() is called twice -- the memoized second call on BidiUtils$BoundedIsolatedValue.render line 209, which no corpus template reaches because no isolated template repeats a placeholder. maximumInterpolatedOutputCharacters is left at its default so the second render succeeds.

owed-bidi-repeated-placeholder-tight-lim.description: The same repeated-placeholder template under maximumInterpolatedOutputCharacters 11. 'abcd' isolates to 6 characters; the first occurrence fits, and the second is offered a remaining budget of 5, so the MEMOIZED path's own limit check (render line 210) rejects it. Note the threshold differs from the first render's: line 210 compares the ISOLATED length against the remaining budget, while BidiUtils.isolate line 98 compares the RAW length -- and the reported maximum is the FULL limit (11), not the remaining budget.

owed-construct-base.description: Control for the construction-refusal family: an ordinary fixture that MUST construct, so a refusal row is read against an accepting one rather than in isolation.

owed-construct-catalog-null.description: Construction refusal subject. DefaultStrings:262 -- a catalog supplier that answers null, which is NOT the same as supplying none. Its files load cleanly; the refusal is at Strings construction, which is what makes it invisible without the 'construct' operation.

owed-construct-catalog-omitted.description: Construction refusal subject. DefaultStrings:250 -- no catalog source at all. Its files load cleanly; the refusal is at Strings construction, which is what makes it invisible without the 'construct' operation.

owed-construct-duplicate-tag.description: Construction refusal subject. DefaultStrings:280 -- two distinct Locale keys whose tags lowercase to the same BCP 47 tag. Its files load cleanly; the refusal is at Strings construction, which is what makes it invisible without the 'construct' operation.

owed-construct-locale-source-absent.description: Construction refusal subject. DefaultStrings:254, both-ABSENT arm. Its files load cleanly; the refusal is at Strings construction, which is what makes it invisible without the 'construct' operation.

owed-construct-null-catalog-value.description: Construction refusal subject. DefaultStrings:286 -- a null catalog for one locale, which a port might read as an empty catalog. Its files load cleanly; the refusal is at Strings construction, which is what makes it invisible without the 'construct' operation.

owed-construct-null-entry.description: Construction refusal subject. DefaultStrings:293 -- a null entry inside an otherwise valid catalog; the failure mode of skipping it is a silently smaller catalog. Its files load cleanly; the refusal is at Strings construction, which is what makes it invisible without the 'construct' operation.

owed-construct-null-locale-key.description: Construction refusal subject. DefaultStrings:273 -- a null locale key, which a JS Map catalog can carry but a plain object cannot. Its files load cleanly; the refusal is at Strings construction, which is what makes it invisible without the 'construct' operation.

owed-define-catalog.description: One loaded catalog holding one entry per SHAPE a LocalizedString can take: plain, commented, a value-based LanguageFormTranslation, a range-based one, a generated ExpressionTranslation fragment with an alternative, and a whole-message alternative. Every `define` case hands a hand-built probe to DefaultStrings$LocalizedStringSet.contains against this catalog, so each field of LocalizedString#equals and of the four nested equals methods has both an EQUAL row and a row where exactly that field differs. Nothing here is degenerate: the fixture loads and constructs like any other, because the hand-built side lives in the case input rather than in the fixture -- which is why `define` needs no construction exemption and no permutation gate, unlike `construct`. Single locale, so tiebreakers is null.

owed-ds-alias-ladder.description: Catalogs for both ends of several IANA/CLDR equivalence classes, so the identity-preference ladder in semanticLanguageRangeForDerivedMatching has somewhere to land in either direction. Requests use UNRECOGNIZED range spellings (isKnownLanguageTag false), which is the only condition under which the ladder runs at all.

owed-ds-extlang-accepted.description: The accepting partner of owed-ds-extlang-jdk-spelling: 'ar-ary' collapses losslessly to 'ary', which the JDK materializes identically, so the extlang identity IS established and the Moroccan Arabic catalog is reachable from the extlang spelling. Without this partner the refusal case above would be satisfied by a port that never derives extlang equivalences at all.

owed-ds-extlang-jdk-spelling.description: A 'nyn' (Nyankole) catalog beside English. The range 'no-nyn' has the exact extlang SHAPE the lossless-extlang fallback accepts -- two alphabetic subtags of length 2 and 3 -- and its collapsed candidate 'nyn' IS a known CLDR language tag, so only the second half of DefaultStrings:2124 refuses it: the JDK materializes 'no-nyn' as the grandfathered 'nn', not as 'nyn'. A port that checked only 'is the collapsed tag known' derives a bogus nyn identity and serves the Nyankole catalog for a Norwegian request.

owed-ds-fallback-tiebreaker-walk.description: The configured fallback locale 'sr-Latn' is loaded under NEITHER of its two canonically equivalent spellings: hbs and sh both canonicalize to sr-Latn, and sr-Cyrl does not. Construction must therefore disambiguate the fallback through the language's tiebreaker list, and that list deliberately leads with sr-Cyrl -- a member of the language's tiebreaker permutation that is NOT equivalent to the fallback. The walk must SKIP it and land on sh. A port that took the first tiebreaker unconditionally serves every fallback translation from the Cyrillic catalog.

owed-ds-fallback-tiebreaker-walk-alt.description: The same catalogs and the same unloaded fallback tag as owed-ds-fallback-tiebreaker-walk, with only the tiebreaker ORDER changed so that an equivalent spelling leads. The resolved fallback must move from sh to hbs; a port that ignored tiebreaker order entirely, or sorted the equivalent set, cannot satisfy both halves.

owed-ds-heuristic-depth-order.description: Two regional English catalogs plus an unrelated fallback. Requests are written so that TWO specific heuristic ranges compete for them: neither range is an anchor for either catalog (no exact, canonical, structural or CLDR-fallback relationship exists between en-US/en-CA/en-Latn-US and en-GB/en-AU), so both go through assignPreferredSpecificHeuristicLocales and its comparator decides which range claims which catalog. The configured tiebreaker order makes the first claim deterministic, so the OUTPUT reveals the comparator's ordering.

owed-ds-likely-subtag-tiebreakerless-fal.description: Two Min Nan catalogs whose likely subtag is identically nan-Hans, requested through the grandfathered spelling zh-min-nan. The tiebreaker lookup key is derived from the range's FIRST subtag -- 'zh' -- while the catalogs are keyed under 'nan', so the lookup misses and lookupMatchByLikelySubtag must disambiguate by fallback-then-first instead. Here the configured fallback is the SECOND candidate, so 'first candidate' and 'fallback' disagree.

owed-ds-likely-subtag-tiebreakerless-fir.description: The partner of owed-ds-likely-subtag-tiebreakerless-fallback with the fallback locale outside the likely-subtag candidate set, so the same request must resolve to the first candidate.

owed-ds-private-use-wildcard-fallback.description: Two private-use catalogs under one x-foo stem, reachable together only through an extended range. LocaleUtils.normalizedLanguage is empty for private-use tags, so DefaultStrings never records a language code for them and the tiebreaker map has NO entry the lookup key 'x' could hit -- the silent-fallthrough state of lookupMatchByTiebreakers:2640. preferredLocaleForRange must then prefer the configured fallback locale, which here is one of the two candidates and is NOT the first of them. The 'mo' catalog is present only so ingest's alias heuristic treats the fixture as alias-affected; Java requires no tiebreakers for private-use tags and would REFUSE a tiebreaker entry for 'x'.

owed-ds-private-use-wildcard-first.description: The partner of owed-ds-private-use-wildcard-fallback with the fallback locale moved OUT of the candidate set, so the same request must fall through to the first candidate instead. Together the pair pins 'tiebreakers, then fallback, then first' rather than the plain 'first' a port can pass the whole corpus with.

owed-ds-redundant-tiebreakers.description: A tiebreaker list supplied for a language that has exactly ONE loaded catalog. Java keeps the caller's single-element list instead of synthesizing the identity one, and -- the observable part -- ACCEPTS the configuration rather than rejecting it as redundant. No existing fixture supplies tiebreakers for an unambiguous language, so a port that refused them would pass the entire corpus.

owed-ds-semantic-ladder-known-then-unkno.description: Catalogs for the sign-language equivalence class the JDK materializes for sgn-be-fr. The range 'sgn-be-fr-x-a' is not a known tag, its JDK rendering (sgn-BE) is LOSSY and therefore appears in none of its identities, and its identity set carries a known member (sfb-x-a) followed by an unknown one (sgn-be-fx-x-a). That ordering is the only shape in which semanticLanguageRangeForDerivedMatching's known-tag rung has to REJECT a later candidate rather than accept it -- an exhaustive sweep of 879,768 range spellings found no other.

owed-ds-undetermined-catalog.description: A bare 'und' catalog beside an ordinary one. und's own likely subtag IS populated (CLDR maximizes und to en-Latn), but SupportedLocaleStatics nulls it out for undetermined locales before the likely-subtag comparison at DefaultStrings:2071. The two catalogs are deliberately in unrelated languages so that nothing else can claim an English request: if a port compares the raw likely subtag instead of the undetermined-suppressed one, und wins an en request outright.

owed-loader-bom-prefixed.description: An en catalog whose bytes begin with the UTF-8 BOM EF BB BF, and a byte-identical fr catalog without it. Supplied through rawFilesBase64 because a BOM cannot survive being written from a JSON object. normalizeLocalizedStringsFileContents strips a leading U+FEFF before the JSON parser ever sees it; a port that decodes UTF-8 without BOM handling fails to parse the en file entirely.

owed-loader-bounded-diagnostics.description: Two files whose duplicate-JSON-member diagnostics exceed the loader's own bounds. `en` has a 4092-character top-level key, so the JSON path reaches 4094 characters and the next member name lands with exactly ONE character of room -- the single-ellipsis tail -- and the duplicate below it is reported at an already-saturated path. `fr` has a 5000-character key (truncated with room to spare) whose value repeats a 300-character member name, so the reported member is cut to 255 characters plus U+2026. Verbatim text: JSON.stringify cannot emit a duplicate member.

owed-loader-duplicate-language-tag.description: Two DIFFERENT java.util.Locale keys that render as the SAME BCP 47 language tag. Locale.forLanguageTag("no-NO-x-lvariant-NY") produces the legacy no_NO_NY locale, whose toLanguageTag() is "nn-NO" -- exactly what the second filename parses to -- while the two Locale objects are not equal (language `no` with variant `NY` versus language `nn`). The per-file duplicate check inside loadFromDirectory keys on Locale and therefore lets both through; only unmodifiableLocaleMapInLanguageTagOrder's rendered-tag set catches it. AUDIT NOTE: the disposition suggested ja-JP-x-lvariant-JP / ja-JP-u-ca-japanese, which does NOT collide on JDK 21 -- the lvariant form renders as ja-JP-u-ca-japanese-x-lvariant-JP, keeping the private-use suffix. Verified by probe before authoring. loadOnly because the directory cannot load at all.

owed-loader-range-endpoints.description: The two range-endpoint shapes the malformed-structure family left out: a range object with ONLY an end (no start member at all, versus the existing explicit-null start) and a range object whose end is explicitly null (versus the existing missing end). Together with the fixtures already present, all four combinations of absent/null x start/end are pinned.

owed-loader-unexpected-code-point.description: A whole-message alternative expression containing '?', a character no token pattern can match and which is NOT '='. The corpus's only lexer failure is 'count =? 0', which fails on '=' and therefore always carries the did-you-mean hint; this one must not. A second file uses a NO-BREAK SPACE between tokens, which the tokenizer's ASCII-only whitespace class rejects.

owed-m3b-alias-group-likely-subtag.description: The alias-group semantic-member election, made observable. nsl and nsi are the two sides of the JDK/CLDR alias conflict named in DefaultStrings.matchFor's own comment: the JDK's IANA table maps nsl to sgn-NO, while CLDR canonicalizes sgn-NO to nsi. The catalogs are deliberately nsl-Latn-DE and nsi-Latn-DE rather than bare nsl and nsi: a bare catalog is reachable through the SYNTACTIC exact/identity/canonical rungs, which are NOT gated by the election, and every such shape answers 'nsl' whichever member is elected. Attaching a script and a region leaves only the LIKELY-SUBTAG rung -- nsl's likely language-script is nsl-Latn and sgn-NO's is nsi-Latn -- and that rung is non-syntactic, so it is supplied by the elected semantic member alone (matchFor:1642-1648). The three primary languages en, nsl and nsi are pairwise distinct, so construction needs no tiebreakers and nothing here is attributable to tiebreaker order.

owed-m3b-election-guard-exact-nsl.description: The alias-group semantic-member election's 'already elected' guard (DefaultStrings.matchFor:1622), made observable. The catalog for nsl is spelled EXACTLY 'nsl' rather than nsl-Latn-DE, and that is the load-bearing choice: the guard is only observable when the elected member governs its locale through a SYNTACTIC relationship, because matchFor:1772 sends a locale to the group's representative position when its governor is the elected semantic member and to the governor's own position otherwise. A likely-subtag (non-syntactic) catalog such as nsl-Latn-DE takes the representative position either way, which is why the sibling fixture owed-m3b-alias-group-likely-subtag cannot discriminate this branch -- measured, not assumed. The second catalog is en so that a member unrelated to the nsl group occupies an index between the representative and the elected member; without it there is no position for the answer to move to. en and nsl have distinct primary languages, so construction needs no tiebreakers and nothing here is attributable to tiebreaker order.

owed-member-statics.description: Three catalogs whose tags make the three MemberStatics flags separable: an ordinary regional catalog (en-US), an unrelated ordinary catalog (fr) and a PRIVATE-USE catalog (x-lokal-a) that a wildcard-free private-use range would reach if canonical statics were computed for it. Private-use tags carry no language code, so no tiebreakers are owed.

owed-options-instance-en.description: The options-smoke-policy catalogs with the INSTANCE locale set to en and the fallback to fr, so a lookup that supplies no locale option still lands on the failing en entry. options-smoke-policy itself resolves straight to fr when no locale is passed, which makes a policy-only or handler-only option unobservable; this fixture is what lets those two options actually change the output.

owed-supplied-match-matched-without-rang.description: A fabrication that selects a locale with a weight and a non-NONE type but omits the matched RANGE. The corpus's only matched-state violation is the NONE type; the range and weight disjuncts are unexercised.

owed-supplied-match-matched-without-weig.description: A fabrication that selects a locale with a range and a non-NONE type but omits the effective WEIGHT -- the middle disjunct of the matched-state clause, which the corpus never takes.

owed-supplied-match-selected-locale-not-.description: A fabrication whose selected locale is absent from consideredLocales while the fallback is present, so the fallback-containment check on line 129 passes and the SELECTED-locale containment check on line 131 is the one that fires. Every existing considered-list fixture either contains the selected locale or fails earlier.

owed-supplied-match-unmatched-with-range.description: A fabrication with NO selected locale that nevertheless names a matched language range. LocaleMatchResult's unmatched-state clause is a three-way disjunction; the corpus already violates it with a weight and with a non-NONE type, but never with a RANGE, which is the first disjunct and therefore short-circuits the other two.

phonetic-resolver-absent-expression.description: No resolver configured, exercised on the expression path. DefaultStrings always installs its fail-fast default, so the evaluator's own 'no PhoneticResolver was provided' branch is unreachable and the default's IllegalStateException surfaces instead; a tagged value on the same expression still succeeds.

phonetic-resolver-absent-unreferenced.description: No resolver configured, and a phonetic definition the template never interpolates. Because the fail-fast default throws the moment it is reached, a successful render is a HARD proof that an unreferenced definition is never evaluated -- an eager port explodes here rather than merely showing an extra resolver call.

phonetic-resolver-by-term-default.description: A by-term resolver WITH a 'default', so an unmapped term reaches the default rather than the null-return rejection. Mapping keys differ in case and in script from some of the terms the cases pass, so exact-match lookup is observable in the rendered text. The 'Arger' entry is spelled with the PRECOMPOSED U+00C4, so a case passing the decomposed A + U+0308 form misses it.

phonetic-resolver-expression.description: The OTHER phonetic dispatch: ExpressionEvaluator#phoneticFromOperand, reached from alternative expressions rather than from a language-form placeholder. Two alternatives compare the same variable against two different PHONETIC_* constants, and a second key compares two variables, so which operands reach the resolver and how often is observable. The mapping includes an entry for the empty string so an empty operand answers a constant that matches neither alternative.

phonetic-resolver-expression-donor.description: The donor rule for the EXPRESSION dispatch. The key exists only in the fr fallback, so an en request is evaluated against the fr entry; the by-locale resolver's answer selects between two alternatives that name which locale the evaluator handed it.

phonetic-resolver-expression-limit.description: maximumInterpolatedOutputCharacters lowered to 8 on the expression path, where the same CharSequenceUtils conversion runs but its IllegalArgumentException is caught and rewrapped in ExpressionEvaluationException.

phonetic-resolver-expression-null.description: A null-returning resolver reached through an expression rather than a placeholder. The expression path raises its own ExpressionEvaluationException whose message omits the key, unlike the placeholder path's IllegalArgumentException.

phonetic-resolver-expression-throws.description: A throwing resolver reached through an expression. The resolver's own exception propagates UNWRAPPED out of the evaluator, unlike the length-limit failure on the same path, which is caught and rewrapped.

phonetic-resolver-first-letter-edges.description: The first-letter-vowel resolver driven with terms whose first character is unusual: empty, whitespace, digit, punctuation, uppercase, precomposed versus decomposed accents, a byte-order mark, a control character and an astral emoji. The resolver inspects charAt(0) against 'aeiouAEIOU', so each term pins a different assumption a port might make about normalization, trimming, or code-point iteration.

phonetic-resolver-handler-throws.description: A throwing translation failure handler over a phonetic resolution failure, so the failure the resolver's answer produced is re-raised rather than absorbed into a returned key -- on getResult as well as on get.

phonetic-resolver-input-types.description: One phonetic definition driven with every input shape the dispatch at DefaultStrings:1157-1186 can see: a tagged value from another axis, numbers of several Java types, a boolean, PluralOperands, an explicit null, an absent binding, and no placeholder map at all, plus two raw strings that spell constant names. A resolver IS installed, so no diagnostic here can reduce to 'no resolver'. A second key ('Plain') carries no placeholder and a third ('Gendered') carries a GENDER definition, both for must-not-be-called observations. The plain raw-term and plain tagged-value controls are deliberately NOT re-authored here; callback-smoke already owns them.

phonetic-resolver-locale-argument.description: A by-locale resolver whose answer encodes WHICH locale it was handed. 'en' and 'fr-CA' are loaded -- distinct primary languages, so tiebreakers stays null -- and the mapping names 'en' and 'en-US' with a LUNAR default, so an en-US request served by the en catalog is distinguishable from one where the requested tag were passed through, and a fr-CA request reaches the resolver's own default. The en-US mapping entry is what makes the absence of the requested tag falsifiable rather than assumed.

phonetic-resolver-missing-branch.description: A constant resolver returning PHONETIC_S_IMPURE against a definition that declares only VOWEL and CONSONANT, so the returned constant has no branch. Also serves the tagged half: an explicitly tagged constant with no branch fails identically without any resolver call.

phonetic-resolver-output-limit.description: maximumInterpolatedOutputCharacters lowered to 8. The phonetic dispatch converts the CharSequence through CharSequenceUtils.toString under that limit BEFORE calling the resolver, so an over-long term must fail with no invocation while a term exactly at the limit resolves.

phonetic-resolver-policy-throws-final-ca.description: A throwing fallback policy with only ONE candidate. The phonetic failure happens on the final distinct candidate, where the policy is never consulted, so the throwing policy becomes proof by absence: the lookup completes normally with a RESOLUTION_FAILURE result.

phonetic-resolver-policy-throws-two-cand.description: The same throwing policy where a SECOND candidate exists, so the identical phonetic failure does consult it and the policy's exception escapes the lookup entirely.

phonetic-resolver-range-rejected.description: DELIBERATELY UNLOADABLE, hence loadOnly. A placeholder combining a cardinality-style range with phonetic branches. DefaultStrings carries a phonetic-specific 'Phonetic translations cannot use ranges' guard, but the loader rejects the file first with a different message, making that guard unreachable; this fixture pins the diagnostic a port must actually produce, through both the directory loader and the single-file parser.

phonetic-resolver-sixteen-onsets.description: A by-term resolver mapping sixteen distinct terms onto the sixteen Phonetic constants, against one definition that declares a branch for every constant with a distinct text. Covers each constant as a resolver return value reaching its matching branch and, with NO 'default' configured, an unmapped term reaching the null-return rejection deliberately.

phonetic-resolver-structure.description: How many times, in what order and for which placeholders the resolver runs inside ONE lookup. Keys cover: two phonetic placeholders over two sources (control, template order == definition order); the SAME two definitions with the template mentioning them in the OPPOSITE order and reading DIFFERENT sources, so resolverCalls order actually discriminates template order from definition order; two differently-named placeholders reading one source (no memoization); one placeholder referenced twice in a template (resolved once); a phonetic definition the template never references; an alternative that shadows the top-level placeholder; a phonetic branch whose text names a second phonetic placeholder, so the second call happens only because the first selected that branch; a first placeholder whose selected constant has no branch; and a definition mixing a tagged value with a raw term.

phonetic-resolver-throwing-two-candidate.description: A throwing resolver against two COMPLETE catalogs, so the throw rather than a missing branch is what fails each candidate. Under any-failure both candidates are attempted, so the resolver is invoked once per candidate with a different locale each time and both invocations are recorded as throwing. A tagged value on the same fixture must render without reaching the resolver at all -- and because the resolver would have thrown, that absence is falsifiable by exception rather than only by the channel.

phonetic-resolver-two-candidates.description: A phonetic RESOLUTION_FAILURE on the first candidate with a second candidate available. The instance locale is en and the fallback fr; the en entry declares only a VOWEL branch while the resolver always answers CONSONANT, so en fails on the missing branch and fr can serve. The instance policy is any-failure and the cases override it per call, driving every fallback decision against one identical failure.

pt-flattening-cardinal-catalogs.description: Plan v7 section 8.3, clause 'pt to pt-PT at 0, 0.0, and 1.5 to prohibit same-language flattening'. Loads pt and pt-PT as two independent catalogs for one key whose generated placeholder selects on cardinality. GeneratedCldrPluralData.java:794 gives pt cardinal 'one' as `i = 0..1`; :799 gives pt-PT cardinal 'one' as `i = 1 and v = 0`, so the two locales are in different rule groups and disagree at exactly 0, 0.0 and 1.5 (CLDR's own decimal samples in those two rows are literally "0.0" and "1.5"). Each catalog tags its text with the locale that supplied it on every branch, so catalog merging is observable independently of rule selection: the integer-two pair is a value where pt and pt-PT choose the SAME category and only the catalog prefix differs. Both catalogs enumerate every category pt and pt-PT support (ONE, MANY, OTHER) so no case in this family can trip a missing-branch resolution failure by accident; MANY is present for that completeness and is deliberately not exercised here (see skipped). Tiebreakers are mandatory because pt and pt-PT share the primary language code 'pt', and DefaultStrings.java:394 requires the list to be an exact permutation of the loaded locales for that language.

I have {{itemCount}} items.commentary: The literal 'pt|' prefix makes the SUPPLYING catalog visible in the emitted translation, so a port that merged the two same-language catalogs is detectable even at values where pt and pt-PT choose the same cardinality.

The literal 'ptPT|' prefix makes the SUPPLYING catalog visible in the emitted translation, so a port that merged the two same-language catalogs is detectable even at values where pt and pt-PT choose the same cardinality.

pt-flattening-supplying-locale.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 same-language-flattening clause, boundary half: pt-PT is loaded but does NOT carry the key, so per-key fallback reaches the pt catalog. DefaultStrings.getResult passes `candidateLocale` -- the locale that SUPPLIED the entry -- into getInternal (DefaultStrings.java:712), and cardinalityForValue classifies with that locale (DefaultStrings.java:1438), so the pt entry's cardinality placeholder is evaluated under pt's rules even though the caller asked for pt-PT. This fixture exists so that 'never flatten pt-PT into pt' cannot be over-applied into 'a pt entry served to a pt-PT caller must use pt-PT rules'. The pt-PT file carries an unrelated key rather than being absent or empty: pt-PT must remain a LOADED locale, otherwise the mandatory pt tiebreaker list would no longer be an exact permutation of the loaded pt-language locales and the fixture would not build.

raw-vs-tagged-expressions.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 raw-vs-tagged clause, alternatives-expression half. Two keys whose single alternative compares a caller placeholder against a GENDER_* language-form literal and against a numeric literal, each with a default translation. The default is now actually exercised: fall-through cases supply a tagged form and a tagged integer that do NOT satisfy the alternative, so the positive controls prove discrimination rather than unconditional matching. Exists so the corpus pins that a raw string is never lifted to the constant the expression names, nor coerced to the number it spells.

GenderAlternative.commentary: Reached when the alternative does not match; distinct text from the branch so a match and a fall-through are never confusable.

raw-vs-tagged-language-form-placeholders.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 raw-vs-tagged clause, generated-placeholder half. Four single-axis LanguageFormTranslation placeholders (gender, cardinality, ordinality, phonetic), each keyed on a caller placeholder; two "both channels" keys that render the caller value as text AND dispatch on it in the same translation, so one observation shows both halves of the clause for a single value; and two duplicate-shape keys whose KEY TEXT contains the caller placeholder so the RETURNED_KEY failure path echoes the raw value verbatim, making the raw/tagged divergence visible in the translation string rather than only in status. en branch sets are complete for the locale (ONE/OTHER cardinal, ONE/TWO/FEW/OTHER ordinal) and every axis has at least two distinct branch texts so a tagged form must select ITS branch rather than any branch. Single loaded locale keeps attemptedLocales at [en]; tiebreakers is null because no two loaded locales share a primary language code.

BothChannelsCardinality.commentary: Numeric counterpart of BothChannelsGender: renders the number's own text next to the branch its plural classification selected.

BothChannelsGender.commentary: The caller placeholder appears both as a plain slot and as the value of a generated placeholder, so one translation observes text rendering and dispatch for the same value.

CardinalityLine.commentary: Number-converting axis. Distinct texts for ONE and OTHER so integer 1 and decimal 1.0 are told apart.

GenderLine.commentary: Strict-enum axis. Only a Gender value may select a branch here.

OrdinalityLine.commentary: The other number-converting axis, reached through ordinalityForValue, which is independent code from cardinalityForValue.

PhoneticLine.commentary: The only axis that accepts a raw CharSequence at all -- and it hands that text to the PhoneticResolver as an opaque term rather than reading it as the constant it spells.

{{bookCount}} books read.commentary: Numeric counterpart of the failure-key echo key.

{{who}} needs a pronoun.commentary: Key text carries the caller placeholder so that when gender dispatch fails and the key is returned, the raw value is interpolated into it verbatim.

raw-vs-tagged-plain-slot.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 clause "raw text 1.0 and GENDER_FEMININE remaining text while tagged forms dispatch", plain-interpolation half. One key with a single ordinary placeholder slot and no placeholder definitions, so the value never reaches a selector — StringInterpolator renders it directly (CharSequence appended verbatim, everything else via String.valueOf; verified against StringInterpolator.java). Single loaded locale so attemptedLocales is exactly [en] and no fallback policy is consulted. Verified by execution: the fixture builds and all eleven cases against it return TRANSLATED.

resolver-locale-canonical-equivalent.description: A request whose FIRST candidate is resolved onto an equivalent loaded catalog rather than matched by tag, so the supplying locale differs from the request with no fallback step involved at all. mo is not loaded; localizedStringsFor (DefaultStrings.java:2506) maps it onto loaded ro, and localeFallbackCandidates keys the candidate by that RESOLVED attempted locale (:2495-2500). The loader does not apply CLDR aliases, so ro is loaded as ro and no mo catalog exists. ro and en have distinct language codes, so tiebreakers are not required.

resolver-locale-cldr-parent.description: The CLDR parent chain. en-AU is not loaded; en-001 and en are, and both carry a complete Article. An en-AU request reaches en-001 through the parent chain rather than jumping to the en fallback, so the resolver must be handed en-001 — a locale that is neither the request nor the fallback. Tiebreakers are MANDATORY here because two loaded locales share the language code en, and the list is the exact permutation of the en locales that are loaded.

resolver-locale-divergent-selection.description: The diagnostic channel and the resolution channel deliberately disagree, rebuilt around a phonetic placeholder. The matcher SELECTS zh-Hant for a zh-TW request, but zh-Hant carries only a marker, so per-key resolution walks past it to the en fallback WITHOUT visiting the loaded zh. Article lives in zh and en only, and the resolver mapping distinguishes zh-TW, zh-Hant, zh and en, so the rendered branch says whether the callback was handed the requested locale, the diagnostically selected one, the locale resolution must not reach, or the actual supplying one. Tiebreakers are mandatory because zh and zh-Hant share a language code.

resolver-locale-instance-locale.description: The same rule reached through the AMBIENT locale ingress instead of a per-call one. The instance locale is de, which is loaded but carries no Article, so a call that passes no locale at all is still served by the en fallback and the resolver must be handed en. fr owns a complete Article so a per-call locale on the same instance can be contrasted against the ambient one. Three distinct primary language codes, so tiebreakers are not required.

resolver-locale-likely-subtag.description: A likely-subtag walk carried into the callback channel. fr-BE is not loaded; the tiebreaker list prefers fr-FR over fr-CA, so a fr-BE request is supplied by fr-FR after passing through a bare fr candidate that is never loaded. The resolver mapping covers fr-FR, fr-CA, fr-BE and fr so all four possible answers are distinguishable in the rendered text. Tiebreakers are mandatory because both loaded locales share the language code fr, and the list is the exact permutation of them.

resolver-locale-ltr-request-rtl-donor.description: The mirror image: ar is the fallback locale and owns the only Article, so an en request is served by an RTL donor. The default RTL_LOCALES must isolate the interpolated name AND the resolver must be handed ar. Together with resolver-locale-rtl-request-ltr-donor this pins, in BOTH directions, that bidi isolation and the resolver locale are decided by the same supplying locale, and — via the per-call NONE override — that changing the isolation mode does not move that locale.

resolver-locale-multi-step-walk.description: A multi-step walk in which an intermediate candidate FAILS after invoking the resolver. en-001's Article deliberately omits the PHONETIC_CONSONANT branch that the resolver returns when handed en-001, so that candidate raises IllegalStateException at DefaultStrings.java:1181 AFTER the resolver call has been made and recorded; the fixture policy is any-failure so the walk continues to en, whose Article carries every branch. resolverCalls therefore holds one entry PER CANDIDATE, each with a different locale. Per-call policy overrides on this same fixture truncate the walk at chosen points so the calls that must NOT happen are observable too.

resolver-locale-no-matching-alternative.description: ADDED IN REVIEW. A candidate that fails ALTERNATIVE SELECTION rather than placeholder resolution. en-001's Article has no top-level translation, only a single alternative guarded by 'count == 1', and the phonetic placeholder is declared alongside it. When the predicate holds the placeholder is evaluated and the resolver is handed en-001; when it does not, the candidate ends in NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE and the resolver is never reached at that candidate at all — the two cases differ only in the value of count, which makes the absence falsifiable rather than vacuous. Under any-failure the walk then reaches en. Tiebreakers are mandatory: en and en-001 share a language code.

resolver-locale-own-catalog.description: The control fixture for the family. en and fr each own a complete Article; de is loaded but carries only a marker, so a de request is served by the en fallback. The by-locale resolver maps every loaded locale to a DISTINCT phonetic and both Article catalogs carry every branch, so the rendered text names the locale the callback was handed instead of throwing on a missing branch. Three loaded locales with three distinct primary language codes, so tiebreakers are not required.

resolver-locale-rtl-request-ltr-donor.description: An RTL request served by an LTR donor, with both donor-rule consumers in one string. ar carries only a marker, so an ar request for Article is supplied by the en fallback. getResult hands getInternal the candidateLocale (DefaultStrings.java:712) — the same locale shouldApplyBidiIsolation consults at :1367 and the same one the resolver is handed at :1167 — so under the default RTL_LOCALES the interpolated Hebrew name must NOT be isolated AND the resolver must be handed en. The template joins the phonetic branch and the caller-supplied name with a pipe so neither channel can be satisfied while the other is wrong. A per-call bidiIsolation override on this same fixture then shows the two knobs are independent.

resolver-locale-throwing-across-walk.description: The same three-candidate walk with a resolver that always raises. Under any-failure every candidate that carries Article invokes the resolver and every invocation throws, so resolverCalls records the locale of each candidate on the FAILING path too. Both catalogs carry a complete branch set, so the only failure in play is the resolver's own — the locale channel must be populated for calls that returned nothing.

resolver-locale-two-phonetic-placeholder.description: ADDED IN REVIEW. Call MULTIPLICITY within a candidate, crossed with the donor rule. Both catalogs carry an Article with TWO phonetic placeholders, a and b, bound to the SAME caller term, so a correct implementation invokes the resolver once per placeholder per candidate rather than once per term or once per call. At en-001 placeholder b's branch set omits PHONETIC_CONSONANT — the answer the resolver gives when handed en-001 — so that candidate throws only after BOTH of its calls have been made and recorded; under any-failure en then supplies with two more calls. The branch labels are prefixed a: and b: so the rendered string shows both placeholders were resolved independently. Tiebreakers are mandatory: en and en-001 share a language code.

runtime-limits-absolute-number-scale-zer.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 zero-boundary clause: maximumAbsoluteNumberScale is non-negative and zero builds, admitting only integer-scaled values. PluralOperands.validateNumericValue compares Math.abs((long) number.scale()), so both a positive scale (1.5, scale 1) and a negative scale (1E+1, scale -1) must be rejected while 15 (scale 0) resolves.

runtime-limits-ceilings.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 runtime-limits clause: every limit set to its hard ceiling (MAXIMUM_NUMBER_PRECISION 4096, MAXIMUM_ABSOLUTE_NUMBER_SCALE 4096, MAXIMUM_VISIBLE_DECIMAL_PLACES 4096, MAXIMUM_COMPACT_EXPONENT 4096, MAXIMUM_EXPRESSION_CHARACTERS 4096, MAXIMUM_EXPRESSION_TOKENS 512, MAXIMUM_EXPRESSION_NESTING_DEPTH 64, MAXIMUM_GENERATED_PLACEHOLDER_DEPTH 64, MAXIMUM_INTERPOLATED_OUTPUT_CHARACTERS 1048576, MAXIMUM_GENERATED_EXPANSION_CHARACTERS 8388608), all read from TranslationRuntimeLimits.java lines 80-101. Builder.build's validateCeiling rejects anything above a ceiling, so the fixture constructing at all pins the ceilings from below. The cases then show two values that fail under the defaults succeeding here — pinning that the configured limit, not a hardcoded default, governs at runtime — and one that still fails, pinning that PluralOperands.Builder's own bound is not reached by the instance configuration.

runtime-limits-compact-exponent-zero.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 zero-boundary clause: maximumCompactExponent is non-negative and zero builds. PluralOperands.Builder.build treats an unset compact exponent as an effective 0, so at this limit both an absent and an explicit zero exponent resolve while exponent 1 is rejected by DefaultStrings.validatePluralOperands — not by the operands builder, whose own limit is still the default 64.

runtime-limits-expansion-default.description: Plan v7 section 8.3: the cumulative generated-expansion budget at its DEFAULT of 1,048,576 (1_024 * 1_024), pinned from both sides with no override. Each key is a six-link constant passthrough chain a1..a6 feeding an eighteen-level doubling chain b1..b18 whose leaf is one character, plus a sibling z. Billing is one consume per distinct placeholder: the b chain costs 1+2+...+131072 = 262,143, each of the six a levels costs 131,072 for 786,432, and z costs its own length. z = "A" totals exactly 1,048,576 and z = "AB" totals 1,048,577. The deepest recursion is 24, inside the default generated-placeholder depth of 32; the largest single expansion is 131,072 and the top-level output is 131,073, both far below the 262,144 interpolated-output default, so the cumulative budget — not the depth cap or the per-output cap — is what decides these two keys.

runtime-limits-expansion-fallback-budget.description: Plan v7 sections 4.6 and 8.3: 'Generated depth and cumulative expansion budgets reset for each locale attempt', and DefaultStrings.java:1203 constructs a new GeneratedExpansionBudget inside every per-candidate getInternal call. With the budget at 6, fr spends 7 and fails while en spends exactly 6; an implementation that shared one budget across the fallback walk would have nothing left for en. en and fr are different primary languages, so tiebreakers are absent.

runtime-limits-expansion-six.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 runtime-limits clause: maximumGeneratedExpansionCharacters pinned exactly at 6. GeneratedExpansionBudget.consume is called once per generated placeholder expansion at depth > 0 with that expansion's own length, and interpolateTemplate memoizes by placeholder name, so the five keys separate three independently wrong billing models: 3+3 exactly spends the budget, 3+4 exceeds it, one 6-character placeholder referenced twice is billed once, and a two-link chain is billed at BOTH links (3+3 fits, 4+4 does not).

runtime-limits-expansion-zero.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 zero-boundary clause: maximumGeneratedExpansionCharacters is non-negative (TranslationRuntimeLimits.Builder.build line 428), so zero builds. The budget check is consumedCharacters > maximum, and depth-0 output is never billed, so a key with no generated placeholder still renders while a single one-character generated fragment trips the budget.

runtime-limits-expression-characters-sev.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 runtime-limits clause: maximumExpressionCharacters pinned exactly at 17, the length of BOTH of this catalog's expressions — the whole-message alternative '(a > 0) && b == 1' and the generated-fragment predicate '(a > 1) && a == 2'. DefaultStrings compiles every loaded expression eagerly in its constructor (compileExpressions, calling ExpressionEvaluator.compile at DefaultStrings.java:576 for fragment predicates and 594 for whole-message alternatives) through an evaluator carrying the instance limits, so this fixture only builds at all if the implementation measures both sources at 17 UTF-16 units and treats validateExpressionSourceLength as strictly greater-than. Probe-verified against the real library: at limit 16 each expression is rejected by name.

runtime-limits-expression-nesting-one.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 runtime-limits clause: maximumExpressionNestingDepth pinned exactly at 1, the maximum group depth of both expressions in this catalog. ExpressionEvaluator.validateInfixTokens increments a counter on GROUP_START, throws when it exceeds the limit, and decrements on GROUP_END, so an implementation that seeded the counter at 1 for the whole expression, or that never decremented, would refuse to construct this fixture. Probe-verified: at limit 0 the library reports 'Expression grouping depth exceeds maximum supported depth 0'. Same catalog as the characters and tokens fixtures.

runtime-limits-expression-nesting-zero.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 zero-boundary clause: maximumExpressionNestingDepth is non-negative, so zero builds, and it is the one expression setting that forbids grouping outright. Every expression here is the parenthesis-free form of the corresponding expression in runtime-limits-expression-nesting-one, so group depth never leaves zero and the catalog compiles; an implementation that counted an implicit top-level group would reject it. Holding the operands identical also lets the case pairs show that the grouped and ungrouped forms evaluate alike.

runtime-limits-expression-tokens-nine.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 runtime-limits clause: maximumExpressionTokens pinned exactly at 9, the infix token count of both expressions in this catalog — GROUP_START, a, >, 0, GROUP_END, &&, b, ==, 1 and its fragment twin. ExpressionEvaluator.validateInfixTokens counts the INFIX list at the head of convertTokensToReversePolishNotation, before shunting-yard conversion, and whitespace produces no token, so an implementation that counted RPN tokens (7, parentheses dropped), counted whitespace, or dropped the parentheses would measure something other than 9 and fail to construct this fixture. Probe-verified: at limit 8 the library reports 'Expression contains 9 tokens'. Same catalog as the characters and nesting fixtures so only the limit under test differs.

runtime-limits-failure-key-eight.description: Plan v7 section 8.3's 'missing keys containing placeholders and failure-key fail-soft behavior', measured against the interpolated-output limit. DefaultStrings.interpolateFailureKey interpolates the KEY under maximumInterpolatedOutputCharacters and wraps the whole thing in try/catch(RuntimeException) { return key; }, so an overflow there silently degrades to the raw key instead of propagating. The catalog holds one unrelated key so the fixture loads; every case looks up a key that is deliberately absent.

runtime-limits-generated-depth-fallback.description: Plan v7 section 4.6: 'Generated depth and cumulative expansion budgets reset for each locale attempt.' The expansion half is covered by runtime-limits-expansion-fallback-budget; this fixture covers the depth half. With maximumGeneratedPlaceholderDepth 2, fr's Deep is a three-link chain that breaches the limit while en's is a two-link chain that sits exactly on it, so a permissive walk must reach en with a depth counter seeded back to 0. en and fr are different primary languages, so tiebreakers are absent.

runtime-limits-generated-depth-two.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 runtime-limits clause: maximumGeneratedPlaceholderDepth pinned exactly at 2. DefaultStrings.interpolateTemplate enters a generated placeholder's template at recursion depth k and throws when depth > limit (DefaultStrings.java:1321), so with the limit at 2 the depth-0, depth-1 and depth-2 keys all resolve and only the depth-3 chain trips. Lowering the limit rather than building a 33-link chain keeps the boundary exact and the fixture readable. One loaded locale, so no language code is ambiguous.

runtime-limits-generated-depth-zero.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 zero-boundary clause, from the permitted side: maximumGeneratedPlaceholderDepth is validated as NON-negative (TranslationRuntimeLimits.Builder.build line 426), so zero builds and is meaningful — it forbids generated placeholders entirely while leaving plain templates working. Same catalog as runtime-limits-generated-depth-two minus the deeper chains.

runtime-limits-interpolated-output-defau.description: Plan v7 section 8.3: maximumInterpolatedOutputCharacters at its DEFAULT of 262,144 (256 * 1_024), pinned from both sides with no override. A nineteen-level doubling chain from a one-character leaf yields exactly 2^18 = 262,144 characters at d1; the second key appends a single literal X after the same chain to produce 262,145. Cumulative expansion for either key is 2^19 - 1 = 524,287, half the 1,048,576 default budget, and the deepest recursion is 19, inside the default depth of 32 — so the per-output cap and nothing else is what decides these two keys.

runtime-limits-interpolated-output-eight.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 runtime-limits clause: maximumInterpolatedOutputCharacters pinned exactly at 8, with bidiIsolation left at the library default so per-call overrides can be measured against it. StringInterpolator.appendChecked bounds the OUTPUT builder, not the template, so 'Hi {{name}}' separates value length from template length. When isolation is in force the interpolator hands BidiUtils.BoundedIsolatedValue the REMAINING budget for rendering while DefaultStrings.java:1367 passes it the FULL maximum for error reporting, so the FSI and PDI markers are charged against the same 8 characters but the message still names 8. The Fragment keys put an 8- and a 9-character generated fragment at depth 1, where the same cap applies per expansion and the failure is contextualized by placeholder.

Companion to runtime-limits-interpolated-output-eight, identical except that the INSTANCE declares bidiIsolation ALWAYS. It exists because a per-call NONE on a default-configured instance is undetectable: DefaultStrings.DEFAULT_BIDI_ISOLATION is RTL_LOCALES (DefaultStrings.java:80) and en is LTR, so NONE and the default agree. Against an ALWAYS instance the same 'Bobby' at a limit of 8 fails unisolated-length-8-plus-two-markers, and each per-call override that turns isolation off makes it render — which is the only arrangement in which the override changes an observable.

runtime-limits-numeric-defaults.description: Plan v7 section 8.3: the numeric limits at their DEFAULTS, with no override, so a port cannot ship different default values unnoticed. Absolute scale 1024 versus 1025 is expressed compactly as 1E+1024 and 1E+1025 (BigDecimal scale -1024 and -1025). Visible decimal places 1024/1025 and compact exponent 64/65 straddle DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_VISIBLE_DECIMAL_PLACES and DEFAULT_MAXIMUM_COMPACT_EXPONENT; note that those two exceed-side values are rejected by the PluralOperands.Builder itself, which seeds its own limits from TranslationRuntimeLimits.defaults(), so they surface as a throw from operand construction rather than a resolution failure. That is the library's real behavior and is what the oracle records.

runtime-limits-numeric-lowered.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 runtime-limits clause, numeric side: all four numeric limits lowered to small exact values — precision 4, absolute scale 3, visible decimal places 2, compact exponent 2 — so all three numeric ingress paths named by plan section 4.6 can be pinned at one boundary.
