'Counted' drives a cardinality-tagged generated placeholder, which reaches PluralOperands.validateNumericValue and DefaultStrings.validatePluralOperands (defined at DefaultStrings.java:1494, called at 1451 and 1479) with the INSTANCE limits; 'Positive' drives the same values through an expression OPERAND, which validates inside ExpressionEvaluator with the same limits but a different exception identity; and 'Literal' carries the numeric LITERAL 1.234, whose precision 4 and scale 3 sit exactly on the two lowered limits and are checked by ExpressionEvaluator.validateNumericLiteralTokens at compile time, so the fixture only builds if literals are measured identically. The only other literals are 0 and 1, well inside every lowered limit.

runtime-limits-visible-decimal-places-ze.description: Plan v7 section 8.3 zero-boundary clause: maximumVisibleDecimalPlaces is non-negative and zero builds. DefaultStrings.validatePluralOperands checks operands.explicitVisibleDecimalPlaces() only when it isPresent(), so at zero a plain decimal whose scale already implies one visible place is unaffected while an explicitly requested single place is rejected. Every other limit stays at its default so nothing else can decide these cases.

supplied-match-considered-duplicate.description: A fabrication listing fr twice among its considered locales. The constructor deduplicates by lowercased language TAG (LocaleMatchResult.java:120-123); as a SET this list equals the supported locales exactly, so the instance validation would have accepted it and only the constructor's duplicate check can catch it. Its fallback locale IS considered, so this fixture deliberately makes no claim about check ORDER -- that is what supplied-match-considered-duplicate-and-fallback-absent is for.

supplied-match-considered-duplicate-and-.description: A fabrication whose considered list is [fr, fr]: it repeats a tag AND omits the fallback locale, so the duplicate check and the fallback-containment check are both violated inside the same constructor. The locale is null and the type NONE so no matched-state check can fire first.

supplied-match-considered-empty.description: A fabrication considering NOTHING, with a null locale so the matched-state checks pass cleanly. Its considered list also differs from the supported locales, so BOTH the constructor's fallback-containment check (LocaleMatchResult.java:130-131) and the instance's set comparison are violated -- which is what makes it able to pin constructor-before-instance ordering.

supplied-match-considered-extra-loadable.description: A fabrication that considers en, fr and de while only en and fr are loaded -- a superset rather than a subset, where de is an ordinary well-formed language the instance simply does not have.

supplied-match-considered-missing-locale.description: A fabrication that considers only en while the instance loaded fr and en. DefaultStrings.validateSuppliedLocaleMatchResult (DefaultStrings.java:2461-2471) compares the considered locales as a SET against getSupportedLocales and rejects any difference.

supplied-match-considered-nonexistent-lo.description: The same superset shape, but the extra considered locale is qq -- syntactically well-formed BCP 47 and assigned to no language. Isolates whether the rejection is about a locale EXISTING or purely about set equality with the loaded locales.

supplied-match-considered-reordered.description: A fabrication whose considered locales are the loaded ones in REVERSE of the instance's own sorted order (fr before en). The instance validation compares sets, so this is accepted, and the result must then report the caller's order rather than the library's.

supplied-match-effective-weight-lower-th.description: A fabrication whose effectiveWeight (0.25) contradicts the weight carried by its own matched range (1.0). The constructor only checks the (0,1] interval (LocaleMatchResult.java:112-113), so this survives construction and must be echoed rather than recomputed.

supplied-match-failure-identity.description: The identity fixture. A match no matcher could have produced -- it selects fr with type CLDR_FALLBACK at effective weight 0.25 while naming de, which is not loaded, as its only requested range -- over a catalog engineered so every failure reason is reachable: Missing.Everywhere is absent from both locales, NoMatch.Alternatives is an alternatives-only root whose predicate is false for the counts these cases pass, and Res.Failure declares only CARDINALITY_ONE. Section 8.3 requires the SAME match object through the result and failure paths; every existing observation of that in the corpus comes from a matcher-derived match, so this asserts it for a supplied one.

NoMatch.Alternatives.commentary: The fallback candidate misses the same way, so the walk ends in a failure rather than resolving.

Res.Failure.commentary: The fallback candidate is under-declared the same way, so a permissive policy still ends in a failure.

NoMatch.Alternatives.commentary: Alternatives-only root with no default translation, so a predicate miss is NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE rather than MISSING_TRANSLATION.

Res.Failure.commentary: Only CARDINALITY_ONE is declared, so any count French classifies as OTHER throws inside resolution and getResult classifies the attempt as RESOLUTION_FAILURE.

supplied-match-failure-identity-throwing.description: The same impossible match and catalog with the instance failure handler set to throwException, which is the thrown-failure path section 8.3 names alongside the result and failure-observer paths.

NoMatch.Alternatives.commentary: The fallback candidate misses the same way, so the walk ends in a failure rather than resolving.

Res.Failure.commentary: The fallback candidate is under-declared the same way, so a permissive policy still ends in a failure.

NoMatch.Alternatives.commentary: Alternatives-only root with no default translation, so a predicate miss is NO_MATCHING_ALTERNATIVE rather than MISSING_TRANSLATION.

Res.Failure.commentary: Only CARDINALITY_ONE is declared, so any count French classifies as OTHER throws inside resolution and getResult classifies the attempt as RESOLUTION_FAILURE.

supplied-match-foreign-fallback-and-cons.description: Both INSTANCE-level invariants broken at once: the fabrication's fallback is fr and its considered list is fr alone, which also differs from the supported locales. The constructor is satisfied (fr is considered), so the two instance checks are the only candidates and exactly one can win.

supplied-match-foreign-fallback-locale.description: A fabrication naming fr as ITS fallback locale while the instance's fallback is en. Both are loaded and fr is among the considered locales, so the value type is satisfied; the instance's own check (DefaultStrings.java:2464-2465) is the only one that can fire.

supplied-match-loaded-but-unasked.description: The lookup difference in its purest form: the fabricated match names en as the selection while its requested range says fr, and BOTH are loaded. Nothing about the fabrication is structurally impossible, so if the library re-derived the match from the range it would select fr and every observable would change.

supplied-match-no-requested-ranges.description: A MATCHED fabrication that reports no requested ranges at all -- the shape a caller who negotiated out of band would naively build. Because the matched range must be present in the requested list, an empty list makes any matched result unconstructible.

supplied-match-range-absent-and-weight-z.description: Two constructor invariants broken at once: the matched range (de) is absent from the requested list AND the effective weight is 0. Only one exception can be thrown, so this fixture -- and only this fixture -- pins which of the two checks runs first.

supplied-match-range-not-among-requested.description: A fabrication whose matched range (de) is absent from its own requested ranges (fr), with a valid weight so only the containment check can fire (LocaleMatchResult.java:109-110).

supplied-match-range-weight-mismatch.description: The matched range and the requested range share a range string (fr) but not a weight: the oracle builds the matched range with LanguageRange's default weight of 1.0 while the requested list carries 0.5. Locale.LanguageRange equality includes weight, so the containment check sees two different ranges even though the strings agree.

supplied-match-region-selection.description: A supplied selection carrying a region: fr-CA, claimed as PRIMARY_LANGUAGE at effective weight 0.8 for range fr. Three locales load and two share the fr language code, so tiebreakers are mandatory and are given as the exact permutation [fr, fr-CA] of that language's loaded locales.

supplied-match-requested-ranges-above-ma.description: One range past the ceiling: 33 requested ranges, which the constructor rejects with an explicit count message before any other check runs.

supplied-match-requested-ranges-at-maxim.description: A fabrication carrying exactly LocaleMatcher.MAXIMUM_LANGUAGE_RANGES (32) requested ranges, the largest list the constructor admits (LocaleMatchResult.java:84-87). All 32 must survive onto the result untouched; 31 of them correspond to nothing loaded.

supplied-match-type-canonical.description: A fabricated match that differs from reality in matchType ALONE: it selects fr, names range fr at weight 1, and considers exactly the loaded locales, so matchType=CANONICAL is the only counterfactual field. TranslationResult.isFallback (TranslationResult.java:250-274) ORs negotiationUsedFallback, which switches on the SUPPLIED matchType, with a resolved-locale term that is inert when the key is served from the supplied locale.

supplied-match-type-cldr-fallback.description: A fabricated match that differs from reality in matchType ALONE: it selects fr, names range fr at weight 1, and considers exactly the loaded locales, so matchType=CLDR_FALLBACK is the only counterfactual field. TranslationResult.isFallback (TranslationResult.java:250-274) ORs negotiationUsedFallback, which switches on the SUPPLIED matchType, with a resolved-locale term that is inert when the key is served from the supplied locale.

supplied-match-type-none-with-locale.description: A fabrication that contradicts itself: matchType NONE paired with a non-null locale, a range, and a weight. LocaleMatchResult's constructor (LocaleMatchResult.java:107-108) rejects the matched-state combination, and because the supplier is a lambda the library invokes lazily, the rejection lands on the CALL rather than on instance construction -- which is what makes the ingress-bypass cases on this same fixture possible.

supplied-match-type-primary-language.description: A fabricated match that differs from reality in matchType ALONE: it selects fr, names range fr at weight 1, and considers exactly the loaded locales, so matchType=PRIMARY_LANGUAGE is the only counterfactual field. supplied-match-unmatched-no-requested-ra.description: An unmatched fabrication carrying NO requested ranges at all -- the shape a caller who negotiated nothing would build. It is the accepted counterpart of the rejected matched-with-no-ranges fixture, since the containment check only applies when a matched range is present.

supplied-match-unmatched-none.description: A VALID unmatched fabrication: null locale, NONE, no range and no weight, while still reporting a requested range (de) that matched nothing. localeLookupFor falls back to the supplied result's own fallbackLocale (DefaultStrings.java:2453), so the lookup locale is en even though nothing was selected.

supplied-match-unmatched-throwing-handle.description: An unmatched (null locale, NONE) supplied match with a throwing instance failure handler, so the least informative match a supplier can hand over travels the thrown-failure path.

supplied-match-unmatched-with-non-none-t.description: The other half of the unmatched-state check: no selected locale, no range, no weight, but a non-NONE matchType. Everything a matched result needs is absent except the type, so only the type can be what makes this invalid.

supplied-match-unmatched-with-weight.description: A fabrication with NO selected locale that nonetheless carries an effective weight. LocaleMatchResult.java:104-105 requires an unmatched result to use NONE and omit both range and weight, and this trips the weight half of that check. Authored after MEASURING that the earlier claim -- that a null-locale-with-match-implications shape cannot be expressed through the fixture format -- is false.

supplied-match-weight-above-one.description: A fabricated effective weight of 1.5, outside the (0,1] interval on the upper side, with everything else valid.

supplied-match-weight-zero.description: A fabricated effective weight of exactly 0, the exclusive lower end of the (0,1] interval. Its matched range and requested list agree, so the weight check is the only one that can fire.

warnings-cardinality-matrix.description: One catalog whose only cardinality-driven placeholder supplies CARDINALITY_ONE and CARDINALITY_OTHER. Parsed under many locales it serves the 8.3 'warning sets' clause: the missing-form set is a function of the locale's CLDR cardinal categories, never of the catalog.

warnings-control-expression-placeholder.description: Russian catalog whose only placeholder is an EXPRESSION (generated-fragment) translation, which is not a LanguageFormTranslation at all and is skipped by the instanceof guard before any form inspection. Separated from the gender control so a port that mishandles one of the two cannot hide behind the other.

warnings-control-gender-placeholder.description: Russian catalog whose only placeholder is a GENDER-driven language-form translation. Russian has four cardinal and one ordinal CLDR form, so a loader that inspected every language-form placeholder rather than only the plural-driven ones would warn here. Split out from the expression control so each silence proposition stands alone.

warnings-control-range-driven.description: Russian catalog whose cardinality placeholder is RANGE-driven and supplies only ONE and OTHER of Russian's four forms. LocalizedStringLoader skips range-driven placeholders on purpose (line 1995), so this must produce no warning despite being incomplete on its face.

warnings-limit-four-four-warnings.description: The four-warning ordering catalog with maximumWarnings 4. Exactly at the limit the load succeeds, proving the comparison is 'already emitted >= limit' rather than 'about to emit > limit'. Loadable, and verified to construct a Strings instance.

warnings-limit-one-four-warnings.description: The four-warning ordering catalog with maximumWarnings 1. Deliberately unloadable: the second warning trips the limit after the first has already been handed to the handler.

warnings-limit-one-one-warning.description: The same one-warning Russian catalog with maximumWarnings 1. The satisfied side of the one boundary: exactly at the limit the load succeeds and the warning is delivered, so this fixture is loadable.

warnings-limit-two-four-warnings.description: The four-warning ordering catalog with maximumWarnings 2. Deliberately unloadable: pins that exactly two warnings are delivered before the third throws, and which two.

warnings-limit-zero-clean.description: A complete English catalog loaded with maximumWarnings lowered to 0. The clean side of the zero boundary: a limit of zero must not fail a load that produces no warnings.

warnings-limit-zero-one-warning.description: A Russian catalog that produces exactly one warning, loaded with maximumWarnings 0. Deliberately unloadable: the session throws on the first warning, so no Strings instance can be built and loadOnly is required.

warnings-mixed-axis-placeholder.description: One Russian key whose single placeholder supplies CARDINALITY_ONE and ORDINALITY_ONE together. Deliberately unloadable: axis purity is enforced at parse time (LocalizedStringLoader.java:2647-2654), so no warning can ever span two axes for one placeholder and the load fails before any warning is raised.

warnings-multi-locale-single-warner.description: Two locale files where only one can warn: a complete Japanese catalog (CLDR gives Japanese only OTHER) and an Arabic catalog missing four of Arabic's six forms. Exactly one warning regardless of directory iteration order, which is what makes this fixture reproducible where a two-warner fixture would not be. Fallback and instance locale are Japanese so the warning's locale cannot have come from either.

warnings-nested-alternative-attribution.description: One Russian key with an own placeholder, a first alternative that itself nests a deeper alternative, and a second sibling alternative. Distinguishes depth-first from breadth-first traversal and pins that every warning names the ROOT key, not the alternative expression.

warnings-order-single-file.description: A single Russian file engineered to emit four warnings whose order is fully determined: keys are declared Zulu-then-Alpha (not alphabetical), Alpha's placeholders are declared zeta-then-beta (not alphabetical), and Alpha carries an alternative with its own incomplete placeholder. Pins traversal order and root-key attribution entirely inside one file, so nothing depends on directory iteration.

warnings-ordinality-matrix.description: One catalog whose only ordinality-driven placeholder supplies ORDINALITY_ONE and ORDINALITY_OTHER. Parsed under many locales; a language's ordinal category set differs from its cardinal one, so this separates the two CLDR tables.

warnings-unsupported-forms-only.description: A catalog supplying ONLY CARDINALITY_TWO and ONLY ORDINALITY_TWO, in two placeholders declared in that order. No real locale is satisfied by it, so it separates 'no warning because complete' from 'no warning because the locale has no CLDR forms at all'.
